sec01-card-f01.front: What credential is needed to drive legally in Illinois, and what vehicle metric sets the required license class?
sec01-card-f01.expected_back: Driving legally in Illinois requires a valid Illinois license, and the vehicle’s gross vehicle weight rating determines its license classification.

sec01-card-f02.front: Which Illinois license class covers basic everyday passenger cars?
sec01-card-f02.expected_back: A basic Illinois license for driving a car is Class D.

sec01-card-f03.front: Under what conditions may a Class D driver operate a rental truck up to twenty-six thousand pounds inside Illinois?
sec01-card-f03.expected_back: A Class D holder may drive a rental vehicle weighing up to twenty-six thousand pounds within Illinois when carrying personal property belonging to the driver or an immediate family member for a nonbusiness purpose.

sec01-card-f04.front: What safety-training step applies when using a Class D license for that personal-property rental truck exception?
sec01-card-f04.expected_back: For that personal-property rental exception, the rental company must supply safety-course information that the driver is required to complete successfully.

sec01-card-f05.front: Which five passenger-transport vehicle categories trigger special Illinois licensing requirements beyond a basic car license?
sec01-card-f05.expected_back: Special licensing requirements apply to school buses, religious-organization buses, child-care vehicles, for-profit ride-sharing vehicles and vehicles used to transport senior citizens.

sec01-card-f06.front: When did Illinois stop issuing Temporary Visitor Driver's Licenses, and what may formerly eligible applicants seek instead?
sec01-card-f06.expected_back: Illinois stopped issuing Temporary Visitor Driver’s Licenses on July first, two thousand twenty-four; someone previously eligible for one may apply for a standard license.

sec01-card-f07.front: What is the general minimum age to earn an Illinois driver's license?
sec01-card-f07.expected_back: The general minimum age for an Illinois driver’s license is sixteen, subject to the handbook’s listed age-specific conditions.

sec01-card-f08.front: Which three major requirements must a sixteen- or seventeen-year-old finish to get an Illinois license?
sec01-card-f08.expected_back: An applicant aged sixteen or seventeen must finish state-approved driver education, log fifty hours of practice and pass all three examination components to receive a license.

sec01-card-f09.front: Who must sign a minor's consent affidavit if a parent or guardian cannot come along to the facility?
sec01-card-f09.expected_back: When a parent or guardian cannot accompany a minor applicant, a legal guardian or responsible adult older than twenty-one must sign the minor’s consent affidavit.

sec01-card-f10.front: What training is required for a first-time applicant aged eighteen through twenty who never took high-school or commercial driver ed?
sec01-card-f10.expected_back: A first-time applicant aged eighteen through twenty who has never held a license or finished an approved high-school or commercial driver-education program must complete a six-hour course from a state-certified adult driver-education provider.

sec01-card-f11.front: Which two commercial or paid-delivery driving jobs are off-limits to drivers under eighteen?
sec01-card-f11.expected_back: A driver younger than eighteen cannot drive a for-hire property-delivery vehicle or a vehicle requiring a commercial license.

sec01-card-f12.front: Which passenger-carrying vehicles cannot be driven by anyone younger than twenty-one in Illinois?
sec01-card-f12.expected_back: Drivers younger than twenty-one cannot operate for-hire vehicles carrying more than ten passengers, commuter vans, religious or school buses, senior-citizen transport vehicles or child-care vehicles.

sec01-card-f13.front: How long can a new Illinois resident drive on a valid out-of-state license after moving in?
sec01-card-f13.expected_back: A new Illinois resident with a valid license from elsewhere must obtain the Illinois license within ninety days of moving or before the existing license expires, whichever happens sooner.

sec01-card-f14.front: What license lets a nonresident visitor legally drive while traveling through Illinois?
sec01-card-f14.expected_back: A visitor passing through Illinois may drive using a valid license issued by the visitor’s home state or country.

sec01-card-f15.front: How does Illinois treat out-of-state college students—and their spouses and kids—who hold valid home licenses?
sec01-card-f15.expected_back: An out-of-state college or university student in Illinois, along with that student’s spouse and children, may drive on valid licenses from their home jurisdiction.

sec01-card-f16.front: Which driving credential rule applies to active-duty Armed Forces members and dependents living with them?
sec01-card-f16.expected_back: Active-duty members of the United States Armed Forces and the spouses and dependent children living with them may drive on valid home-state licenses.

sec01-card-f17.front: How long after returning from overseas military duty can an Illinois resident and live-in family use a prior license deferral?
sec01-card-f17.expected_back: An Illinois resident serving in the military outside the United States may use a previously obtained license deferral for the first one hundred twenty days after returning; the returning resident’s spouse and dependent children living with the resident share that provision.

sec01-card-f18.front: Who else serving overseas alongside the military qualifies for that same one-hundred-twenty-day return deferral?
sec01-card-f18.expected_back: The same one-hundred-twenty-day return provision, with a deferral obtained beforehand, covers Illinois-resident civilian employees of the Armed Forces or Defense Department serving abroad and their spouses and dependent children living with them.

sec01-card-f19.front: When can a federal employee or service member drive in Illinois without holding an Illinois driver's license?
sec01-card-f19.expected_back: A federal employee or service member driving a government-owned or government-leased vehicle on official business does not need an Illinois license for that travel.

sec01-card-f20.front: Which two temporary roadway equipment operations do not require an Illinois driver's license?
sec01-card-f20.expected_back: An Illinois license is not required to operate a road machine temporarily on a roadway or a farm tractor between farm buildings and nearby farmland.

sec01-card-f21.front: How soon after a legal name change must you apply for a corrected Illinois card, and what proof is needed?
sec01-card-f21.expected_back: After a legal name change, apply for a corrected license or identification card within thirty days and present documents linking the new name to the name already recorded.

sec01-card-f22.front: Which exact name gets printed on an Illinois license or identification card?
sec01-card-f22.expected_back: The name printed on an Illinois credential is the full given name and surname established through birth, marriage, Social Security records or another legal action.

sec01-card-f23.front: Within how many days of moving must you notify the Secretary of State, and which three channels work?
sec01-card-f23.expected_back: Notify the Secretary of State of a move within ten days, using a facility visit, online services or a written notice.

sec01-card-f24.front: Does reporting an address move automatically mail you a new card, or what does printing the new address take?
sec01-card-f24.expected_back: Reporting an address change alone does not produce a replacement card; getting the new address printed requires a facility visit, acceptable residency documents and the appropriate fee.

sec01-card-f25.front: Which five personal details require acceptable documentary proof when applying for an Illinois license or ID?
sec01-card-f25.expected_back: Applying for an Illinois license or identification card requires acceptable evidence of legal name, birth date, Social Security number, residence and signature.

sec01-card-f26.front: What handwriting check does the agency perform during verification, and does every visit need the same document count?
sec01-card-f26.expected_back: The agency compares signatures during identification verification, and the required document count varies between a first application and a duplicate or correction request.

sec01-card-f27.front: Along with giving a working mailing address and taking a photo, what must an applicant hand over?
sec01-card-f27.expected_back: An applicant must supply a usable mailing address, have a photograph taken and surrender other Illinois licenses, identification cards and instruction permits.

sec01-card-f28.front: Besides bringing acceptable identity documents, what else is still required to actually receive your credential?
sec01-card-f28.expected_back: Receiving the requested credential also requires the applicable examinations and fee; providing identity documents does not replace those steps.

sec01-card-f29.front: What identity details and how many Illinois residency documents does a first-time REAL ID application require?
sec01-card-f29.expected_back: A first-time REAL ID application needs evidence of identity that includes citizenship or lawful status, birth date, Social Security number and signature, plus two documents establishing Illinois residence.

sec01-card-f30.front: What extra paperwork do you need if your birth certificate or identity record shows an earlier legal name?
sec01-card-f30.expected_back: If an identity document uses an earlier legal name, the applicant must add documentation showing the reason for the name change, such as a certified marriage record, divorce decree or adoption papers.

sec01-card-r01.front: What proofs—and how many residency documents—does a first-time standard Illinois credential require?
sec01-card-r01.expected_back: A first-time standard Illinois credential needs documentation of birth date, Social Security number and signature, with one residency document.

sec01-card-r02.front: Can a single acceptable document satisfy more than one identification-document category?
sec01-card-r02.expected_back: One acceptable document can satisfy more than one of the identification-document groups.

sec01-card-r03.front: What proof does every duplicate or corrected card need, and when must you add residency proof too?
sec01-card-r03.expected_back: A duplicate or corrected credential requires signature evidence, and an address printed differently on the replacement also requires residency evidence.

sec01-card-r04.front: Under what condition are you allowed to order a duplicate Illinois credential online?
sec01-card-r04.expected_back: An online duplicate application is available only when the applicant is not changing the address, name or date of birth.

sec01-card-r05.front: What kind of identification is required to change your name, birth date, Social Security number, or gender on a card?
sec01-card-r05.expected_back: Changing a name, birth date, Social Security number or gender requires identification linking the previous information with the requested replacement information.

sec01-card-r06.front: What must an applicant under age sixty bring to replace a stolen Illinois credential free of charge?
sec01-card-r06.expected_back: For an applicant younger than sixty, a police report saying the credential was stolen is required to obtain the stolen-card duplicate without a charge.

sec01-card-r07.front: Do applicants older than sixty need a police report to get a free duplicate license or ID card?
sec01-card-r07.expected_back: The handbook says people older than sixty do not need a police report to obtain a duplicate license or identification card without a charge.

sec01-card-r08.front: Roughly how early are renewal notices sent, and what happens if no reminder ever reaches your mailbox?
sec01-card-r08.expected_back: The agency normally sends a renewal notice roughly ninety days before expiry, but renewing on time remains the driver’s responsibility even when no notice arrives.

sec01-card-r09.front: How early before expiration can you renew a two- or four-year license versus a one-year license?
sec01-card-r09.memory_hook: Multi-year one year, annual six months
sec01-card-r09.expected_back: A two-year or four-year license may be renewed as early as one year before its expiry, while a one-year license may be renewed up to six months early.

sec01-card-r10.front: How long is an ordinary Illinois driver's license valid, and on what date does it expire?
sec01-card-r10.expected_back: The ordinary Illinois license term is four years with expiry on the driver’s birthday, but the handbook lists age-based exceptions.

sec01-card-r11.front: When does an Illinois driver's license issued to someone under twenty-one expire?
sec01-card-r11.expected_back: A license for someone younger than twenty-one expires three months after that person’s twenty-first birthday.

sec01-card-r12.front: How often must Illinois drivers aged eighty-seven or older renew their driver's license?
sec01-card-r12.expected_back: For drivers aged eighty-seven or older, the handbook requires license renewal every year.

sec01-card-r13.front: Which two channels handle standard license renewal, and what extra items go along with renewing?
sec01-card-r13.expected_back: Standard renewal uses a facility visit with the current credential, or online services when a PIN renewal notice permits it, together with any required examination, fee and new photograph.

sec01-card-r14.front: What must a renewal applicant provide if they cannot turn in their current license at the counter?
sec01-card-r14.expected_back: A renewal applicant who cannot surrender the current credential must provide proof of signature.

sec01-card-r15.front: How many residency documents are needed if you update your address while renewing a standard card versus a REAL ID?
sec01-card-r15.expected_back: Changing an address at renewal requires one residency document for a standard credential and two for a REAL ID credential.

sec01-card-r16.front: Which document set is needed at renewal when you lack your current card or request profile changes?
sec01-card-r16.expected_back: Without the current credential, or when making changes, renewal documentation includes birth date, Social Security number and signature, with residency proof when an address change is requested.

sec01-card-r17.front: What must a noncitizen show when renewing an Illinois REAL ID credential?
sec01-card-r17.expected_back: A noncitizen renewing a REAL ID credential must present current evidence of lawful status.

sec01-card-r18.front: What temporary credential do you get at the facility after paying and passing tests, and how long is it good?
sec01-card-r18.expected_back: After payment and successful completion of required testing, the agency issues a secure temporary paper credential valid for ninety days.

sec01-card-r19.front: How is your permanent Illinois plastic card produced, and how soon does it usually arrive?
sec01-card-r19.expected_back: The permanent credential is printed centrally after document verification and usually reaches the supplied mailing address within fifteen business days.

sec01-card-r20.front: Which two postal settings block delivery of your permanent Illinois license or ID card?
sec01-card-r20.expected_back: A forwarding order or a hold on mail service prevents postal delivery of the permanent Illinois credential to that address.

sec01-card-r21.front: What should you do if your permanent Illinois card still has not arrived fifteen business days after your visit?
sec01-card-r21.expected_back: If the permanent credential has not arrived after fifteen business days from the facility visit, check its status online or contact the agency.

sec01-card-r22.front: What arrest, prison, and license penalties can hit someone caught committing Illinois credential fraud?
sec01-card-r22.expected_back: Credential fraud can lead to arrest, imprisonment for as long as five years and a twelve-month license suspension or revocation.

sec01-card-r23.front: Which five false-information, fake-card, or document-sharing acts are listed as credential-fraud offenses?
sec01-card-r23.expected_back: False application information, false identity documents, fictitious or unlawfully altered driving credentials, using someone else’s credential and knowingly lending identity documents for an application in one’s name are listed credential-fraud offenses.

sec01-card-r24.front: Which four health or substance factors does an Illinois license application ask you to disclose?
sec01-card-r24.expected_back: A license application asks about physical or mental conditions, medicines, other drugs and alcohol that could impair safe driving.

sec01-card-r25.front: When a physician's Medical Report is required, how soon after the doctor signs it must you turn it in?
sec01-card-r25.expected_back: In cases requiring a physician’s Medical Report, present that completed report to facility staff within ninety days after the physician signs it.

sec01-card-r26.front: How soon must you notify the Secretary of State after learning of a condition that could cause blackouts or loss of control, and what happens if you stay silent?
sec01-card-r26.expected_back: After learning of a condition likely to cause unconsciousness or loss of safe vehicle control, notify the Secretary of State within ten days; not reporting can lead to cancellation of driving privileges.

sec01-card-r27.front: What violations and crashes go onto an Illinois driver's state record, including events outside Illinois?
sec01-card-r27.expected_back: Illinois keeps a record of a licensed driver’s traffic violations and crashes, including convictions received in other states.

sec01-card-r28.front: What does Illinois do when an out-of-state driver commits an Illinois offense requiring immediate action?
sec01-card-r28.expected_back: When a nonresident commits an Illinois violation requiring immediate action, Illinois creates a record and reports the violation to the person’s home state.

sec01-card-r29.front: Through which three channels can a driver buy a copy of their Illinois driving record?
sec01-card-r29.expected_back: A driver may obtain a paid copy of the driving record through online services, selected facilities or a written request.

sec02-card-f01.front: What three driver details, payment, and requester proof must accompany a written driving-record request?
sec02-card-f01.expected_back: A written driving-record request must identify the driver by full name, birth date and license number, include the fee and provide proper identification for the requester.

sec02-card-f02.front: Starting at what age are Illinois applicants asked if they want to join the organ and tissue donor registry?
sec02-card-f02.expected_back: Applicants aged sixteen or older are asked whether they want to join the Illinois organ and tissue donor registry.

sec02-card-f03.front: What military service or discharge proof is required to add the veteran designation to an Illinois credential?
sec02-card-f03.expected_back: An applicant requesting a veteran designation must document honorable military discharge, military retirement or service in the reserves or National Guard.

sec02-card-f04.front: How is voter registration handled during a standard Illinois credential application?
sec02-card-f04.expected_back: Standard-credential applicants are told their voter-registration status and address, then asked whether to register or update an unregistered or outdated record.

sec02-card-f05.front: What happens with voter registration when a REAL ID applicant proves United States citizenship?
sec02-card-f05.expected_back: A REAL ID applicant who proves United States citizenship is also applying for voter registration unless the applicant chooses to opt out.

sec02-card-f06.front: How do license-facility voter registrations reach your local election office?
sec02-card-f06.expected_back: The agency sends voter-registration applications electronically to the state election board, which forwards them to the proper local election authority.

sec02-card-f07.front: May a noncitizen register to vote while applying for an Illinois driver's license?
sec02-card-f07.expected_back: A person who is not a United States citizen cannot register to vote through a license application.

sec02-card-f08.front: What affirmation details are needed to get a Gold Star Family designation on an Illinois credential?
sec02-card-f08.expected_back: A Gold Star Family credential designation requires an affirmation of qualifying family membership naming the service member and the applicant’s relationship.

sec02-card-f09.front: For required male applicants aged eighteen through twenty-five, what does signing the credential application do regarding Selective Service?
sec02-card-f09.expected_back: For a male applicant required to register with Selective Service, aged eighteen through twenty-five, signing the credential application certifies registration or authorizes the agency to submit it.

sec02-card-f10.front: What helpful personal and health details can Illinois cardholders add to a confidential police and responder database?
sec02-card-f10.expected_back: Illinois credential holders may supply emergency contacts and information about disabilities or special medical needs to a database used by police and emergency responders.

sec02-card-f11.front: How much is the Illinois instruction-permit application fee listed in the handbook?
sec02-card-f11.expected_back: The handbook lists the instruction-permit application fee as twenty dollars.

sec02-card-f12.front: What is the listed Illinois driver's-license fee for applicants aged eighteen through twenty?
sec02-card-f12.expected_back: The listed driver’s-license fee for applicants aged eighteen through twenty is five dollars.

sec02-card-f13.front: What license fee does the handbook list for adults aged twenty-one through sixty-eight?
sec02-card-f13.expected_back: For a license applicant aged twenty-one through sixty-eight, the handbook lists a thirty-dollar fee.

sec02-card-f14.front: What driver's-license fee applies to Illinois applicants aged sixty-nine through eighty?
sec02-card-f14.expected_back: The license fee listed for ages sixty-nine through eighty is five dollars.

sec02-card-f15.front: How much is the Illinois driver's-license fee for ages eighty-one through eighty-six?
sec02-card-f15.expected_back: For ages eighty-one through eighty-six, the handbook lists a two-dollar license fee.

sec02-card-f16.front: Which age group is completely exempt from paying an Illinois driver's-license fee?
sec02-card-f16.expected_back: A license applicant aged eighty-seven or older is listed as exempt from the license fee.

sec02-card-f17.front: How much does adding a noncommercial classification outside of renewal cost, and what is excluded from that table line?
sec02-card-f17.expected_back: Adding a noncommercial license classification outside renewal costs five dollars; the table excludes commercial classifications from that entry.

sec02-card-r01.front: What fee does the Illinois handbook list for a school-bus permit?
sec02-card-r01.expected_back: The listed school-bus permit fee is four dollars.

sec02-card-r02.front: How much extra does adding or renewing a motorcycle classification tack onto your regular license fee?
sec02-card-r02.expected_back: Adding or renewing a motorcycle classification adds five dollars to the ordinary driver’s-license fee.

sec02-card-r03.front: What are the initial Illinois identification-card fees across age brackets and for persons with disabilities?
sec02-card-r03.memory_hook: Five youth, twenty adult, seniors free
sec02-card-r03.expected_back: The initial state identification-card fee is five dollars below eighteen and twenty dollars from eighteen through sixty-four, while ages sixty-five and older and persons with disabilities are listed as free.

sec02-card-r04.front: What does a duplicate or corrected Illinois license or permit cost ordinarily, and what senior discounts apply?
sec02-card-r04.memory_hook: Five standard, two eighties, eighty-seven free
sec02-card-r04.expected_back: A duplicate or corrected license or permit ordinarily costs five dollars, with two dollars listed for ages eighty-one through eighty-six and no fee for ages eighty-seven and older.

sec02-card-r05.front: What is the listed fee for a duplicate or corrected ninety-day temporary license or legacy visitor license?
sec02-card-r05.expected_back: A duplicate or corrected ninety-day temporary license is listed at five dollars, as is a duplicate or corrected Temporary Visitor Driver’s License.

sec02-card-r06.front: When is replacing a lost or stolen Illinois license or permit free under age sixty versus at sixty and up?
sec02-card-r06.memory_hook: Police report under sixty, free sixty-plus
sec02-card-r06.expected_back: A stolen license or permit can be duplicated without charge for someone younger than sixty who provides a full police report; lost or stolen licenses or permits are free to duplicate at age sixty or older.

sec02-card-r07.front: How much does it cost to duplicate or correct a temporary ninety-day Illinois identification card?
sec02-card-r07.expected_back: A duplicate temporary ninety-day identification card costs five dollars, and the same listed fee applies to correcting that temporary card.

sec02-card-r08.front: What does a duplicate standard identification card cost under eighteen versus ages eighteen through sixty-four?
sec02-card-r08.expected_back: A duplicate identification card costs five dollars below eighteen and twenty dollars for ages eighteen through sixty-four, subject to the table’s free replacement provisions.

sec02-card-r09.front: Which two situations waive the duplicate fee for an Illinois identification card?
sec02-card-r09.expected_back: The table waives the duplicate identification-card fee for theft supported by a full police report, and for a lost or stolen card when the holder is at least sixty.

sec02-card-r10.front: How much does a corrected Illinois identification card cost under eighteen, from eighteen through sixty-four, and at sixty-five-plus?
sec02-card-r10.memory_hook: Five youth, ten adult, sixty-five free
sec02-card-r10.expected_back: A corrected identification card costs five dollars below eighteen, ten dollars from eighteen through sixty-four and nothing from sixty-five onward.

sec02-card-r11.front: How much do active Armed Forces members and live-in spouses or children pay for duplicate licenses, permits, or IDs?
sec02-card-r11.expected_back: Active Armed Forces members and the spouses and children living at home with them are listed as eligible for free duplicate licenses, permits and identification cards.

sec02-card-r12.front: Why does the handbook advise checking the agency website before visiting for exact credential fees?
sec02-card-r12.expected_back: Credential fees can change through legislation, so the handbook directs readers to the agency’s website for current amounts.

sec02-card-r13.front: Even though duplicate TVDL fees still appear, what changed starting July first, two thousand twenty-four?
sec02-card-r13.expected_back: Illinois no longer issues Temporary Visitor Driver’s Licenses beginning July first, two thousand twenty-four; a previously eligible applicant may seek a standard license.

sec02-card-r14.front: How can eligible Illinois drivers renew a valid license without visiting a facility?
sec02-card-r14.expected_back: Eligible drivers can renew a valid license through the agency’s online services.

sec02-card-r15.front: Which age group can renew valid ID cards online, and what special ID rule applies at age sixty-five and up?
sec02-card-r15.memory_hook: Online twenty-two to sixty-four, seniors nonexpiring
sec02-card-r15.expected_back: The handbook lists online renewal of valid identification cards for ages twenty-two through sixty-four and says seniors aged sixty-five or older have free cards that do not expire.

sec02-card-r16.front: Which three additional vehicle, record, or business tasks does the agency's website handle online?
sec02-card-r16.expected_back: The agency’s online services include obtaining a driving-record abstract, renewing a plate sticker and filing business-service documents.

sec02-card-r17.front: How can customers reach the agency when they have questions or issues involving administrative hearings?
sec02-card-r17.expected_back: Customers with administrative-hearing issues may contact the agency’s administrative-hearings email service.

sec03-card-f01.front: Which tests can a license application require, and which two tests are mandatory every time you get or renew a permit?
sec03-card-f01.expected_back: Applying for a driver’s license can require vision screening plus written and driving tests, while every permit issuance or renewal requires vision screening and a written test.

sec03-card-f02.front: How long does your application fee stay active, and how many tries at each exam does it cover?
sec03-card-f02.expected_back: Payment of an application fee starts a one-year period in which an applicant has three attempts at each examination.

sec03-card-f03.front: What events on your driving record can require you to take a written test, a driving test, or both?
sec03-card-f03.expected_back: A crash or moving violation on the driving record can trigger a requirement to take a written test, a driving test or both.

sec03-card-f04.front: Which three suspicious behaviors during a written test can prompt an examiner warning?
sec03-card-f04.expected_back: An examiner may warn a written-test applicant about suspicious conduct such as an open book in view, looking around or checking a wireless device.

sec03-card-f05.front: What happens to your exam score and wait time if an examiner catches you cheating?
sec03-card-f05.expected_back: Being caught cheating results in a failed examination and a thirty-day wait before another attempt.

sec03-card-f06.front: How severe is the criminal penalty for taking any part of another person's Illinois license exam?
sec03-card-f06.expected_back: Taking any portion of someone else’s license examination is a criminal offense carrying a fine and at least seven days in jail.

sec03-card-f07.front: What can happen to your application if you try to bribe or influence facility staff, driving schools, or examiners?
sec03-card-f07.expected_back: Trying to bribe or influence agency staff, driving-school owners or authorized instructors or examiners can lead to refusal of a license or permit.

sec03-card-f08.front: Instead of an on-site vision screening, what specialist report is accepted and how recent must it be?
sec03-card-f08.expected_back: Every license applicant needs a vision screening or a Vision Specialist Report signed by a licensed optometrist, ophthalmologist or physician within the six months before the facility visit.

sec03-card-f09.front: What is the minimum visual acuity standard in Illinois, with or without corrective lenses?
sec03-card-f09.expected_back: The listed minimum visual acuity is twenty over forty, measured with corrective lenses or without them.

sec03-card-f10.front: Which visual-acuity range restricts an Illinois driver to daylight driving only?
sec03-card-f10.expected_back: A driver whose visual acuity falls between twenty over forty-one and twenty over seventy is restricted to driving during daylight.

sec03-card-f11.front: At least how many degrees of peripheral side vision are required to qualify in Illinois?
sec03-card-f11.expected_back: The vision requirement includes at least one hundred forty degrees of peripheral vision, with corrective lenses or without them.

sec03-card-f12.front: What rule applies behind the wheel if you used glasses or contact lenses to pass the vision screening?
sec03-card-f12.expected_back: A license restriction requires a driver who uses glasses or contact lenses for vision qualification to wear them while driving.

sec03-card-f13.front: What extra steps apply to Illinois applicants who use telescopic lenses?
sec03-card-f13.expected_back: Applicants using telescopic lenses must satisfy special requirements and undergo additional vision testing.

sec03-card-f14.front: How often does the handbook require a renewal written test, and who gets excused from it?
sec03-card-f14.expected_back: The handbook requires a written examination every eight years, with an exception for drivers who have no traffic convictions.

sec03-card-f15.front: How does the basic written exam test your knowledge of road signs, signals, and markings?
sec03-card-f15.expected_back: The basic written test asks applicants to recognize signs from their shape, color or symbol and to recognize signals and roadway markings.

sec03-card-f16.front: Which two question styles and four safety topics appear on the Illinois written examination?
sec03-card-f16.expected_back: Written-test questions include multiple-choice and true-or-false items on traffic laws, safe operation, crash prevention and vehicle equipment.

sec03-card-f17.front: Where are the distinct exam rules for motorcycles, heavy trucks, and buses covered?
sec03-card-f17.expected_back: Motorcycles, trucks and buses have different examination requirements that are covered in their corresponding operator manuals.

sec03-card-f18.front: Besides every brand-new driver, which renewal age group must always take a behind-the-wheel exam?
sec03-card-f18.expected_back: Every new driver must take a driving examination, and the handbook also requires it at renewal for drivers aged eighty-seven or older, including those turning that age.

sec03-card-r01.front: What preparation does the handbook suggest for first-time drivers aged twenty-one or older before applying?
sec03-card-r01.expected_back: For a first-time driver aged twenty-one or older, the handbook suggests adult driving-school enrollment before the license application.

sec03-card-r02.front: What licensing, equipment, and weight-class rules must your road-test vehicle satisfy?
sec03-card-r02.expected_back: A road-test vehicle must be properly licensed, equipped as required and in the weight class stated on the application.

sec03-card-r03.front: What coverage requirement must you prove for the car used on your driving exam?
sec03-card-r03.expected_back: The driving-test vehicle must have insurance, with proof presented for the examination.

sec03-card-r04.front: What plate and sticker setup must an Illinois-registered test car display, and how are out-of-state cars judged?
sec03-card-r04.memory_hook: Both plates, current sticker, home rules
sec03-card-r04.expected_back: An Illinois-registered test vehicle needs valid plates at the front and rear and a current registration sticker; an out-of-state vehicle must meet its own state’s registration rules.

sec03-card-r05.front: Who has to drive the test vehicle into the licensing facility?
sec03-card-r05.expected_back: Someone holding a valid license or permit must drive the test vehicle to the facility.

sec03-card-r06.front: Who may ride inside the car during the Illinois road test, and who is barred from tagging along?
sec03-card-r06.expected_back: Only the examiner may ride with the applicant during the road test, so children and pets cannot accompany the test.

sec03-card-r07.front: What rule applies if you bring children or pets along to the facility on road-test day?
sec03-card-r07.expected_back: Children and pets cannot be left at the facility without supervision during a driving test; an applicant bringing them needs another caretaker.

sec03-card-r08.front: Who has to wear safety belts throughout the Illinois driving examination?
sec03-card-r08.expected_back: Both the examiner and applicant must use safety belts during the driving examination.

sec03-card-r09.front: What two on-road events trigger an automatic failure during the driving examination?
sec03-card-r09.expected_back: A traffic violation or dangerous action during the road test produces an automatic failure.

sec03-card-r10.front: What cabin checks and adjustments should you complete before putting the road-test car in motion?
sec03-card-r10.expected_back: Before moving the road-test vehicle, check the controls and adjust the seat, belt, mirrors and other equipment.

sec03-card-r11.front: How far, how fast, and where should you look during the road-test backing maneuver?
sec03-card-r11.expected_back: The road test includes backing about fifty feet slowly in a smooth, straight path while turning the head right to look behind.

sec03-card-r12.front: How do you signal and position the car during the tested left-side alley turnabout?
sec03-card-r12.memory_hook: Signal left in, back proper side
sec03-card-r12.expected_back: For the tested turnabout, signal left before entering an alley on the left, then back out while remaining on the proper side of the road.

sec03-card-r13.front: Which uphill and downhill tasks are graded as part of the Illinois road test?
sec03-card-r13.expected_back: The road-test tasks include parking uphill, parking downhill and starting from each parked slope position.

sec03-card-r14.front: Which five traffic-rule and communication habits count toward road-test vehicle control?
sec03-card-r14.expected_back: Road-test vehicle control includes compliance with signs, traffic controls, right-of-way rules and lane markings, together with correct turn-signal use.

sec03-card-r15.front: What two accessible-parking credentials does the agency issue as special services?
sec03-card-r15.expected_back: The agency provides disability parking plates and placards as special services.

sec03-card-r16.front: Who can qualify for reduced license-plate renewal fees through the Benefit Access Program?
sec03-card-r16.expected_back: Seniors aged sixty-five or older and persons with disabilities who satisfy the Benefit Access Program’s income conditions may qualify for reduced plate-renewal fees.

sec03-card-r17.front: How should a deaf or hard-of-hearing applicant arrange interpreter assistance for licensing?
sec03-card-r17.expected_back: A deaf or hard-of-hearing applicant can request an interpreter for license issuance or renewal and should arrange the service before visiting.

sec03-card-r18.front: Who can request an in-person oral written exam, and on which days of the week is it offered?
sec03-card-r18.expected_back: An applicant facing a language barrier or a reading or learning disability may request an oral written examination in person at a license facility from Monday through Thursday.

sec04-card-f01.front: How many minimum classroom hours and instructor behind-the-wheel hours make up an approved Illinois driver-ed course?
sec04-card-f01.expected_back: An approved Illinois driver-education course includes at least thirty classroom hours and six hours driving a regular passenger vehicle with an instructor.

sec04-card-f02.front: What driver-education enrollment proof must a fifteen- through seventeen-year-old bring to get an instruction permit?
sec04-card-f02.memory_hook: Enrolled now or starting thirty days
sec04-card-f02.expected_back: An applicant aged fifteen through seventeen needs provider evidence of enrollment in approved driver education or a course starting within thirty days to receive an instruction permit.

sec04-card-f03.front: For ages fifteen through seventeen, how long is an instruction permit valid, and how long must you hold it before licensing?
sec04-card-f03.expected_back: For ages fifteen through seventeen, an instruction permit lasts twenty-four months and must be held for nine consecutive months before licensing.

sec04-card-f04.front: At what exact age can an Illinois teen apply for an instruction permit without taking driver education?
sec04-card-f04.expected_back: Beginning at seventeen years and three months, an applicant may seek an instruction permit without taking driver education.

sec04-card-f05.front: Which two exams are required for a permit, and how long do those passing scores stay good?
sec04-card-f05.expected_back: A permit applicant must pass the vision and written examinations for the requested license class, and those results remain valid until the permit expires.

sec04-card-f06.front: What school-led driving activity does your instruction permit authorize?
sec04-card-f06.expected_back: An instruction permit allows behind-the-wheel instruction in the driver-education course.

sec04-card-f07.front: Outside driver-ed lessons, what age, license, experience, and seating rules apply to a permit supervisor?
sec04-card-f07.expected_back: Other permit practice requires a parent, guardian or responsible adult who is at least twenty-one, holds a valid license and has a year of driving experience, seated beside the learner in front.

sec04-card-f08.front: Does finishing driver education let a permit holder drive solo, or what rule stays in place?
sec04-card-f08.expected_back: After finishing driver education, a permit holder may continue practicing under the same direct adult supervision.

sec04-card-f09.front: How many supervised practice hours—and how many at night—must an under-eighteen applicant complete beyond driver ed?
sec04-card-f09.expected_back: Before licensing at sixteen, an applicant younger than eighteen must complete fifty supervised practice hours, including ten at night, in addition to driver-education training.

sec04-card-f10.front: How are Illinois licenses formatted visually for drivers younger than twenty-one?
sec04-card-f10.expected_back: Licenses for people younger than twenty-one use a vertical layout with distinguishing features.

sec04-card-f11.front: Which documents, logs, and certificates must an applicant under eighteen bring on licensing day?
sec04-card-f11.expected_back: An applicant younger than eighteen brings the instruction permit, acceptable identity documents, a properly signed fifty-hour log and any applicable minor-consent affidavit or Cooperative Driver Testing Certificate.

sec04-card-f12.front: What additional paperwork rule applies when a young driver asks for a REAL ID license?
sec04-card-f12.expected_back: A young applicant requesting REAL ID must also provide the full first-time REAL ID identity-document set.

sec04-card-f13.front: What must reach and post to your Illinois driving record before the facility can issue your teen license?
sec04-card-f13.expected_back: License issuance requires the agency to receive the driver-education completion notice and post it to the applicant’s driving record.

sec04-card-f14.front: What happens if your birthday lands on a state spot-check date even after passing your school instructor's road test?
sec04-card-f14.expected_back: A student selected by a birthday-based spot-check date must pass a facility road test even after passing the instructor’s road test.

sec04-card-f15.front: When does a teen avoid paying an extra license-application fee when upgrading from an instruction permit?
sec04-card-f15.expected_back: An applicant licensed before the instruction permit expires does not pay an additional license-application fee.

sec04-card-f16.front: What high-school course grades can exempt a student from taking the state facility road test?
sec04-card-f16.expected_back: A high-school student completing accredited classroom and driving instruction with a combined A or B grade may qualify for exemption from the agency’s road test through cooperative testing.

sec04-card-f17.front: Whose two signatures must appear on a Cooperative Driver Testing Certificate after you pass the school road exam?
sec04-card-f17.expected_back: A Cooperative Driver Testing Certificate follows a successful driving examination and needs both the instructor’s signature and the parent’s or guardian’s signature.

sec04-card-f18.front: When does a Cooperative Driver Testing Certificate expire, and can it ever be extended?
sec04-card-f18.expected_back: The cooperative-testing certificate expires with the instruction permit, cannot be extended and must be presented when applying for the license.

sec04-card-f19.front: Which four exceptions allow a school dropout under eighteen to still receive the driver-education completion notation?
sec04-card-f19.expected_back: A dropout younger than eighteen needs a qualifying exception before the education-completion notation can be added: verified alternative-program enrollment, a GED, eight passed courses in the preceding two semesters or the required written consents.

sec04-card-f20.front: Whose written approvals are required to use the dropout-consent exception?
sec04-card-f20.expected_back: The dropout-consent exception requires written consent from the parent or guardian and the regional superintendent.

sec04-card-f21.front: Who has authority to waive dropout licensing restrictions when enforcing them hurts the student's best interest?
sec04-card-f21.expected_back: A local superintendent or chief school administrator may waive dropout conditions considered contrary to the student’s best interest.

sec04-card-f22.front: What course must a first-time eighteen- through twenty-year-old finish if they never held a license or took teen driver ed?
sec04-card-f22.expected_back: A first-time applicant aged eighteen through twenty who has neither a previous license nor approved driver education must complete a six-hour adult driver-education course.

sec04-card-f23.front: What provider rule governs classroom or online six-hour adult courses, and what happens with uncertified courses?
sec04-card-f23.expected_back: The adult course must come from an agency-certified provider; classroom or online delivery depends on that provider’s certification, and an uncertified course is not accepted.

sec04-card-f24.front: Which age span and how many progressive stages make up Illinois graduated licensing, and what governs moving up?
sec04-card-f24.expected_back: Illinois graduated licensing covers ages fifteen through twenty through three progressive phases, with advancement dependent on driving behavior.

sec04-card-r01.front: What are the Illinois nighttime driving curfews during the permit phase on weeknights versus weekends?
sec04-card-r01.expected_back: During the permit phase, nighttime restrictions run from ten at night until six in the morning Sunday through Thursday and from eleven at night until six Friday and Saturday, subject to differing local curfews.

sec04-card-r02.front: What minimum holding months, total practice hours, night hours, and coach age apply during the permit phase?
sec04-card-r02.memory_hook: Nine months, fifty hours, ten night
sec04-card-r02.expected_back: The permit phase requires at least nine months and fifty supervised practice hours, including ten after dark, with a licensed parent or adult at least twenty-one.

sec04-card-r03.front: Which three types of violations or dispositions cannot appear during your nine-month permit phase?
sec04-card-r03.expected_back: The nine-month permit phase must be free of driving infractions, underage alcohol convictions and court supervision.

sec04-card-r04.front: How many passengers may ride in the front and back seats during the permit phase?
sec04-card-r04.expected_back: Permit-phase passengers are limited to one in the front and the number of available safety belts in the rear.

sec04-card-r05.front: Until what age are Illinois drivers banned from all wireless phone use—even hands-free—and what is the lone exception?
sec04-card-r05.expected_back: A driver younger than nineteen cannot use a cellphone or wireless device while driving, including hands-free use, except an emergency contact with police, a health-care provider or an emergency-services agency.

sec04-card-r06.front: Which nighttime driving restrictions apply to sixteen- and seventeen-year-old initial license holders?
sec04-card-r06.expected_back: For initial license holders aged sixteen or seventeen, nighttime restrictions use ten-to-six Sunday through Thursday and eleven-to-six Friday and Saturday, with local curfews potentially different.

sec04-card-r07.front: How many conviction-free months must an initial license holder log before turning eighteen, and what happens after a ticket?
sec04-card-r07.expected_back: An initial license holder must keep six conviction-free months before turning eighteen; a conviction in this phase can extend restrictions beyond the eighteenth birthday.

sec04-card-r08.front: For the first twelve licensed months or until eighteen, how many passengers under twenty are allowed, and which relatives are exempt?
sec04-card-r08.expected_back: Until the earlier of twelve licensed months or age eighteen, only one passenger younger than twenty is allowed unless the passengers are the driver’s siblings, stepsiblings, children or stepchildren.

sec04-card-r09.front: Once that initial twelve-month young-passenger window ends, what cabin seating limit still applies?
sec04-card-r09.expected_back: After the initial young-passenger period, passengers remain limited to one front-seat occupant and the number of rear safety belts.

sec04-card-r10.front: What happens to age restrictions in the full eighteen-to-twenty phase, and which wireless rule still lingers at eighteen?
sec04-card-r10.memory_hook: Age limits lift, under-nineteen phone stays
sec04-card-r10.expected_back: Full licensing at ages eighteen through twenty removes age-based restrictions unless the driver failed to advance out of the initial phase; the under-nineteen wireless restriction still applies.

sec04-card-r11.front: Who can cancel a sixteen- or seventeen-year-old's Illinois driver's license at any time and for any reason?
sec04-card-r11.expected_back: Licensing at sixteen or seventeen requires written parental or guardian consent, and the person who gave it may cancel the license for any reason before the driver turns eighteen.

sec04-card-r12.front: If a parent withdraws consent, when and how can the teen regain an Illinois license?
sec04-card-r12.expected_back: After consent is withdrawn, privileges cannot return until that person consents again or the driver turns eighteen, whichever comes first; the driver must reapply, take required exams and pay applicable fees.

sec04-card-r13.front: How can a parent or guardian check an under-eighteen teen's driving record online without paying?
sec04-card-r13.expected_back: A parent or guardian can view an under-eighteen permit or graduated-license holder’s driving record free online using the agency-provided personal identification number.

sec04-card-r14.front: How can an under-twenty-one permit holder and parent verify online whether high-school driver ed has posted?
sec04-card-r14.expected_back: A valid permit holder younger than twenty-one and the parent or guardian can use the permit number online to check whether high-school driver-education completion is recorded.

sec04-card-r15.front: Which two family resources does the agency offer to help parents and teens agree on driving rules?
sec04-card-r15.expected_back: The agency offers a Parent-Teen Driving Guide and a voluntary driving contract to help families set learning expectations and boundaries.

sec04-card-r16.front: How is court supervision restricted for drivers under twenty-one, and what class must they complete to get it?
sec04-card-r16.expected_back: A driver younger than twenty-one is limited to one court supervision for serious traffic offenses and must attend traffic safety school to obtain supervision for a traffic violation.

sec04-card-r17.front: Who must appear in court alongside a driver under eighteen seeking court supervision for a ticket?
sec04-card-r17.expected_back: A driver younger than eighteen seeking court supervision for a traffic violation must appear with a parent or guardian.

sec04-card-r18.front: How long can court supervision for certain alcohol offenses delay a minor's full graduated license?
sec04-card-r18.expected_back: Court supervision for certain alcohol offenses can postpone a minor’s full graduated license for nine months.

sec04-card-r19.front: What happens to a driver under twenty-one convicted of two or more moving violations within twenty-four months?
sec04-card-r19.expected_back: For a driver younger than twenty-one, at least two moving-violation convictions within twenty-four months lead to a license suspension of at least thirty days, with duration depending on offense seriousness.

sec04-card-r20.front: After a young-driver suspension, what extra class might reinstatement require, and are hardship permits guaranteed?
sec04-card-r20.expected_back: Reinstatement after a young-driver suspension may require remedial driver education, and eligibility for a restricted permit during suspension is not guaranteed.

sec04-card-r21.front: For an under-twenty-one vehicle occupant caught with alcohol, what suspension hits for court supervision versus a conviction?
sec04-card-r21.expected_back: An under-twenty-one vehicle occupant receiving court supervision for possessing, consuming, buying or receiving alcohol faces a three-month license suspension; conviction brings at least six months.

sec04-card-r22.front: What license penalty can hit an under-eighteen permit or initial-license driver caught breaking nighttime curfew?
sec04-card-r22.expected_back: A permit or initial-phase driver younger than eighteen may have driving privileges suspended for violating the nighttime driving restriction.

sec04-card-r23.front: What licensing block can hit an under-eighteen driver charged after a serious-injury or fatal crash, even with zero alcohol?
sec04-card-r23.expected_back: An under-eighteen driver charged after a crash causing serious injury or death may be denied license issuance or renewal even if alcohol was not involved.

sec04-card-r24.front: How does an unresolved court traffic ticket affect someone under eighteen applying for a license?
sec04-card-r24.expected_back: An unresolved court traffic citation can prevent license issuance for someone younger than eighteen.

sec05-card-f01.front: Which four groups of officials must drivers obey when they direct traffic?
sec05-card-f01.expected_back: Drivers must obey traffic directions from police, firefighters, highway officials and uniformed adult school-crossing guards acting in their official roles.

sec05-card-f02.front: How should you pull over for a police stop, and what if the right shoulder is unsafe?
sec05-card-f02.expected_back: For a police stop, slow down, signal and pull safely onto the right shoulder; if it cannot safely accommodate the vehicle, continue to the next safe stopping place.

sec05-card-f03.front: What braking mistakes and hazardous locations should you avoid during a police traffic stop?
sec05-card-f03.expected_back: During a police stop, avoid sudden hard braking, stopping in a traffic lane or choosing bridges, curves, barriers or other places where traffic cannot pass safely.

sec05-card-f04.front: Once stopped for police, what should you do with your body and hands while waiting?
sec05-card-f04.expected_back: After stopping, stay inside with both hands visible on the steering wheel until instructed otherwise or the stop is finished.

sec05-card-f05.front: Which side of your car might an officer approach, and when may you step out?
sec05-card-f05.expected_back: An officer may approach either side of a stopped vehicle, and the driver should not get out unless the officer asks.

sec05-card-f06.front: How should you handle retrieving your license or phone-based insurance proof during a traffic stop?
sec05-card-f06.expected_back: Provide a requested license and insurance proof, but tell the officer where the items are and follow directions before reaching into storage or using the phone displaying insurance.

sec05-card-f07.front: Which three valid items are legally required to operate a motor vehicle in Illinois?
sec05-card-f07.expected_back: Operating a vehicle requires a valid license, registration and insurance.

sec05-card-f08.front: What should you do if you cannot confirm whether an unmarked vehicle pulling you over is real police?
sec05-card-f08.expected_back: If an unmarked vehicle or its driver cannot be identified as police, proceed carefully below the limit toward a well-lit populated stop or police station, or call nine hundred eleven; hazard lights can communicate intentions.

sec05-card-f09.front: Is switching on your dome light appropriate during a nighttime police stop?
sec05-card-f09.expected_back: Turning on the vehicle’s interior light is acceptable during a nighttime police stop.

sec05-card-f10.front: Does signing an Illinois traffic ticket mean you are pleading guilty?
sec05-card-f10.expected_back: A driver should sign an issued traffic ticket; the signature acknowledges receiving it rather than admitting guilt.

sec05-card-f11.front: Where should a disputed traffic ticket be argued, and how must you behave if arrested?
sec05-card-f11.expected_back: Disputes about a traffic ticket belong in traffic court rather than an argument at the roadside, and a driver should not resist an arrest.

sec05-card-f12.front: What identifying details must an officer give on request, and how are misconduct concerns handled?
sec05-card-f12.expected_back: An officer must provide a name and badge number when asked, and concerns about improper conduct can be reported to supervisors or submitted through the agency’s complaint channels.

sec05-card-f13.front: What driver details must be recorded during every Illinois traffic stop, even without a ticket?
sec05-card-f13.expected_back: Every traffic stop must be documented, including collection of the driver’s name and address, regardless of the action taken.

sec05-card-f14.front: What phone uses does Illinois ban behind the wheel, and at what age is hands-free allowed?
sec05-card-f14.expected_back: Illinois prohibits handheld phone use, texting and other electronic communications while driving; hands-free or Bluetooth use is permitted for drivers aged nineteen or older.

sec05-card-f15.front: When is an electronic earpiece legal while driving in Illinois, and how are hearing aids treated?
sec05-card-f15.expected_back: Headsets for receiving electronic communications are prohibited except for a permitted single-sided cellphone earpiece; a hearing aid is excluded from the headset definition.

sec05-card-f16.front: Even with legal hands-free gear, what does the Illinois handbook advise before placing a call?
sec05-card-f16.expected_back: Hands-free technology can still distract, and the handbook recommends pulling off the road before making a call even when the system is hands-free.

sec05-card-f17.front: Does holding a phone in your hand on speakerphone count as legal hands-free driving?
sec05-card-f17.expected_back: Holding a phone while using its speaker does not qualify as hands-free operation.

sec05-card-f18.front: Are live video streaming, video calls, or scrolling social media legal while driving in Illinois?
sec05-card-f18.expected_back: Watching or streaming live video, joining a video conference or accessing social media on a cellphone while driving violates Illinois law.

sec05-card-f19.front: Under which three specific situations may a driver legally use a handheld phone?
sec05-card-f19.expected_back: Non-hands-free phone use is allowed to report an emergency, while parked on the shoulder, or during an obstruction of normal traffic when the vehicle is in park or neutral.

sec05-card-f20.front: Beyond a traffic fine, what severe legal consequences can follow a distracted-driving crash?
sec05-card-f20.expected_back: A distracted-driving crash involving another road user can expose the driver to criminal punishment and incarceration.

sec05-card-f21.front: Who must wear a safety belt in Illinois, and do air bags change that rule?
sec05-card-f21.expected_back: Every driver and passenger aged eight or older must wear a safety belt in either seat row, including in vehicles with air bags; younger children need an appropriate child restraint.

sec05-card-f22.front: Who must buckle and adjust the seat belt if a passenger's medical condition or disability prevents them?
sec05-card-f22.expected_back: The driver must secure and adjust the belt for a passenger whose disability or medical condition prevents that passenger from doing so.

sec05-card-f23.front: Who holds legal responsibility for making sure every passenger obeys Illinois belt and child-restraint laws?
sec05-card-f23.expected_back: The driver is responsible for every passenger’s compliance with the belt and child-restraint laws.

sec05-card-f24.front: Where across your body should the lap portion of a seat belt rest?
sec05-card-f24.expected_back: Position the lap belt over the hip bones rather than the stomach or soft abdomen.

sec05-card-f25.front: How should your shoulder belt fit, and which two shortcuts must you never take?
sec05-card-f25.expected_back: Keep the shoulder belt snug while preserving access to driving controls, and never route it behind the back or beneath an arm.

sec05-card-f26.front: How are air bags designed to work in relation to safety belts?
sec05-card-f26.expected_back: An air bag supplements a safety belt and is intended to work together with the belt.

sec05-card-f27.front: How many inches of space does the handbook recommend between the driver and the steering-wheel air bag?
sec05-card-f27.expected_back: The handbook recommends ten to twelve inches between the driver and the air bag, particularly for short, older or pregnant drivers.

sec05-card-f28.front: How should front-seat passengers adjust their seat relative to the dashboard air bag?
sec05-card-f28.expected_back: Passengers should move the seat as far back as possible, with a slight seat-back tilt if necessary.

sec05-card-f29.front: Up through what age does the Illinois handbook recommend securing children in the back seat, and why?
sec05-card-f29.expected_back: The handbook recommends properly securing children aged twelve or younger in the rear seat because a deploying front air bag can cause severe or fatal injury.

sec05-card-f30.front: What two steps are required if a child under eight has no choice except riding ahead of an active air bag?
sec05-card-f30.expected_back: If a child younger than eight must sit ahead of an active passenger air bag, use the appropriate properly installed restraint and move the seat as far back as possible.

sec05-card-f31.front: May a rear-facing infant seat ever be placed in front of an active air bag?
sec05-card-f31.expected_back: Never install a rear-facing child restraint in front of an active air bag.

sec05-card-f32.front: Until what age must children use a child restraint, and what belt type must pair with a booster seat?
sec05-card-f32.expected_back: Children younger than eight must use a suitable child restraint, and a booster must be used with a combined lap-and-shoulder belt.

sec05-card-f33.front: When may a child ride in the back seat using only a lap belt without a booster?
sec05-card-f33.expected_back: When the rear seat has no lap-and-shoulder belts, a child weighing more than forty pounds may ride there using a lap belt without a booster.

sec05-card-f34.front: Until what age, weight, or height must Illinois children ride in a rear-facing restraint?
sec05-card-f34.expected_back: Children must remain in a rear-facing restraint until age two unless their weight exceeds forty pounds or their height exceeds forty inches.

sec05-card-f35.front: When is driving the maximum limit appropriate, and what limits how slowly you may drive?
sec05-card-f35.expected_back: The maximum posted or default speed is appropriate only when conditions make it safe, and an unposted minimum does not permit driving slowly enough to obstruct ordinary traffic.

sec05-card-f36.front: What is the default Illinois speed limit on rural interstates and tollways when no other limit is posted?
sec05-card-f36.expected_back: Unless a different limit is posted, interstates and toll roads have a seventy-mile-per-hour limit.

sec05-card-f37.front: What default speed limit applies on an Illinois four-lane highway unless signs state otherwise?
sec05-card-f37.expected_back: A four-lane highway has a default limit of sixty-five miles per hour unless posted otherwise.

sec05-card-r01.front: What is the default Illinois speed limit on other highways and rural roads without posted signs?
sec05-card-r01.expected_back: The default for other highways and rural roads is fifty-five miles per hour when another limit is not posted.

sec05-card-r02.front: Unless posted otherwise, what default speed limit governs Illinois cities and towns?
sec05-card-r02.expected_back: Cities and towns have a default thirty-mile-per-hour limit, subject to a different posted limit.

sec05-card-r03.front: What is the default maximum speed inside an Illinois alley unless another limit is posted?
sec05-card-r03.expected_back: The default alley speed limit is fifteen miles per hour unless a different limit is posted.

sec05-card-r04.front: What speed limit, hours, and conditions apply in a posted Illinois school zone?
sec05-card-r04.expected_back: A posted school zone has a twenty-mile-per-hour limit on school days from six thirty in the morning until four in the afternoon when children are present.

sec05-card-r05.front: Can cities or counties set speed limits that differ from Illinois's statutory defaults?
sec05-card-r05.expected_back: Local governments may post limits different from the handbook’s defaults.

sec05-card-r06.front: Which road features and changing conditions require slowing below normal cruising speed?
sec05-card-r06.expected_back: Slow when approaching or crossing intersections, rounding curves, nearing hilltops or using narrow winding roads, while accounting for people, traffic, weather, equipment and road hazards.

sec05-card-r07.front: What five safety duties apply when approaching or driving through an Illinois construction zone?
sec05-card-r07.expected_back: When nearing or entering road work, slow down, stop wireless use other than allowed hands-free use, yield to workers and authorized vehicles, move away from workers if possible and proceed carefully.

sec05-card-r08.front: Does a posted Illinois work-zone speed limit still apply at midnight when no workers are on site?
sec05-card-r08.expected_back: A posted work-zone limit applies around the clock every day whether or not workers are present, and reduced speed continues until safely beyond workers and authorized vehicles.

sec05-card-r09.front: What physical roadway changes show up inside work zones, and when must you slow even further?
sec05-card-r09.expected_back: Work areas can contain narrow lanes, pavement edges or drop-offs, closures, equipment and nearby obstructions, with additional speed reductions when workers are present.

sec05-card-r10.front: What must you do when approaching a stationary emergency or maintenance vehicle flashing warning lights?
sec05-card-r10.expected_back: Near a stationary emergency or maintenance vehicle using warning lights, yield, move to a lane farther from workers when possible and continue cautiously at a speed suited to traffic conditions.

sec05-card-r11.front: How must you pass a stopped emergency scene if heavy traffic makes changing lanes impossible?
sec05-card-r11.memory_hook: Cannot move over, slow way down
sec05-card-r11.expected_back: If a lane change away from a stationary emergency scene is impossible, slow down and proceed carefully, keeping the reduced speed until safely beyond the stopped emergency vehicles.

sec05-card-r12.front: Within what distance of an emergency scene does Illinois restrict taking photos or using wireless phones?
sec05-card-r12.memory_hook: No phones within five hundred feet
sec05-card-r12.expected_back: Illinois restricts photography and wireless-phone use within five hundred feet of an emergency scene, with exceptions the handbook does not specify in this paragraph.

sec05-card-r13.front: How must you react when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights or a siren?
sec05-card-r13.expected_back: When an emergency vehicle approaches using warning lights or a siren, move immediately to the road’s right side and let it pass, stopping if necessary.

sec05-card-r14.front: What should you do if an emergency vehicle approaches while you are already stopped at a two-way intersection?
sec05-card-r14.expected_back: If already stopped at a two-way-traffic intersection, remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed through it.

sec05-card-r15.front: When, if ever, may you drive your vehicle across a fire hose laid on the street?
sec05-card-r15.expected_back: Do not drive across a fire hose without permission from the fire official controlling the scene.

sec05-card-r16.front: How do vehicles in an Illinois funeral procession identify themselves, and who gets right-of-way?
sec05-card-r16.expected_back: Yield to every vehicle in a funeral procession, whose drivers should use headlights and hazard lights.

sec05-card-r17.front: What three maneuvers are prohibited around an organized funeral procession?
sec05-card-r17.expected_back: Do not cut between organized funeral vehicles unless police direct it, join a procession to gain priority or pass it without a specifically provided passing lane.

sec05-card-r18.front: What vehicle penalty can a local town impose on a driver who recklessly interferes with a funeral procession?
sec05-card-r18.expected_back: A municipality may impound a vehicle that interferes recklessly with a funeral procession.

sec05-card-r19.front: After coming to a full stop for an allowed right turn on red, which three road users must you yield to?
sec05-card-r19.expected_back: After stopping before a permitted right turn on red, yield to other vehicles, bicycles and pedestrians.

sec05-card-r20.front: Where in priority order must you halt at a stop sign or flashing red light?
sec05-card-r20.expected_back: At a stop sign or flashing red light, stop at the line, otherwise before the crosswalk, or where approaching traffic is visible if neither marking exists, then yield appropriately.

sec05-card-r21.front: Under what street layout and duties is a left turn on red permitted in Illinois?
sec05-card-r21.expected_back: After stopping, a left turn on red from a one-way road to another one-way road carrying traffic leftward requires yielding to other road users.

sec05-card-r22.front: Who goes first at a four-way stop, and how are ties broken between different roads?
sec05-card-r22.expected_back: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle stopped goes first; simultaneous arrivals from different roads give priority to the vehicle on the right.

sec05-card-r23.front: At an intersection with no signs or lights, who yields when two cars arrive from different streets together?
sec05-card-r23.expected_back: At an uncontrolled intersection, simultaneous arrivals from different roads require the left vehicle to yield to the right vehicle.

sec05-card-r24.front: What must you do before entering an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow arrow?
sec05-card-r24.expected_back: A flashing yellow arrow requires yielding before entering the intersection.

sec05-card-r25.front: Who must a left-turning driver yield to, and what happens if the light turns red after entering on green?
sec05-card-r25.expected_back: A driver turning left yields to approaching traffic, and a turn begun after entering on green may be finished if the signal turns red.

sec05-card-r26.front: How does your required action at a merge sign differ from your duty at a yield sign?
sec05-card-r26.expected_back: At a merge sign, adjust speed to avoid conflict with through traffic; at a yield sign, slow or stop as needed to avoid a collision.

sec05-card-r27.front: Does a fresh green light let you pull into vehicles still clearing the intersection?
sec05-card-r27.expected_back: A green light does not remove the duty to yield to vehicles already inside the intersection.

sec05-card-r28.front: What two steps are mandatory before pulling onto a street from a driveway, alley, building, or private road?
sec05-card-r28.expected_back: Before entering a road from an alley, building exit, private road or driveway, stop completely and yield.

sec05-card-r29.front: Who must yield at an unsigned T-intersection where one street dead-ends into a continuing road?
sec05-card-r29.expected_back: At an uncontrolled T intersection, traffic on the road that ends yields to traffic crossing on the continuing road.

sec05-card-r30.front: When must you hold back even if your signal is green at an intersection or marked crosswalk?
sec05-card-r30.expected_back: Do not enter an intersection or marked crosswalk without sufficient space for other vehicles and pedestrians to pass.

sec05-card-r31.front: What action is required for someone in a marked crosswalk or children near a school-zone crosswalk on school days?
sec05-card-r31.expected_back: Stop completely and yield for someone in a marked crosswalk and, on school days, for children close to a school-zone crosswalk.

sec05-card-r32.front: When must you yield to a pedestrian crossing in an unmarked crosswalk at an unsignalized corner?
sec05-card-r32.expected_back: Yield to a person in an unmarked crossing on your side of an unsignalized roadway.

sec05-card-r33.front: Must you still yield to pedestrians when turning after a stop sign, flashing red, or red light?
sec05-card-r33.expected_back: Yield to pedestrians while turning at an intersection, including a lawful turn on red after stopping or a turn following a stop sign or flashing red.

sec05-card-r34.front: Who keeps right-of-way if a pedestrian started crossing legally before the traffic signal changed?
sec05-card-r34.expected_back: A pedestrian who entered before a light changed or proceeds with a green light or walking signal must receive the right of way.

sec05-card-r35.front: How must you treat pedestrians at alleys, driveways, building exits, and flashing-yellow-arrow corners?
sec05-card-r35.expected_back: Yield to pedestrians entering or leaving the roadway at an alley, building, private road or driveway, and at an intersection displaying a flashing yellow arrow.

sec05-card-r36.front: Which categories of pedestrian disabilities specifically receive right-of-way protection from Illinois drivers?
sec05-card-r36.expected_back: Drivers must yield to people with disabilities, including physical, hearing and visual disabilities.

sec06-card-f01.front: What must you confirm about the oncoming lane before passing on a two-lane road?
sec06-card-f01.expected_back: Before passing on a two-lane road, make sure the opposing lane is visible and clear far enough ahead to complete the maneuver.

sec06-card-f02.front: What mirror cue and oncoming-car distance tell you when to finish returning to the right lane?
sec06-card-f02.expected_back: Return to the right lane only after the entire passed vehicle appears in the rearview mirror, and finish returning before coming within two hundred feet of an approaching vehicle.

sec06-card-f03.front: What speed rule applies to your vehicle while another driver is passing you?
sec06-card-f03.expected_back: A driver being passed must not accelerate until the other driver finishes passing.

sec06-card-f04.front: Is flashing your turn signal to wave a trailing driver past you legal in Illinois?
sec06-card-f04.expected_back: Using flashing turn signals to invite another driver to pass is unlawful.

sec06-card-f05.front: May you ever drive off the pavement or main traveled roadway to pass on either side?
sec06-card-f05.expected_back: Passing on either side does not permit leaving the pavement or the road’s main traveled portion.

sec06-card-f06.front: How much side clearance must you leave when passing someone walking on the road or shoulder?
sec06-card-f06.expected_back: Leave at least three feet when passing a person walking on the road or its shoulder.

sec06-card-f07.front: What minimum clearance applies when passing a bicycle, even if the rider is on a shoulder or bike lane?
sec06-card-f07.expected_back: Keep at least three feet from a bicycle when passing, including when the rider is on a shoulder or in a dedicated bike lane.

sec06-card-f08.front: When may an ordinary driver legally pass on the right, and what surface remains off-limits?
sec06-card-f08.expected_back: Passing on the right is permitted with enough space beside a left-turning vehicle on a two-lane road, on a one-way road, with two clear lanes each way or at an intersection widened for it; ordinary drivers may not use the shoulder.

sec06-card-f09.front: Which pavement marking and roadside sign forbid passing on a two-lane two-way road?
sec06-card-f09.expected_back: On a two-way road with two lanes, do not pass where a solid yellow line or no-passing sign prohibits it.

sec06-card-f10.front: Why must you stay in your lane on hills and curves along a two-lane two-way road?
sec06-card-f10.expected_back: Do not pass on a two-lane two-way road at a hill or curve hiding opposing vehicles.

sec06-card-f11.front: Within what distance of an intersection or railroad crossing is passing banned on a two-lane two-way road?
sec06-card-f11.expected_back: On a two-lane two-way road, passing is prohibited within one hundred feet of an intersection or railway crossing.

sec06-card-f12.front: When does approaching a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel trigger a hundred-foot no-passing rule?
sec06-card-f12.expected_back: Passing on a two-lane two-way road is prohibited where the view is blocked within one hundred feet of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel.

sec06-card-f13.front: Which two stopped vehicles must you never overtake at a crossing or roadside stop?
sec06-card-f13.expected_back: Never pass a vehicle stopped at a crossing or intersection for a pedestrian, or a stopped school bus loading or unloading passengers.

sec06-card-f14.front: How does Illinois treat passing inside construction zones and school zones?
sec06-card-f14.expected_back: Illinois construction zones are no-passing zones, as are school zones in unincorporated areas and posted school zones in incorporated areas.

sec06-card-f15.front: Which half of the roadway do drivers generally use, and what common situations create exceptions?
sec06-card-f15.expected_back: The general rule is to use the road’s right half, with listed exceptions for passing, certain marked lanes, one-way roads and directed lane use.

sec06-card-f16.front: What must you do before steering left of center to get around an obstruction in your lane?
sec06-card-f16.expected_back: A blockage may justify crossing left of center only after yielding to approaching traffic.

sec06-card-f17.front: Is crossing the centerline allowed when turning left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway?
sec06-card-f17.expected_back: Crossing the center to turn left into or out of a private road, alley or driveway is among the keep-right exceptions.

sec06-card-f18.front: Which stopped vehicles or roadside conditions justify moving left away from the right lane?
sec06-card-f18.expected_back: Approaching a stopped emergency or disabled vehicle, or construction close to the right lane or shoulder, can justify moving left under the roadway-position exceptions.

sec06-card-f19.front: What is the primary purpose of the left lane on Illinois interstates, and when may you stay in it?
sec06-card-f19.expected_back: On interstates and fully controlled-access freeways, left lanes are generally for passing, with exceptions for no vehicle directly behind, congestion, weather, right-lane hazards or yielding to emergency or construction vehicles.
