sec06-card-f20.front: Which lane should slower traffic stay in, and what two maneuvers allow leaving it?
sec06-card-f20.expected_back: Slow vehicles should remain in the right lane except to pass or turn left.

sec06-card-f21.front: Is darting back and forth between lanes to move faster than surrounding traffic legal?
sec06-card-f21.expected_back: Weaving between lanes to travel faster than the flow is illegal.

sec06-card-f22.front: Who is exempt from following the posted arrow direction on an Illinois one-way street?
sec06-card-f22.expected_back: Follow the posted direction on a one-way road, except for authorized police or emergency vehicles using a siren or flashing lights.

sec06-card-f23.front: May you drive across an unpaved median strip or median barrier on a divided road?
sec06-card-f23.expected_back: Driving across an unpaved median strip or median barrier is unlawful.

sec06-card-f24.front: Where are you legally allowed to get onto or off a controlled-access highway?
sec06-card-f24.expected_back: Use only posted entrances and exits to enter or leave a controlled-access highway.

sec06-card-f25.front: Where is backing up completely banned, and when is reversing legal on ordinary streets?
sec06-card-f25.expected_back: Backing is prohibited on the roadway or shoulder of a controlled-access highway; on other roads it is allowed only when safe and noninterfering.

sec06-card-f26.front: When may you open a vehicle door on the traffic side, and how long can it stay open?
sec06-card-f26.expected_back: A traffic-side door may be opened only when it is safe and does not obstruct vehicles or bicycles, and it may stay open only long enough for passengers to enter or leave.

sec06-card-f27.front: Which hand does the Illinois handbook recommend using to open your driver-side door, and why?
sec06-card-f27.expected_back: The handbook recommends opening a vehicle door with the right hand to encourage turning and checking approaching cars and bicycles.

sec06-card-f28.front: How does Illinois law treat street sideshows that block traffic for stunts or speed contests?
sec06-card-f28.expected_back: A street sideshow that blocks traffic for unauthorized stunts, speed contests or speed exhibitions is illegal.

sec06-card-f29.front: How far ahead must you signal continuously in business or residential districts versus other roads?
sec06-card-f29.expected_back: Signal continuously for at least one hundred feet before turning in a business or residential area and at least two hundred feet elsewhere.

sec06-card-f30.front: Which electric turn signal must you activate before making a turn?
sec06-card-f30.expected_back: Use the electrical signal matching the intended direction of the turn.

sec06-card-r01.front: How do you signal a right turn, left turn, and slow or stop using your left arm?
sec06-card-r01.expected_back: With the left arm, point upward for a right turn, straight left for a left turn and downward for slowing or stopping.

sec06-card-r02.front: How should you position, signal, yield, and scan when starting a right turn?
sec06-card-r02.expected_back: Begin a right turn in the correct turning lane with the right signal, obey controls, yield to pedestrians and other priority traffic and check traffic approaching from the left.

sec06-card-r03.front: How close to the curb should you track during a right turn, and which lane do you enter?
sec06-card-r03.expected_back: Follow the curb closely through a right turn and enter the right lane of the destination road.

sec06-card-r04.front: Which two road users need extra attention around right-turn corners?
sec06-card-r04.expected_back: Allow for trucks and buses needing extra turning space, and check bike lanes for cyclists approaching the intersection.

sec06-card-r05.front: What signaling, yielding, and scanning steps are required before making a left turn?
sec06-card-r05.expected_back: For a left turn, signal from the proper lane, obey traffic controls, yield to pedestrians and vehicles with priority and check traffic from every approach.

sec06-card-r06.front: How should your front wheels point while waiting to turn left, and which lane should you finish in?
sec06-card-r06.expected_back: Keep the front wheels pointing forward until beginning the left turn, then finish in the lane closest to the intended direction of travel.

sec06-card-r07.front: What head check is required before shifting from a right lane into a left lane?
sec06-card-r07.expected_back: Before moving from a right lane into a left lane, turn your head to examine traffic behind and to the left.

sec06-card-r08.front: What sequence of head check and signaling applies before moving into a right-hand lane?
sec06-card-r08.expected_back: Before changing right, turn your head to check behind and right, then signal right and move carefully only after confirming the space is clear.

sec06-card-r09.front: How many feet of clear visibility are required for a U-turn near a curve or hill, and can towns ban them?
sec06-card-r09.expected_back: A U-turn at a curve or hill requires visibility of at least five hundred feet in every direction, and local governments may prohibit U-turns on particular roads.

sec06-card-r10.front: What can flashing both turn signals simultaneously warn other drivers about?
sec06-card-r10.expected_back: Flashing both turn signals together can warn that a vehicle is disabled or parked.

sec06-card-r11.front: Which two kinds of left-turn maneuvers is a shared two-way left-turn lane built to handle?
sec06-card-r11.expected_back: A shared two-way left-turn lane serves left turns at intersections and left turns into or out of midblock driveways.

sec06-card-r12.front: What three temporary guides must you watch closely when turning or changing lanes inside roadwork?
sec06-card-r12.expected_back: When turning or changing lanes in road work, closely observe signs, barriers and pavement markings.

sec06-card-r13.front: Which way does roundabout traffic circulate around the center island, and can roundabouts have multiple lanes?
sec06-card-r13.expected_back: Traffic in a roundabout or rotary circulates counterclockwise around a central island, and a roundabout can contain several lanes.

sec06-card-r14.front: Who must drivers yield to when entering or exiting a roundabout?
sec06-card-r14.expected_back: Drivers entering or leaving a roundabout must yield to traffic, including people walking and cycling.

sec06-card-r15.front: How should you handle speed, turn direction, and lane discipline through a roundabout?
sec06-card-r15.expected_back: Slow on approach, follow movement restrictions, enter with a right turn when safe and remain in the selected lane.

sec06-card-r16.front: How should you choose and announce your exit from a roundabout?
sec06-card-r16.expected_back: Use the right signal to show a roundabout exit and read direction signs beforehand to choose the correct exit.

sec06-card-r17.front: What must you check for before changing lanes or peeling out of a multi-lane roundabout?
sec06-card-r17.expected_back: Before changing lanes or leaving a roundabout, check for traffic continuing around it and expect vehicles in blind spots beyond the mirrors’ view.

sec06-card-r18.front: On an Illinois four-lane road, must oncoming drivers stop for a school bus halted in the opposite direction?
sec06-card-r18.expected_back: On a four-lane road, a driver traveling opposite a stopped school bus is not required to stop for it.

sec06-card-r19.front: Outside the four-lane oncoming rule, where must you stop for a school bus loading or unloading riders?
sec06-card-r19.expected_back: Outside the stated exception, stop before meeting or passing a school bus loading or unloading passengers, including on two-lane roads, private roads and school parking lots.

sec06-card-r20.front: How far ahead do school-bus warning lights begin flashing in town versus rural areas before the stop arm extends?
sec06-card-r20.expected_back: A school bus warns of an upcoming stop with front and rear flashing lights at least one hundred feet beforehand, or two hundred feet in rural areas, and extends its stop arm after stopping.

sec06-card-r21.front: Once required to stop for a school bus, when may you start moving again?
sec06-card-r21.expected_back: An opposite-direction driver who must stop for a bus remains stopped until the arm retracts and flashing lights stop, or the bus driver directs traffic to pass.

sec06-card-r22.front: What three mandatory penalties hit a driver convicted of illegally passing a stopped school bus?
sec06-card-r22.expected_back: Conviction for passing a stopped bus using flashing lights and its extended arm causes license suspension, a mandatory three-hundred-dollar fine and court-ordered community service.

sec06-card-r23.front: What happens if your car illegally passes a school bus while someone else was driving and you refuse to name them?
sec06-card-r23.expected_back: An owner who was not driving during a stopped-bus violation must identify the driver to the prosecutor or face a three-month vehicle-registration suspension.

sec06-card-r24.front: Who always holds right-of-way at highway-rail intersections?
sec06-card-r24.expected_back: Yield to approaching trains and other railroad equipment.

sec06-card-r25.front: Within what distance range must you stop at a railroad crossing when signals, gates, signs, flaggers, or trains warn you?
sec06-card-r25.expected_back: At a railway crossing, stop fifteen to fifty feet away for a stop sign, flashing signal, lowered gate, flagger’s stop instruction or an approaching or warning train.

sec06-card-r26.front: What must you check before driving across a multi-track railroad crossing?
sec06-card-r26.expected_back: Look across every track for additional approaching trains or rail equipment before proceeding.

sec06-card-r27.front: How should you handle a railroad crossing that has no gates or lights—or only a crossbuck?
sec06-card-r27.expected_back: At a crossing without warning devices or with only a crossbuck, slow down, look both ways and listen, then cross carefully only when safe.

sec06-card-r28.front: What traffic space must exist on the far side before you drive onto railroad tracks?
sec06-card-r28.expected_back: Enter a railway crossing only when space beyond it can hold the whole vehicle clear of trains and rail equipment.

sec06-card-r29.front: Which three categories of commercial or public vehicles must stop at most railroad crossings?
sec06-card-r29.expected_back: Passenger-for-hire vehicles, school buses and hazardous-material carriers must stop at most railway crossings.

sec06-card-r30.front: If your car stalls or gets trapped on railroad tracks, how should everyone evacuate and which angle do you run?
sec06-card-r30.expected_back: If a vehicle stalls or becomes trapped on tracks, get everyone out immediately, call nine hundred eleven and move away at a forty-five-degree angle toward the approaching train to avoid forward-flying debris.

sec07-card-f01.front: Where do you find the railroad's emergency telephone number if a vehicle or hazard blocks the tracks?
sec07-card-f01.expected_back: The railroad’s emergency-notification telephone number appears on a blue sign attached to a crossing post near the tracks.

sec07-card-f02.front: What train expectation should you hold at every track, and what must you verify after one train passes?
sec07-card-f02.expected_back: Approach every railway track expecting that a train could come at any time, and check for another train on a different track after one passes.

sec07-card-f03.front: When must you wait before starting across railroad tracks even if no train is visible?
sec07-card-f03.expected_back: Do not begin crossing tracks unless the far side has enough room for the vehicle.

sec07-card-f04.front: How should a driver with a manual transmission handle gears when crossing railroad tracks?
sec07-card-f04.expected_back: With a manual transmission, select the lower gear before reaching the tracks and avoid changing gears while crossing to reduce the chance of stalling.

sec07-card-f05.front: Why must you never try to beat a train—and what vehicles ahead should you expect to stop at tracks?
sec07-card-f05.expected_back: Never race a train, and expect to stop behind vehicles legally required to stop at crossings.

sec07-card-f06.front: Where must you bring your vehicle to a stop when pulling out of an urban alley, building, or driveway?
sec07-card-f06.expected_back: In urban areas, stop before the sidewalk when leaving an alley, building, private road or driveway; without a sidewalk, stop near the street where approaching traffic is visible.

sec07-card-f07.front: Once stopped at an urban alley or driveway exit, what yielding and signaling steps follow?
sec07-card-f07.expected_back: After stopping to leave an urban alley or driveway, yield to pedestrians and all vehicles and signal the intended turn.

sec07-card-f08.front: How should you secure the transmission and brakes when parking on a hill?
sec07-card-f08.expected_back: When parking on a hill, select park and set the parking brake if necessary.

sec07-card-f09.front: What four-step sequence applies before pulling out from a parked spot on an incline?
sec07-card-f09.expected_back: Before leaving a parked uphill or downhill position, release the parking brake, signal, check approaching traffic and proceed only when safe.

sec07-card-f10.front: Which way must you angle your front tires when parked facing downhill next to a curb?
sec07-card-f10.expected_back: When parked facing downhill beside a curb, angle the front wheels toward that curb.

sec07-card-f11.front: Which way must you angle your front tires when parked facing uphill beside a curb?
sec07-card-f11.expected_back: When parked facing uphill beside a curb, angle the front wheels away from that curb.

sec07-card-f12.front: How should you turn your wheels when parking uphill or downhill on a road without a curb?
sec07-card-f12.expected_back: Without a curb, turn the wheels toward the roadside where the vehicle is parked, whether facing uphill or downhill.

sec07-card-f13.front: Which wheels go beside the curb and within how many inches when parallel parking on a two-way street?
sec07-card-f13.expected_back: On a two-way road, parallel-park with the right wheels no more than twelve inches from the curb.

sec07-card-f14.front: Which curb may you use when parking on an Illinois one-way street, and how close must you park?
sec07-card-f14.expected_back: On a one-way road, park within twelve inches of either curb and always face the direction of traffic travel.

sec07-card-f15.front: Beyond displaying disability plates or a placard, who must actually be with the vehicle to use an accessible stall?
sec07-card-f15.expected_back: Using a disability-reserved space requires qualifying plates or a placard, and the authorized holder must be present and entering or leaving the vehicle.

sec07-card-f16.front: May a driver with valid disability plates or a placard park on the diagonal stripes next to an accessible stall?
sec07-card-f16.expected_back: The striped area beside an accessible space is reserved space and cannot be parked in even by a vehicle with disability parking credentials.

sec07-card-f17.front: Which vehicles are legally allowed to occupy a designated electric-vehicle charging space?
sec07-card-f17.expected_back: A parking space designated for electric-vehicle charging may be occupied only by an electric vehicle.

sec07-card-r01.front: Where around walkways, intersections, curb-parked cars, and safety zones is stopping or double-parking banned?
sec07-card-r01.expected_back: Do not double-park or stop on a sidewalk, crosswalk, within an intersection or between a safety zone and its adjacent curb.

sec07-card-r02.front: How does Illinois treat stopping, standing, or parking in marked, buffered, or barrel-protected bike lanes?
sec07-card-r02.expected_back: Stopping, standing and parking are prohibited in marked, buffered or barrel-protected bicycle lanes.

sec07-card-r03.front: When is stopping beside or across from street construction or an obstruction illegal?
sec07-card-r03.expected_back: Do not stop beside or opposite street work or an obstruction if doing so blocks traffic.

sec07-card-r04.front: Which five elevated, enclosed, rail, or high-speed facilities ban stopping, standing, and parking?
sec07-card-r04.expected_back: Stopping, standing and parking are prohibited on bridges, overpasses, railway tracks, in highway tunnels and on controlled-access roadways.

sec07-card-r05.front: Are you allowed to stop, stand, or park between the roadways or in a crossover of a divided highway?
sec07-card-r05.expected_back: Do not stop, stand or park between the roadways of a divided highway, including a crossover.

sec07-card-r06.front: Outside town districts, what visibility, lights, and lane space are required if an emergency forces a roadway stop?
sec07-card-r06.expected_back: Outside business and residential districts, use a practical off-road stopping place rather than the paved highway; an emergency roadway stop requires two hundred feet of clear view each way, warning flashers and room for traffic to pass.

sec07-card-r07.front: How do posted no-stopping or no-parking signs relate to statewide parking bans?
sec07-card-r07.expected_back: Official no-stopping, no-standing or no-parking signs must be obeyed even though some statewide restrictions need no sign.

sec07-card-r08.front: Does sitting inside your running car make standing across a driveway or within fifteen feet of a hydrant legal?
sec07-card-r08.expected_back: Do not stand or park in front of a public or private driveway or within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant, whether the vehicle is occupied or empty.

sec07-card-r09.front: Which two locations share Illinois's twenty-foot standing-and-parking clearance rule?
sec07-card-r09.expected_back: The listed standing-and-parking clearance is twenty feet from a fire-station driveway or an intersection crosswalk.

sec07-card-r10.front: How far must standing or parked cars stay from a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal?
sec07-card-r10.expected_back: Keep standing or parked vehicles at least thirty feet from a stop sign, yield sign or traffic signal.

sec07-card-r11.front: Within how many feet of the nearest railroad rail is parking prohibited in Illinois?
sec07-card-r11.expected_back: Parking is prohibited within fifty feet of the closest railway rail.

sec07-card-r12.front: What lighting rules apply to a vehicle parked along a highway between sunset and sunrise?
sec07-card-r12.expected_back: A highway-parked vehicle needs front and rear parking lamps between sunset and sunrise unless an urban-district exception applies, and its headlights must be dimmed.

sec07-card-r13.front: What does Illinois law say about dropping objects from an overpass or elevated spot toward moving traffic?
sec07-card-r13.expected_back: Do not intentionally drop an object from an elevated place toward a moving vehicle to strike it.

sec07-card-r14.front: What is the lone situation where driving a vehicle onto a sidewalk is legal?
sec07-card-r14.expected_back: Driving on a sidewalk is prohibited except where the sidewalk forms part of a driveway.

sec07-card-r15.front: What two limits restrict how you load cargo and seated passengers inside a vehicle?
sec07-card-r15.expected_back: Do not load passengers or freight so the driver’s view is blocked, and do not carry more seated people than available safety belts.

sec07-card-r16.front: May passengers ride inside a towed house trailer while it travels on a street or highway?
sec07-card-r16.expected_back: A person may not ride inside a house trailer while it is moving on a street or highway.

sec07-card-r17.front: At what distance outside your moving vehicle does a loud sound system become illegal on an Illinois highway?
sec07-card-r17.expected_back: Do not operate or allow a vehicle sound system at a volume audible seventy-five feet or farther from the vehicle while it travels on a highway.

sec09-card-f01.front: How does alcohol affect driving skills even before reaching the legal intoxication threshold?
sec09-card-f01.expected_back: Alcohol affects sight and slows reactions, and even a small amount can raise crash risk before the legal intoxication threshold is reached.

sec09-card-f02.front: Which four bodily samples can chemical testing analyze to measure blood-alcohol concentration?
sec09-card-f02.expected_back: Blood-alcohol concentration measures alcohol through testing of breath, blood, urine or another bodily substance.

sec09-card-f03.front: At what blood-alcohol percentage is driving illegal per se, and what if impairment shows below that?
sec09-card-f03.expected_back: Driving at a blood-alcohol concentration of zero point zero eight percent or higher is illegal, and impairment can support a driving-under-the-influence conviction below that level.

sec09-card-f04.front: Which three personal factors can alter how strongly someone reacts to alcohol?
sec09-card-f04.expected_back: Food recently eaten, tolerance and other drugs can affect a person’s response to alcohol.

sec09-card-f05.front: What actually clears alcohol's effects, and do food, coffee, or cold showers speed that up?
sec09-card-f05.expected_back: Only time removes alcohol’s effects; food, coffee and showers do not accelerate its elimination.

sec09-card-f06.front: What cannabis concentration thresholds prohibit driving on Illinois highways?
sec09-card-f06.expected_back: The handbook prohibits highway driving with cannabis concentration at least five nanograms per milliliter of whole blood or ten nanograms per milliliter of another bodily substance.

sec09-card-f07.front: Does lawful medical or adult-use recreational cannabis allow driving while impaired?
sec09-card-f07.expected_back: Medical or recreational cannabis use does not permit driving while impaired.

sec09-card-f08.front: How must cannabis be packaged when transported inside a motor vehicle?
sec09-card-f08.expected_back: The handbook requires vehicle-transported cannabis to be in a sealed container resistant to odor and access by children.

sec09-card-f09.front: Who is prohibited from consuming cannabis inside a motor vehicle?
sec09-card-f09.expected_back: Neither the driver nor a passenger may use cannabis inside a motor vehicle.

sec09-card-f10.front: What tests must a stopped driver submit to when an officer reasonably suspects cannabis impairment?
sec09-card-f10.expected_back: When an officer reasonably suspects cannabis impairment during a stop, the driver must submit to field-sobriety testing, validated roadside chemical testing or both.

sec09-card-f11.front: What happens to your license if you refuse or fail required roadside cannabis testing?
sec09-card-f11.expected_back: Refusing the stated cannabis tests or failing field-sobriety or validated roadside chemical testing leads to license suspension under the handbook’s rule.

sec09-card-f12.front: What two penalties can follow cannabis-impaired driving or illegal vehicle transport for a registered patient?
sec09-card-f12.expected_back: Cannabis-impaired driving or unlawful vehicle transportation can lead to loss of driving privileges and a two-year medical-cannabis card revocation for a registered patient.

sec09-card-f13.front: Which legal medications can impair safe driving ability?
sec09-card-f13.expected_back: Many prescribed and nonprescription medicines can impair driving, including allergy, cold and pain remedies.

sec09-card-f14.front: Why is combining even a small amount of alcohol with other drugs hazardous?
sec09-card-f14.expected_back: Combining even a little alcohol with other drugs is dangerous.

sec09-card-f15.front: How long does an Illinois DUI conviction stay on your driving record, and what penalties can apply?
sec09-card-f15.expected_back: An Illinois driving-under-the-influence conviction remains permanently on the driving record, and arrest or conviction can result in lost driving privileges, registration consequences, fines or imprisonment.

sec09-card-f16.front: What chemical-testing consent do you automatically give simply by driving on Illinois roadways?
sec09-card-f16.expected_back: Driving on Illinois roads gives implied consent to specified alcohol or drug tests using breath, blood, urine or another bodily substance.

sec09-card-f17.front: When must police request alcohol or drug testing after a collision?
sec09-card-f17.expected_back: Following a crash causing injury or death, police with probable cause of impairment must request alcohol or drug testing.

sec09-card-f18.front: May a tested driver arrange extra chemical testing, and who pays for it?
sec09-card-f18.expected_back: A driver may arrange additional tests by a qualified person of the driver’s choosing at the driver’s own expense.

sec09-card-f19.front: When can a convicted impaired driver owe up to five hundred dollars for blood-testing costs?
sec09-card-f19.expected_back: A person convicted of impaired driving may owe up to five hundred dollars for blood-test costs after breath-test refusal or an officer’s belief that blood testing could reveal drugs.

sec09-card-f20.front: How long is the statutory summary suspension for failing a chemical test for alcohol, cannabis, or unlawful drugs?
sec09-card-f20.expected_back: A chemical test meeting the listed alcohol or cannabis thresholds results in a six-month summary suspension, as does detection of the specified substances from unlawful use.

sec09-card-f21.front: How long is the ordinary suspension for refusing chemical testing?
sec09-card-f21.expected_back: Refusing chemical testing ordinarily results in a one-year suspension.

sec09-card-f22.front: What prior record within five years classifies a driver as a second offender for summary suspension?
sec09-card-f22.expected_back: A qualifying summary action, out-of-state test-refusal suspension, impaired-driving supervision or impaired-driving conviction within five years makes the driver a second offender for the listed summary penalties.

sec09-card-f23.front: What summary suspension lengths hit a five-year second offender for test refusal versus test failure?
sec09-card-f23.expected_back: For a second offender under the stated five-year rule, chemical-test refusal causes a three-year suspension and a failed chemical test causes a one-year suspension.

sec09-card-f24.front: How can prosecutors use a driver's refusal to take a chemical test?
sec09-card-f24.expected_back: Refusal to take a chemical test may be used as evidence against the driver.

sec09-card-f25.front: What receipt does a validly licensed driver get at DUI arrest, and when does summary suspension begin?
sec09-card-f25.expected_back: At arrest the officer takes the license and, if it is valid, issues a temporary receipt allowing forty-five days of driving; summary suspension starts on the forty-sixth day after notice.

sec09-card-f26.front: What two steps must happen before a summary suspension actually terminates?
sec09-card-f26.expected_back: A summary suspension does not terminate until the reinstatement fee is paid and the driving record is updated.

sec09-card-f27.front: What administrative penalty follows refusing chemical testing after a crash involving serious injury or death?
sec09-card-f27.expected_back: Refusing chemical testing after involvement in a crash with serious injury or death brings a revocation of at least one year.

sec09-card-r01.front: How does a criminal DUI conviction relate to a statutory summary suspension or revocation?
sec09-card-r01.expected_back: A driving-under-the-influence conviction can be imposed in addition to a statutory summary suspension or revocation.

sec09-card-r02.front: What minimum revocation periods apply to a first DUI, a second within twenty years, and a third?
sec09-card-r02.expected_back: The general conviction table lists revocation minimums of one year for a first conviction, five years for a second within twenty years and ten years for a third.

sec09-card-r03.front: What license consequence follows a fourth or subsequent DUI conviction in Illinois?
sec09-card-r03.expected_back: A fourth or later driving-under-the-influence conviction results in lifetime revocation.

sec09-card-r04.front: What higher BAC figure or passenger age triggers enhanced DUI punishment?
sec09-card-r04.expected_back: A concentration of zero point one six percent or more, or transporting a child younger than sixteen during impaired driving, can bring enhanced punishment.

sec09-card-r05.front: What steps can restoring driving privileges after an impaired-driving revocation require?
sec09-card-r05.expected_back: Restoring privileges after impaired-driving revocation can require substance-use evaluation, rehabilitation or education, an administrative hearing, a reinstatement fee and other conditions.

sec09-card-r06.front: How long must financial-responsibility insurance remain on file after a DUI conviction?
sec09-card-r06.expected_back: A driving-under-the-influence conviction requires financial-responsibility insurance to be filed for three years.

sec09-card-r07.front: How does Illinois handle an Illinois resident's impaired-driving conviction or test refusal in another state?
sec09-card-r07.expected_back: An Illinois resident’s out-of-state impaired-driving conviction or test refusal is reported to Illinois, recorded and treated administratively as a comparable Illinois offense.

sec09-card-r08.front: What permit and vehicle device allow an eligible first-time offender to drive during summary suspension?
sec09-card-r08.expected_back: An eligible first-time offender may seek a Monitoring Device Driving Permit requiring an approved breath-alcohol ignition interlock installation for driving relief during summary suspension.

sec09-card-r09.front: Who pays for the monitoring permit, interlock installation, and monthly monitoring unless found indigent?
sec09-card-r09.expected_back: Unless found indigent, the offender pays the monitoring-permit, interlock-installation and monitoring costs.

sec09-card-r10.front: What events does the breath interlock report back to the monitoring agency?
sec09-card-r10.expected_back: The agency monitors the interlock during the permit and receives alerts about attempts to start after drinking or to tamper with the device.

sec09-card-r11.front: What may a first-time offender decline, and what crime occurs if they drive during suspension anyway?
sec09-card-r11.expected_back: A first-time offender may decline monitoring relief and refrain from driving, but driving during that suspension without participating in the program is a felony.

sec09-card-r12.front: Which crash outcomes, offense counts, or prior fatal records elevate impaired driving to Aggravated DUI?
sec09-card-r12.expected_back: Impaired driving can be aggravated when it involves a crash with injury or death, is a third or later offense or follows a qualifying history of reckless homicide or a fatal aggravated offense.

sec09-card-r13.front: Which passenger-transport roles or missing credentials also elevate impaired driving to Aggravated DUI?
sec09-card-r13.expected_back: Impaired driving can be aggravated when committed with children on a school bus, while operating a for-hire vehicle or without the required license, permit or insurance.

sec09-card-r14.front: Who is barred from drinking alcohol in a vehicle, and which four passenger vehicles are exempted?
sec09-card-r14.expected_back: Alcohol consumption in a vehicle is generally illegal for drivers and passengers, with the handbook’s exception for passengers on nonschool charter buses, motor homes, mini motor homes and limousines.

sec09-card-r15.front: What rule governs an opened alcoholic-beverage container inside a vehicle?
sec09-card-r15.expected_back: An opened alcoholic-beverage container may not be kept in the passenger compartment.

sec09-card-r16.front: How can impaired motorboat operation affect your highway driver's license?
sec09-card-r16.expected_back: Operating a motorboat under alcohol, drug or intoxicating-compound impairment is illegal, and an injury or fatal boating crash can also lead to driving-privilege loss for refusal or specified failed testing.

sec09-card-r17.front: What alcohol duty binds parents or guardians on property, vehicles, or boats they control?
sec09-card-r17.expected_back: A parent or guardian may not allow under-twenty-one drinking or fail to control access to alcohol on controlled property, including vehicles or watercraft, and resulting injury or death can bring criminal punishment.

sec09-card-r18.front: What three consequences can hit someone caught driving while suspended or revoked for DUI or serious crashes?
sec09-card-r18.expected_back: Driving while suspended or revoked for the listed impaired-driving, reckless-homicide or serious hit-and-run offenses can bring jail, a longer withdrawal period and seizure or forfeiture of the vehicle.

sec09-card-r19.front: May you drive in another state while suspended or revoked in Illinois for serious offenses?
sec09-card-r19.expected_back: An Illinois suspension or revocation for the listed serious offenses prohibits driving in every state, and an out-of-state arrest for violating it is reported to Illinois.

sec09-card-r20.front: What rule governs letting a visibly or knowingly impaired friend drive your car?
sec09-card-r20.expected_back: Do not knowingly allow an impaired person to drive your vehicle.

sec09-card-r21.front: What three penalties can follow a conviction for supplying alcohol to someone under twenty-one?
sec09-card-r21.expected_back: Conviction for supplying alcohol to someone younger than twenty-one may result in a fine, jail and license suspension.

sec09-card-r22.front: How long is the minimum license revocation for a first DUI conviction under age twenty-one?
sec09-card-r22.expected_back: For a driver younger than twenty-one, a first impaired-driving conviction brings at least two years of revocation.

sec09-card-r23.front: What minimum suspension hits a driver under twenty-one caught operating with any trace of alcohol?
sec09-card-r23.expected_back: A driver younger than twenty-one with any alcohol trace while operating a vehicle faces at least a three-month suspension.

sec09-card-r24.front: How does an underage conviction or supervision for buying, holding, or drinking alcohol affect driving privileges?
sec09-card-r24.expected_back: Under-twenty-one conviction or supervision for illegal alcohol consumption, purchase, possession or receipt as a gift causes driving-privilege loss even when the person was not driving.

sec09-card-r25.front: What education and testing can be required to get your license back after a suspension before age twenty-one?
sec09-card-r25.expected_back: A suspension occurring before age twenty-one requires successful remedial driver education and can require the full license examination before reissuance.

sec09-card-r26.front: Why does the handbook direct readers to check the current impaired-driving fact book or official website?
sec09-card-r26.expected_back: The handbook warns that impaired-driving laws change continually and directs readers to the agency’s current impaired-driving fact book or website.

sec10-card-f01.front: Where should you pull over after encountering or being involved in a crash?
sec10-card-f01.expected_back: After encountering or being involved in a crash, stop in a safe, lit public location without blocking traffic when possible.

sec10-card-f02.front: What two urgent actions are required when someone is injured in a crash?
sec10-card-f02.expected_back: Provide needed or requested help to an injured person and immediately call nine one one after a crash.

sec10-card-f03.front: Which two warning tools should you use at a crash scene to alert approaching traffic?
sec10-card-f03.expected_back: Use hazard flashers and available flares to warn other drivers at a crash.

sec10-card-f04.front: Which five contact, licensing, and vehicle details should you collect from people involved in a crash?
sec10-card-f04.expected_back: Collect involved persons’ names, addresses, telephone numbers, license numbers and plate numbers.

sec10-card-f05.front: What happens if you miss or fail to pay a minor-violation ticket's initial court date?
sec10-card-f05.expected_back: The minor-violation ticket gives the court date; nonpayment or absence can lead to another date at least thirty days later and a clerk’s notice through the available contact system.

sec10-card-f06.front: What is the consequence of missing that second scheduled court date?
sec10-card-f06.expected_back: Missing the second court date results in a conviction entered without the driver present and reported to the licensing agency like other convictions.

sec10-card-f07.front: How does Illinois treat failure-to-appear suspensions imposed from January twenty-twenty through December twenty-twenty-four?
sec10-card-f07.expected_back: The handbook says failure-to-appear suspensions imposed from January first, two thousand twenty through December thirty-first, two thousand twenty-four are cleared.

sec10-card-f08.front: What two steps are required to lift a failure-to-appear suspension imposed before January first, two thousand twenty?
sec10-card-f08.expected_back: For a failure-to-appear suspension imposed before January first, two thousand twenty, the handbook requires court resolution of the ticket and payment of a reinstatement fee before the suspension ends.

sec10-card-f09.front: Who must accompany a driver younger than eighteen to a mandatory traffic court appearance?
sec10-card-f09.expected_back: A required court appearance by someone younger than eighteen must include a parent or guardian.

sec10-card-f10.front: How may an Illinois driver handle a citation in another compact state, and what if they break promised compliance?
sec10-card-f10.expected_back: For a ticket in another compact-member state, an Illinois driver may contest it there, pay it or promise compliance and handle it from home; breaking that promise may suspend the Illinois license.

sec10-card-f11.front: When does an insured crash require an official report regardless of fault?
sec10-card-f11.expected_back: A crash involving death, injury or property damage above fifteen hundred dollars requires a report regardless of who caused it.

sec10-card-f12.front: What lower property-damage threshold triggers a mandatory crash report when any vehicle is uninsured?
sec10-card-f12.expected_back: If any involved vehicle lacks insurance, property damage exceeding five hundred dollars requires a crash report.

sec10-card-f13.front: When does a crash involving a school bus require an official report?
sec10-card-f13.expected_back: A crash involving a school bus requires a report for property damage or personal injury.

sec10-card-f14.front: When must a crash within fifty feet of a school bus be reported even if the bus wasn't hit?
sec10-card-f14.expected_back: A crash within fifty feet of a school bus must be reported when it injures or kills someone waiting to board or someone who has just left the bus.

sec10-card-r01.front: How quickly must you notify police and report a crash, and where if no officer comes?
sec10-card-r01.expected_back: Notify police immediately after a crash and make the report within thirty minutes; if no officer attends, report at the nearest police station promptly, or notify the sheriff or state police in a rural area.

sec10-card-r02.front: Who must file the crash report when the driver is physically unable and a passenger was riding?
sec10-card-r02.expected_back: When the driver cannot report a crash and a passenger is present, the passenger must make the report.

sec10-card-r03.front: What maximum fine and jail sentence can follow failing to report a vehicle crash?
sec10-card-r03.expected_back: Failure to report a vehicle crash can bring a fine up to twenty-five hundred dollars and imprisonment up to one year.

sec10-card-r04.front: How do license sanctions differ for leaving an injury or fatal crash versus damage over one thousand dollars?
sec10-card-r04.expected_back: Leaving a crash scene can result in criminal charges; an injury or fatality requires license revocation, while damage above one thousand dollars brings suspension.

sec10-card-r05.front: Where must you stop after hitting unattended property, and what four details go on your note if no owner is found?
sec10-card-r05.expected_back: After damaging an unattended vehicle or other property, stop clear of traffic and, if the owner cannot be found, leave your name, address, telephone number and plate number.

sec10-card-r06.front: What two official steps are still required after leaving a note on damaged unattended property?
sec10-card-r06.expected_back: A crash damaging unattended property still requires notifying police and completing required crash reports.

sec10-card-r07.front: What must an at-fault uninsured driver post after a crash, and who sets the amount?
sec10-card-r07.expected_back: An uninsured driver responsible for a crash causing injury, death or damage must post security to cover the injured party’s damages, with the state transportation department determining its amount.

sec10-card-r08.front: Whose privileges can be suspended if required uninsured-crash security is not posted?
sec10-card-r08.expected_back: Failing to post required crash security can suspend the driver’s license until the lawsuit is settled and can also suspend the vehicle owner’s registration or plates.

sec10-card-r09.front: How long must financial-responsibility insurance be maintained to end a safety-responsibility suspension?
sec10-card-r09.expected_back: The stated driver or registration suspension continues until financial-responsibility proof is supplied and insurance is maintained for three years from the first filing.

sec10-card-r10.front: What suspension length, fee, and permit rule hit a mandatory-insurance conviction?
sec10-card-r10.expected_back: A mandatory-insurance conviction brings at least three months of lost driving privileges, a one-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee and no driving permit.

sec10-card-r11.front: Which four judgment, crash, supervision, or conviction histories require financial-responsibility proof?
sec10-card-r11.expected_back: Financial-responsibility proof is required for an unpaid crash judgment, an uninsured-crash safety-responsibility suspension, insurance-violation court supervision or at least three mandatory-insurance convictions.

sec10-card-r12.front: Which three forms can financial-responsibility proof take, and how does an insurance certificate reach the state?
sec10-card-r12.expected_back: Proof may take the form of an insurance certificate, bond or deposited securities, and the insurer files the required certificate directly with the agency.

sec10-card-r13.front: What happens if required monitored financial-responsibility insurance is canceled or not renewed?
sec10-card-r13.expected_back: The agency monitors required insurance, and cancellation or failure to renew results in license suspension.

sec10-card-r14.front: At what age may completing an eight-hour defensive-driving course qualify a driver for an insurance discount?
sec10-card-r14.expected_back: A driver aged fifty-five or older may qualify for a liability-insurance reduction after an eight-hour defensive-driving course and should ask the insurer about the reduction amount.

sec11-card-f01.front: How long can certain Illinois revocations, suspensions, denials, and cancellations stay on your driving record?
sec11-card-f01.expected_back: Some revocations, suspensions, denials and cancellations can remain permanently recorded in a person’s driving history.

sec11-card-f02.front: What two penalties apply if you get caught driving while your Illinois license is suspended or revoked?
sec11-card-f02.expected_back: Driving during suspension or revocation extends the withdrawal period and may result in imprisonment.

sec11-card-f03.front: How does license revocation affect your driving privileges, and when is the earliest standard window to reapply?
sec11-card-f03.expected_back: Revocation withdraws driving privileges indefinitely; reapplication may become possible after at least one year unless a different rule applies.

sec11-card-f04.front: What happens to your license if you are convicted of a moving violation that causes a fatal crash?
sec11-card-f04.expected_back: A moving-violation conviction causing a fatal crash results in immediate license revocation.

sec11-card-f05.front: Beyond revoking a repeat offender's driver's license, what action can the state also take on their vehicle?
sec11-card-f05.expected_back: The agency can revoke a repeat traffic offender’s license and may suspend vehicle registration during a revocation.

sec11-card-f06.front: What license action applies to aggravated impaired driving or driving under alcohol, cannabis, or other drugs?
sec11-card-f06.expected_back: Aggravated impaired driving and driving under alcohol, cannabis or other drug impairment are among the listed revocation grounds.

sec11-card-f07.front: How does Illinois penalize a driver's license for aggravated police flight, aggravated reckless driving, or street racing?
sec11-card-f07.expected_back: Aggravated flight from police, aggravated reckless driving and illegal drag or street racing are listed revocation grounds.

sec11-card-f08.front: What license consequence follows auto or parts theft, or using a vehicle to commit a felony?
sec11-card-f08.expected_back: Motor-vehicle or vehicle-parts theft and using a vehicle to commit a felony are listed grounds for revocation.

sec11-card-f09.front: What license penalty can result from making, selling, equipping, or helping someone use an unauthorized fake ID or license?
sec11-card-f09.expected_back: Making, selling, possessing production equipment for or helping use an unauthorized nongovernmental identification card or license can lead to revocation.

sec11-card-f10.front: What license action applies to lying to the state agency, vehicle-linked gang offenses, or fleeing an injury crash?
sec11-card-f10.expected_back: Gang-related offenses involving a vehicle or Illinois license, false information to the agency and leaving an injury or fatal crash scene are listed revocation grounds.

sec11-card-f11.front: Can reckless conduct with a vehicle that injures or endangers people trigger license revocation?
sec11-card-f11.expected_back: Reckless vehicle conduct causing injury or danger is a listed ground for revocation.

sec11-card-f12.front: How many reckless-driving convictions in twelve months—or what degree of crash harm—triggers license revocation?
sec11-card-f12.expected_back: Three reckless-driving convictions in twelve months, or driving causing great bodily harm, permanent disability or disfigurement, are listed revocation grounds.

sec11-card-f13.front: Which two deadly scenarios fall under Illinois's reckless-homicide revocation category?
sec11-card-f13.expected_back: Reckless driving causing death, or a fatal crash while driving under an aggravated-impaired-driving suspension or revocation, is included in the reckless-homicide revocation listing.

sec11-card-f14.front: What license action follows a conviction for illegally passing a school bus and causing a fatal crash?
sec11-card-f14.expected_back: A conviction for passing a school bus and causing a fatal crash is listed as a revocation ground.

sec11-card-f15.front: How does a suspension differ from revocation, and what is required to drive again once the fixed term ends?
sec11-card-f15.expected_back: Suspension temporarily withdraws driving privileges; restoration after a fixed term requires the reinstatement fee and any other applicable conditions.

sec11-card-f16.front: How many unpaid automated red-light or speed-camera tickets in a municipality can trigger a license suspension?
sec11-card-f16.expected_back: Five or more unpaid automated red-light or speeding violations in a municipality are listed as grounds for suspension.

sec11-card-f17.front: What license action can follow if you fail to slow down or move over in a work zone and cause damage or injury?
sec11-card-f17.expected_back: Failing to slow or change lanes in road work and causing damage or injury can lead to suspension.

sec11-card-f18.front: How can a court ruling over a child-visitation dispute affect your Illinois driver's license?
sec11-card-f18.expected_back: A court order finding violation of a child-visitation order can trigger suspension.

sec11-card-f19.front: Does refusing a post-arrest alcohol or drug test outside Illinois still affect your Illinois driver's license?
sec11-card-f19.expected_back: Refusing alcohol or drug chemical testing after an impaired-driving arrest in Illinois or another state is a listed suspension ground.

sec11-card-f20.front: What happens to your license if you commit a drug or sex offense while operating or controlling a car?
sec11-card-f20.expected_back: Committing a drug or sex offense while operating or directly controlling a car is listed as a suspension ground.

sec11-card-f21.front: Which missed traffic-court appearance date cutoff remains listed as an Illinois suspension ground?
sec11-card-f21.expected_back: Failure to appear for a traffic citation before January first, two thousand twenty is a listed suspension ground.

sec11-card-f22.front: How many convictions for ignoring an active railroad-crossing warning signal trigger a license suspension?
sec11-card-f22.expected_back: A second conviction for ignoring a railroad-crossing signal is listed as a suspension ground.

sec11-card-f23.front: Which two authorities can direct Illinois to suspend a driver's license over unpaid child support?
sec11-card-f23.expected_back: A child-support court order or direction from the responsible state department can suspend a license for nonpayment.

sec11-card-f24.front: What license penalty applies when failing to slow down and move over for a stopped emergency vehicle causes damage or injury?
sec11-card-f24.expected_back: Failing to slow and move away from a stationary emergency vehicle and causing property damage or injury can lead to suspension.

sec11-card-f25.front: How does Illinois penalize borrowing, altering, lending out a license, or helping with a fraudulent application?
sec11-card-f25.expected_back: Using an altered or borrowed credential, lending a credential for misuse or submitting or facilitating a fraudulent application can lead to suspension.

sec11-card-r01.front: Can an underage vehicle occupant face license suspension for illegally possessing, buying, or drinking alcohol?
sec11-card-r01.expected_back: Illegal alcohol possession, consumption, purchase or receipt by an under-twenty-one vehicle occupant is a listed suspension ground.

sec11-card-r02.front: How do illegal alcohol-transportation suspension rules compare between drivers twenty-one and older versus drivers under twenty-one?
sec11-card-r02.expected_back: For a person at least twenty-one, two illegal-alcohol-transportation offenses in twelve months can cause suspension; illegal transportation by someone younger than twenty-one is also listed.

sec11-card-r03.front: When can failing to file required financial-responsibility insurance suspend your Illinois license?
sec11-card-r03.expected_back: Failure to file required financial-responsibility insurance after insurance-violation supervision or at least three uninsured-driving tickets can cause suspension.

sec11-card-r04.front: Which two uninsured-driving situations are listed grounds for suspending your Illinois license?
sec11-card-r04.expected_back: Driving without mandatory insurance and being an uninsured at-fault crash driver owing damages are listed suspension grounds.

sec11-card-r05.front: Accumulating how many unpaid railroad-crossing violations can suspend your driver's license?
sec11-card-r05.expected_back: Five or more unpaid railway-crossing violations are listed as a suspension ground.

sec11-card-r06.front: Which two school-bus violations can get your Illinois driver's license suspended?
sec11-card-r06.expected_back: Failing to stop for a school bus loading or unloading children, or leaving at least five camera-recorded stopped-bus yielding violations unpaid, can cause suspension.

sec11-card-r07.front: When does a repeat work-zone speeding ticket trigger license suspension in Illinois?
sec11-card-r07.expected_back: A second work-zone speeding violation within two years of the prior violation, when workers are present, is a listed suspension ground.

sec11-card-r08.front: What can happen to your license if you refuse or neglect to file a required crash report?
sec11-card-r08.expected_back: Refusing or neglecting to report a traffic crash is a listed suspension ground.

sec11-card-r09.front: How many moving-violation convictions trigger license suspension for adults versus drivers arrested under age twenty-one?
sec11-card-r09.expected_back: The listed traffic-conviction suspension threshold is three within twelve months, or two within twenty-four months when the driver was younger than twenty-one at arrest.

sec11-card-r10.front: Beyond a steep fine, what license action can result from illegally parking in a disability-reserved stall?
sec11-card-r10.expected_back: Unauthorized parking in a disability-reserved space is a listed suspension ground.

sec11-card-r11.front: What blood alcohol range triggers an Illinois zero-tolerance suspension for a driver younger than twenty-one?
sec11-card-r11.expected_back: For someone younger than twenty-one, an alcohol concentration above zero but below zero point zero eight is listed as a zero-tolerance suspension ground.

sec11-card-r12.front: Why does the state cancel a license or permit, and when can the holder apply again?
sec11-card-r12.expected_back: Cancellation formally ends a license or permit because of a defect, error or loss of entitlement; reapplication is allowed only after its conditions have been satisfied.

sec11-card-r13.front: What happens if the state orders you to take a driver reexamination and you skip or fail it?
sec11-card-r13.expected_back: Missing or failing a required reexamination can lead to cancellation.

sec11-card-r14.front: Which two application or eligibility problems are listed grounds for canceling an Illinois credential?
sec11-card-r14.expected_back: Fraud in a license or identification application and ineligibility for the credential are listed cancellation grounds.

sec11-card-r15.front: What does a license denial block, and what age group faces denial for specified traffic convictions?
sec11-card-r15.expected_back: Denial temporarily prevents applying for a license and sometimes a permit, and can be entered for specified convictions before age eighteen.

sec11-card-r16.front: How does a mandatory-revocation conviction affect a minor's ability to apply for a permit or license?
sec11-card-r16.expected_back: A minor’s conviction for a mandatory-revocation offense can prevent both license and permit applications until the eighteenth birthday.

sec11-card-r17.front: If a minor gets a denial for driving without a valid credential, what happens to license eligibility versus permit privileges?
sec11-card-r17.memory_hook: No license til eighteen, permit stays
sec11-card-r17.expected_back: For a minor’s driving-without-valid-credential denial, a license cannot be requested until eighteen, but a permit remains available and an existing license is reduced to permit privileges.

sec11-card-r18.front: How long does a minor's denial for a serious moving violation last, and how does it treat permit privileges?
sec11-card-r18.expected_back: A minor’s serious-moving-violation denial lasts nine months or until eighteen, whichever comes first, and restricts license applications while allowing a permit or reducing an existing license to permit privileges.

sec11-card-r19.front: Can a pending charge from a serious-injury or fatal crash block license issuance or renewal even when zero alcohol was involved?
sec11-card-r19.expected_back: A charge after a crash seriously injuring or killing another person may cause denial of license issuance or renewal even without alcohol involvement.

sec11-card-r20.front: What travel limits and minimum age apply to an Illinois restricted driving permit?
sec11-card-r20.expected_back: A restricted permit limits driving to approved times and routes for listed work, education, child transport, medical care or substance-treatment purposes and cannot be issued below sixteen.

sec11-card-r21.front: What device and compliance rules govern a monitoring permit for an eligible first-time impaired-driving offender?
sec11-card-r21.expected_back: A monitoring permit may let an eligible first impaired-driving offender drive an interlock-equipped vehicle during summary suspension, provided the driver avoids alcohol before driving and does not tamper with the unit.

sec11-card-r22.front: What is the minimum age to qualify for an Illinois monitoring-device driving permit?
sec11-card-r22.expected_back: A monitoring-device permit cannot be issued to an applicant younger than eighteen.

sec11-card-r23.front: When can an occupational driving permit be used, and which group of drivers is excluded from it?
sec11-card-r23.expected_back: An occupational permit can allow job-related driving after a professional driver’s three-moving-violation suspension, but it does not apply to commercial drivers.

sec11-card-r24.front: Who can qualify for an Illinois probationary license, and what program goes along with it?
sec11-card-r24.expected_back: A probationary license may allow a driver at least twenty-one to drive during a suspension for three moving violations within twelve months in conjunction with driver-improvement participation.

sec11-card-r25.front: What authorization is required before a family-financial-responsibility driving permit can be issued?
sec11-card-r25.expected_back: A family-financial-responsibility permit may allow driving after child-support or visitation-abuse suspension only following a circuit judge’s order or direction from the responsible state department.

sec12-card-f01.front: What are the three main categories of road signs, and what two visual cues distinguish them?
sec12-card-f01.expected_back: Road signs include regulatory, warning and guide categories, distinguished by shapes and colors, and the written examination asks applicants to identify them.

sec12-card-f02.front: Where in exact fallback order must you come to a full stop at an eight-sided red sign before yielding?
sec12-card-f02.expected_back: A red sign with eight sides requires a full stop at the line, otherwise before the crosswalk or, if neither exists, before the intersection, followed by yielding to pedestrians and approaching traffic.

sec12-card-f03.front: How must you obey a portable or temporary stop sign set up by road authorities?
sec12-card-f03.expected_back: Treat a temporary stop sign erected by highway authorities like a permanent stop sign.

sec12-card-f04.front: When a crossing guard or work-zone flagger holds up a stop paddle, when may you start moving again?
sec12-card-f04.expected_back: For a handheld stop sign, remain stopped until the authorized crossing guard or work-zone flagger indicates it is safe to go.

sec12-card-f05.front: What shape and colors identify a yield sign, and who gets priority when you face one?
sec12-card-f05.expected_back: The red-and-white three-sided yield sign requires letting vehicles and pedestrians proceed first.

sec12-card-f06.front: What shape, color, and markings identify an advance railroad-crossing warning sign?
sec12-card-f06.expected_back: A round yellow railway-warning sign uses a black crossed symbol and railway letters to warn that tracks cross the road ahead.

sec12-card-f07.front: How far before rural tracks can a round railroad warning stand, and what four actions should follow?
sec12-card-f07.expected_back: A rural railway advance-warning sign can stand as far as seven hundred fifty feet before the crossing; slow, look, listen through an open window and stop for an approaching train.

sec12-card-f08.front: Which three background colors can appear on diamond warning signs, and how should you respond?
sec12-card-f08.expected_back: A diamond warning sign can be yellow, yellow-green or orange with black text or symbols and calls for slower, careful driving near possible hazards.

sec12-card-f09.front: What unique five-sided sign shape and color scheme alerts drivers to a school zone or school crossing?
sec12-card-f09.expected_back: A five-sided yellow or yellow-green sign with black children symbols identifies a school zone or school crossing.

sec12-card-f10.front: How do you tell an advance school-zone sign apart from a sign marking the exact school crosswalk?
sec12-card-f10.expected_back: A school sign depicting children with a downward arrow marks the crossing itself, while the children symbol without that arrow warns of a nearby school.

sec12-card-f11.front: Where on the roadway is a yellow three-sided no-passing pennant mounted, and what does it mark?
sec12-card-f11.expected_back: A yellow, black-lettered three-sided no-passing sign stands on the left of a two-lane two-way road where the no-passing area begins.

sec12-card-f12.front: Which two broad sign functions can square and rectangular road signs serve?
sec12-card-f12.expected_back: Square and rectangular shapes can serve either regulatory or guide purposes.

sec12-card-f13.front: What common meaning connects red regulatory signs like stop, yield, do-not-enter, and wrong-way?
sec12-card-f13.expected_back: Red regulatory signs such as stop, yield, wrong-way and do-not-enter signs must be obeyed.

sec12-card-f14.front: What two roles do black-and-white road signs fill on Illinois streets and highways?
sec12-card-f14.expected_back: Black-and-white signs can be regulatory controls or route markers.

sec12-card-f15.front: What general message does a standard yellow background communicate on a road sign?
sec12-card-f15.expected_back: Yellow warning signs identify road conditions or dangers ahead.

sec12-card-f16.front: What specific types of people-focused crossings and zones use fluorescent yellow-green warning signs?
sec12-card-f16.expected_back: Yellow-green warnings can identify pedestrian and bicycle crossings, playgrounds, school-bus stops and school zones.

sec12-card-f17.front: What type of temporary roadside hazard does an orange sign background warn you about?
sec12-card-f17.expected_back: Orange usually warns of construction or maintenance dangers along a road.

sec12-card-f18.front: What three types of travel navigation details appear on green highway guide signs?
sec12-card-f18.expected_back: Green guide signs provide location, direction and distance information.

sec12-card-f19.front: What kind of information do blue highway guide signs point drivers toward?
sec12-card-f19.expected_back: Blue guide signs identify services along the road.

sec12-card-r01.front: What destinations do brown-background road signs direct travelers toward?
sec12-card-r01.expected_back: Brown signs identify parks and recreation.

sec12-card-r02.front: When highway responders post fluorescent pink warning signs, what kind of situation lies ahead?
sec12-card-r02.expected_back: Pink signs may warn of unplanned incidents such as crashes or natural disasters.

sec12-card-r03.front: How does a regulatory sign differ legally from an advisory or guide sign?
sec12-card-r03.expected_back: A regulatory sign gives a direction that drivers must obey.

sec12-card-r04.front: How does right-of-way order work after stopping at an all-way stop intersection?
sec12-card-r04.expected_back: At an all-way stop, every approach stops and the first driver stopped proceeds first while the others wait their turns.

sec12-card-r05.front: When must a yield sign be treated as a full stop?
sec12-card-r05.expected_back: Approaching a yield sign requires slowing to a safe speed and stopping when necessary before giving way to vehicles and pedestrians.

sec12-card-r06.front: What does a square red-and-white Do Not Enter sign prohibit, and where is it critically placed?
sec12-card-r06.expected_back: A do-not-enter sign forbids entering the indicated road or ramp, including a wrong-direction expressway entrance.

sec12-card-r07.front: What should you prepare to do when you pass a Speed Zone Ahead sign?
sec12-card-r07.expected_back: A speed-zone-ahead sign warns that a change of speed may soon be required.

sec12-card-r08.front: When is driving slower than a posted freeway minimum speed limit legally allowed?
sec12-card-r08.expected_back: Posted freeway limits can specify minimum and maximum speeds, and traveling below the minimum is unlawful unless safety requires it.

sec12-card-r09.front: What urgent mistake does a red rectangular Wrong Way sign tell you that you have made?
sec12-card-r09.expected_back: A wrong-way sign warns that the vehicle is traveling against the permitted direction, such as after entering a ramp or one-way road incorrectly.

sec12-card-r10.front: What universal symbol inside a regulatory sign tells you the pictured maneuver or vehicle is banned?
sec12-card-r10.expected_back: A red circle crossed diagonally from upper left to lower right means the depicted action is forbidden.

sec12-card-r11.front: Why do paved crossovers in highway medians carry No U-Turn signs for everyday drivers?
sec12-card-r11.expected_back: A no-U-turn restriction at a divided-road opening reserves that crossing for authorized vehicles such as police, emergency or maintenance vehicles.

sec12-card-r12.front: What do No Right Turn and No Left Turn symbol signs forbid at an intersection or driveway?
sec12-card-r12.expected_back: A no-right-turn or no-left-turn sign prohibits turning in its indicated direction.

sec12-card-r13.front: How must you travel when entering or driving along a street posted with One Way arrow signs?
sec12-card-r13.expected_back: On a one-way street or driveway, travel only in the direction indicated by the sign’s arrow.

sec12-card-r14.front: What roadway feature and pavement markings match an overhead or roadside two-way left-turn lane sign?
sec12-card-r14.expected_back: A two-way-left-turn-lane sign identifies a shared center turn lane marked with yellow lines and white arrows.

sec12-card-r15.front: Which two normally legal red-light turns are both blocked when a No Turn on Red sign is posted?
sec12-card-r15.expected_back: A no-turn-on-red sign prohibits a right turn on red and the otherwise permitted one-way-to-one-way left turn on red.

sec12-card-r16.front: What layout ahead does an Approaching Divided Highway sign alert cross-street drivers to expect?
sec12-card-r16.expected_back: An approaching-divided-highway sign warns that a median separates opposing directions on the road being crossed or entered.

sec12-card-r17.front: How must you steer past a traffic island, median nose, or center obstacle marked with a Keep Right sign?
sec12-card-r17.expected_back: At an island, median or central obstruction, a keep-right sign requires using the side identified by its arrow.

sec12-card-r18.front: Who must move into the right lane when a Slower Traffic Keep Right sign is posted?
sec12-card-r18.expected_back: A slower-traffic-keep-right sign directs vehicles moving below the normal traffic speed to the right lane on the multilane road.

sec13-card-f01.front: Why do certain signalized intersections post a Stop Here on Red sign?
sec13-card-f01.expected_back: A stop-here-on-red sign identifies the stopping location at a signal-controlled intersection when that location would otherwise be unclear.

sec13-card-f02.front: What does a Road Closed sign tell every approaching driver?
sec13-card-f02.expected_back: A road-closed sign means the road is closed to all traffic and cannot be used to continue the trip.

sec13-card-f03.front: What maneuver does a rectangular Do Not Pass sign forbid, and what pavement striping often pairs with it?
sec13-card-f03.expected_back: A do-not-pass sign prohibits overtaking and can accompany yellow no-passing pavement lines on a two-way two-lane road.

sec13-card-f04.front: What does a Pass With Care sign mark, and does it guarantee you can overtake right away?
sec13-card-f04.expected_back: A pass-with-care sign marks the end of a no-passing zone but permits passing only when it is safe.

sec13-card-f05.front: How are dedicated bicycle lanes striped along a block, near an intersection corner, and for extra visibility?
sec13-card-f05.expected_back: A bicycle lane is marked by a solid white boundary changing to a dotted line before the corner, and it may be painted bright green for visibility.

sec13-card-f06.front: What shape do most hazard warning signs use, and how do yellow, orange, and yellow-green split up duties?
sec13-card-f06.expected_back: Warning signs usually use a diamond shape for hazards or special conditions; ordinary warnings are commonly yellow, work warnings orange and some school or crossing warnings yellow-green.

sec13-card-f07.front: Why should you scan both sides of the street when passing a pedestrian crosswalk warning sign?
sec13-card-f07.expected_back: A crosswalk warning calls for checking both roadsides because crossings can occur away from intersections.

sec13-card-f08.front: What purpose does a yellow flashing light mounted with a pedestrian crossing sign serve?
sec13-card-f08.expected_back: A yellow flashing beacon on a crossing sign helps alert drivers to the crosswalk and possible pedestrians.

sec13-card-f09.front: What actions do school warning signs call for, and who may direct traffic at the crosswalk?
sec13-card-f09.expected_back: School signs call for watching for children, slowing and stopping when needed; authorized crossing guards or police may supervise the crossing.

sec13-card-f10.front: Under what conditions or posted cues do Illinois reduced school-zone speed signs take effect?
sec13-card-f10.expected_back: The handbook’s reduced-school-speed signs may apply when children are present on school days, when nearby children create a hazard or when a warning light flashes, with posted hours potentially varying.

sec13-card-f11.front: How should you react to Stop Ahead, Yield Ahead, or Signal Ahead diamonds when you cannot see the intersection yet?
sec13-card-f11.expected_back: Stop-ahead, yield-ahead and signal-ahead warnings require beginning to slow even when the actual control is not yet visible.

sec13-card-f12.front: Why do rural highways and fast roads place advance warning signs much farther ahead of intersections?
sec13-card-f12.expected_back: High-speed roads use advance warnings because slowing or stopping requires more distance.

sec13-card-f13.front: What road situations ahead do crossroad, side-road, and T-junction warning diamonds alert you to?
sec13-card-f13.expected_back: Intersection-warning signs identify crossings or junctions where traffic may enter or a turn may be needed.

sec13-card-f14.front: What two pieces of guidance do a curve-arrow diamond and its small square plaque underneath give you?
sec13-card-f14.expected_back: The arrow on a turn or curve warning describes the approaching road direction, and an additional small panel may show the maximum safe speed.

sec13-card-f15.front: What does a yellow Exit speed sign posted along a highway off-ramp tell you?
sec13-card-f15.expected_back: An exit-ramp speed sign identifies the ramp’s maximum safe driving speed.

sec13-card-f16.front: Why must you reduce speed when passing a Slippery When Wet warning sign in rain?
sec13-card-f16.expected_back: A slippery-pavement warning calls for slowing because wet pavement can cause lost control and lengthen stopping distance.

sec13-card-f17.front: When should you slow down after seeing a truck-on-hill downgrade warning sign, and why?
sec13-card-f17.expected_back: A downgrade sign warns of a potentially long, steep or curving descent, so reduce speed before starting downhill.

sec13-card-f18.front: What change in roadway width does a Narrow Bridge diamond warn you to expect ahead?
sec13-card-f18.expected_back: A narrow-bridge warning identifies an approaching bridge with a narrower road surface.

sec13-card-f19.front: What does a lane-reduction warning tell you is happening ahead, and what two roles must drivers prepare for?
sec13-card-f19.expected_back: A lane-reduction warning indicates fewer lanes ahead, temporarily or permanently, requiring preparation to change lanes or admit merging vehicles.

sec13-card-f20.front: When traffic is light approaching a lane drop, when does Illinois advise moving into the continuing lane?
sec13-card-f20.expected_back: When traffic is light near a lane reduction, merge into the open lane early.

sec13-card-r01.front: How should drivers use both lanes when traffic backs up heavily approaching a lane reduction?
sec13-card-r01.expected_back: In congestion near a lane reduction, use both lanes to the merge point and alternate entries there, a method called zipper merging.

sec13-card-r02.front: What specific pavement change ahead does a Road Narrows warning sign indicate?
sec13-card-r02.expected_back: A road-narrows sign warns that a two-lane road becomes narrower abruptly.

sec13-card-r03.front: Which side of a two-lane, two-way highway holds the yellow No Passing Zone pennant?
sec13-card-r03.expected_back: The no-passing pennant appears on the road’s left where a two-lane two-way no-passing zone starts.

sec13-card-r04.front: What happens ahead at a Merge warning diamond, and how should drivers in both streams respond?
sec13-card-r04.expected_back: A merge warning means same-direction lanes will become one, so prepare either to change lanes or to allow another vehicle into the lane.

sec13-card-r05.front: How does the Illinois handbook advise an expressway driver to help a vehicle entering from an on-ramp?
sec13-card-r05.expected_back: The handbook advises an expressway driver to slow enough to let a ramp vehicle merge.

sec13-card-r06.front: Which two kinds of road-alignment hazards can a horizontal arrow or chevron change-in-direction board mark?
sec13-card-r06.expected_back: A change-in-direction warning can mark a sharp curve or a narrowing approach such as a narrow bridge.

sec13-card-r07.front: How does a divided highway separate opposing lanes, and where are Divided Highway diamond warnings placed?
sec13-card-r07.expected_back: A divided road uses a center strip to separate opposing traffic, with warnings before its beginning and before its end.

sec13-card-r08.front: What transition is happening when you pass a yellow diamond showing opposing up-and-down arrows?
sec13-card-r08.expected_back: A two-way-roadway warning indicates departure from a divided roadway toward a highway carrying opposing traffic.

sec13-card-r09.front: What four adjustments should you make as soon as you spot an orange Workers Ahead diamond?
sec13-card-r09.expected_back: Workers-ahead signs provide advance notice to adjust speed, follow the posted work limit, stay alert and leave room beside barriers.

sec13-card-r10.front: What two jobs do orange cones, barrels, and barricades perform inside a construction zone?
sec13-card-r10.expected_back: Cones, drums and barricades mark a path through construction or maintenance areas and warn of hazards.

sec13-card-r11.front: Why are steady or flashing lights mounted atop work-zone barrels and barricades?
sec13-card-r11.expected_back: Warning lights make drums and barriers easier to notice at night.

sec13-card-r12.front: What do large illuminated arrow boards tell approaching drivers in a work zone?
sec13-card-r12.expected_back: Arrow boards warn of an upcoming closure or work-zone caution and show the direction to move or merge.

sec13-card-r13.front: How must you respond when you pass an orange Flagger Ahead symbol or text sign?
sec13-card-r13.expected_back: A flagger warning calls for slowing, careful approach and compliance with the flagger’s instructions, including a required stop when signaled.

sec13-card-r14.front: What kind of live updates appear on portable electronic highway message boards, and how should you treat them?
sec13-card-r14.expected_back: Portable electronic message signs give current road information such as stopped traffic, closures, delays, detours or a merging instruction, and drivers should follow their messages.

sec13-card-r15.front: How should you react upon spotting an orange-and-red triangle on the back of a slow-moving vehicle?
sec13-card-r15.expected_back: A slow-moving-vehicle sign calls for reduced speed and passing only when both safe and lawful.

sec13-card-r16.front: What navigation details do guide signs provide, and how do their shapes vary?
sec13-card-r16.expected_back: Guide signs identify location, road and route toward a destination; most are rectangular, while some route markers have different shapes.

sec13-card-r17.front: How do numbered route shields and their small helper plaques guide drivers along highways?
sec13-card-r17.expected_back: Route markers, alone or with supplementary panels, direct travelers to specific roads using markings that vary by route type.

sec13-card-r18.front: What three visual elements on hazardous-materials placards identify dangerous cargo on trucks or containers?
sec13-card-r18.expected_back: Hazardous-materials placards on transport vehicles, packages or containers use text, color and symbols to identify the presence and type of a hazard.

sec13-card-r19.front: What should you do if you encounter a crash involving a truck displaying hazardous-materials placards?
sec13-card-r19.expected_back: At a crash involving a placarded hazardous-materials vehicle, follow responders’ evacuation instructions; without responders present, avoid the area and report it from a safe location.

sec13-card-r20.front: Why should you get medical care if you feel sick hours after being near a hazardous-materials incident?
sec13-card-r20.expected_back: Toxic-exposure symptoms can be delayed, and the handbook directs anyone feeling ill to seek medical help.

sec14-card-f01.front: Who can legally override traffic signals and markings, and what shortcut around a red light is illegal?
sec14-card-f01.expected_back: Obey signals and roadway markings unless a police or traffic-control officer directs otherwise, and never leave the road to evade a signal.

sec14-card-f02.front: In what exact position order do red, yellow, and green lenses appear on vertical and horizontal traffic lights?
sec14-card-f02.expected_back: A typical three-color traffic signal orders red, yellow and green from top to bottom or left to right.

sec14-card-f03.front: How must drivers treat a dark or nonworking intersection traffic light when no officer is directing traffic?
sec14-card-f03.expected_back: A nonworking intersection signal requires an all-way stop, then observation and yielding before entry, unless police direct another action.

sec14-card-f04.front: Where must you stop at a steady red light, and what two things are required before going straight?
sec14-card-f04.expected_back: At a red signal, stop before the marked line, otherwise before the crosswalk or intersection, and wait for green and a clear intersection unless making a permitted red-light turn.

sec14-card-f05.front: What must you do first—and what must be absent—before turning right at a steady red signal?
sec14-card-f05.expected_back: After a full stop and yielding to pedestrians and approaching traffic, a right turn on red is allowed unless a sign prohibits it.

sec14-card-f06.front: Under what specific street layout is a left turn on a steady red light permitted in Illinois?
