sec14-card-f06.expected_back: A left turn on red is allowed from a one-way street onto a one-way street carrying traffic leftward after stopping and yielding.

sec14-card-f07.front: What transition does a steady yellow traffic light announce, and what entry rule applies when red illuminates?
sec14-card-f07.expected_back: A steady yellow warns that green is changing to red, and the driver must not enter once red appears.

sec14-card-f08.front: Who still has the right-of-way even after your traffic signal turns green?
sec14-card-f08.expected_back: A green signal permits movement only after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians already in the crossing or intersection.

sec14-card-f09.front: How must you handle a flashing red signal light at an intersection?
sec14-card-f09.expected_back: At a flashing red intersection signal, stop, yield to traffic in the intersection or crosswalk and proceed only when safe.

sec14-card-f10.front: How should you drive through an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow signal?
sec14-card-f10.expected_back: A flashing yellow intersection light allows proceeding cautiously.

sec14-card-f11.front: Does a lit directional arrow let you drive immediately if pedestrians or vehicles are still clearing the intersection?
sec14-card-f11.expected_back: Movement in a traffic arrow’s direction still requires yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection or crosswalk.

sec14-card-f12.front: What does a steady red arrow forbid, and which turns remain allowed after stopping and yielding if unposted?
sec14-card-f12.expected_back: A steady red arrow generally forbids its indicated movement, but the handbook allows a right turn or the stated one-way-to-one-way left turn after a full stop and yielding.

sec14-card-f13.front: What change in signal phase does a steady yellow arrow warn turning drivers to expect?
sec14-card-f13.expected_back: A steady yellow arrow warns that a green arrow is ending or that the signal will soon turn red.

sec14-card-f14.front: What does a flashing yellow turn arrow permit you to do?
sec14-card-f14.expected_back: A flashing yellow arrow allows a turn in its direction after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection or crosswalk.

sec14-card-f15.front: What movement does an upward-pointing green arrow allow compared with a left- or right-pointing green arrow?
sec14-card-f15.expected_back: A green arrow pointing up allows straight travel only, while a right- or left-pointing arrow permits the indicated turn.

sec14-card-f16.front: What does an illuminated white walking-person pedestrian signal authorize?
sec14-card-f16.expected_back: A pedestrian facing a walking-person signal may cross in the signal’s direction.

sec14-card-f17.front: How does a flashing orange raised-hand pedestrian signal apply to someone on the curb versus someone already crossing?
sec14-card-f17.expected_back: A flashing orange raised hand means do not begin crossing, but someone who began under a steady walking signal may finish to the sidewalk or safety island.

sec14-card-f18.front: What does a steady, non-flashing orange raised hand tell pedestrians at a crosswalk?
sec14-card-f18.expected_back: A steady orange raised hand means do not enter the roadway.

sec14-card-f19.front: What does a lit red X suspended over a reversible highway or bridge lane mean?
sec14-card-f19.expected_back: An overhead red cross means the lane cannot be used.

sec14-card-f20.front: What should you do when you see a steady overhead yellow X above your lane?
sec14-card-f20.expected_back: An overhead yellow cross warns of a coming red cross, so leave the lane safely before it turns red.

sec14-card-f21.front: What single use does a flashing yellow overhead lane-control arrow allow?
sec14-card-f21.expected_back: The handbook’s flashing yellow overhead arrow identifies a lane available for approaching and making a left turn.

sec14-card-f22.front: Does a downward-pointing green overhead lane-control arrow let you ignore intersection stop signs or red lights ahead?
sec14-card-f22.expected_back: A green lane arrow permits lane use subject to all other traffic signs and signals.

sec14-card-f23.front: How do solid white and solid yellow pavement edge lines tell you which side of a divided road is which?
sec14-card-f23.expected_back: A solid white edge line marks the road’s right boundary, while a solid yellow line marks the left edge of a divided roadway.

sec14-card-f24.front: What direction is traffic moving in adjacent lanes separated by white lane lines?
sec14-card-f24.expected_back: White lane lines divide lanes traveling in the same direction.

sec14-card-r01.front: What lane movements are permitted across a dashed or broken white pavement line?
sec14-card-r01.expected_back: A broken white line may be crossed to change lanes or turn.

sec14-card-r02.front: What rule applies to crossing a single solid white line between same-direction lanes?
sec14-card-r02.expected_back: Crossing a single solid white lane line is discouraged and requires special caution.

sec14-card-r03.front: Are you allowed to change lanes across a double solid white pavement line?
sec14-card-r03.expected_back: Crossing a double solid white lane boundary is prohibited.

sec14-card-r04.front: What traffic flow relationship do yellow centerline markings always indicate?
sec14-card-r04.expected_back: Yellow center markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

sec14-card-r05.front: When may you cross a single broken yellow centerline to pass a slower vehicle?
sec14-card-r05.expected_back: A broken yellow center line allows passing between opposing single lanes when the maneuver is otherwise safe and lawful.

sec14-card-r06.front: For what specific turns are you legally allowed to cross double solid yellow centerlines?
sec14-card-r06.expected_back: Double solid yellow center lines may be crossed for a left turn into or out of an alley, private road, driveway or street.

sec14-card-r07.front: What two narrow exceptions allow crossing a solid yellow line painted on your side of the center?
sec14-card-r07.expected_back: A solid yellow line on your side marks a no-passing area, but it may be crossed to finish a pass begun before the area or to make the stated left-access turn.

sec14-card-r08.front: When a centerline pairs one broken yellow stripe with one solid yellow stripe, which lane is allowed to pass?
sec14-card-r08.expected_back: With one broken and one solid yellow center line, passing is allowed only from the side nearest the broken line.

sec14-card-r09.front: When a road provides a marked two-way center left-turn lane, may you turn left from the regular through lane instead?
sec14-card-r09.expected_back: A two-way left-turn lane is identified by yellow lines and white arrows, and left turns must use that lane when it is provided.

sec14-card-r10.front: Which maneuvers are legally allowed inside a shared two-way left-turn lane?
sec14-card-r10.expected_back: Use a two-way left-turn lane only to prepare for or make a left turn into or out of the road, or a lawful U-turn.

sec14-card-r11.front: How must your front bumper line up with a painted white stop line at a stop sign or red light?
sec14-card-r11.expected_back: A white transverse stop line marks where a red light or stop sign requires stopping, with every part of the vehicle remaining behind the line.

sec14-card-r12.front: About how far ahead of the crosswalk is a white stop line typically painted on city streets?
sec14-card-r12.expected_back: In urban areas the stop line is usually four feet before the crosswalk.

sec14-card-r13.front: How are marked crosswalks painted across a roadway, and who holds right-of-way inside them?
sec14-card-r13.expected_back: White crosswalk markings span the pavement and can include diagonal stripes, and pedestrians in the crossing have priority over vehicles.

sec14-card-r14.front: Do marked pedestrian crosswalks appear only at street corners?
sec14-card-r14.expected_back: A marked crossing can be in the middle of a block and have a pedestrian-crossing sign at its white lines.

sec14-card-r15.front: What do diagonal yellow or white pavement stripes warn you to steer around?
sec14-card-r15.expected_back: Diagonal yellow or white stripes mark fixed obstructions, and solid white or yellow lines can guide traffic around a hazard.

sec14-card-r16.front: Besides upright street signs, how can cities and towns mark zones where parking is banned?
sec14-card-r16.expected_back: Local authorities may designate no-parking areas using curb, fire-lane or pavement markings.

sec14-card-r17.front: Up to how many feet ahead of railroad tracks can a round yellow advance-warning sign be posted?
sec14-card-r17.expected_back: A round yellow advance railway warning with black crossed marks and railway letters may be placed up to seven hundred fifty feet before the tracks.

sec14-card-r18.front: What roles do the solid yellow centerline and the wide white transverse line play right before railroad tracks?
sec14-card-r18.expected_back: A solid yellow line before a railway crossing prohibits passing, and white stop lines indicate where to stop for a train.

sec14-card-r19.front: How must you treat a white X-shaped railroad crossbuck, and what does the smaller plaque underneath tell you?
sec14-card-r19.expected_back: A crossbuck functions as a yield control requiring priority for approaching rail traffic; a supplementary sign gives the number of tracks at a multiple-track crossing.

sec14-card-r20.front: After a train clears a crossing, when may you proceed if the red warning lights are still flashing?
sec14-card-r20.expected_back: When railway warning lights flash, stop and stay stopped until the train passes and the flashing ends.

sec14-card-r21.front: What two conditions must finish before crossing gated railroad tracks, and what gate maneuvers are strictly forbidden?
sec14-card-r21.expected_back: Remain stopped until crossing gates are raised and warning lights stop flashing, and never drive around lowered gates or try to beat gates being lowered.

sec14-card-r22.front: What details can automated railroad-crossing cameras capture, and what two penalties can follow?
sec14-card-r22.expected_back: Automated crossing enforcement can record the plate, location and time of a violation, which can bring fines and possible license suspension.

sec14-card-r23.front: What two critical pieces of information appear on the railroad emergency-notification sign posted at every crossing?
sec14-card-r23.expected_back: An emergency-notification sign identifies the railroad’s contact information and the specific crossing so the public can report an emergency to the responsible railroad.

sec15-card-f01.front: How should you anticipate other drivers' moves, and what principle guides you if a crash becomes unavoidable?
sec15-card-f01.expected_back: Prepare for other drivers’ unexpected actions rather than assuming their intentions, and if a crash cannot be avoided, stay calm and seek the least dangerous outcome.

sec15-card-f02.front: How do you use a fixed roadside landmark to measure Illinois's three-second following rule?
sec15-card-f02.expected_back: For the three-second following check, begin counting when the leading vehicle passes a fixed landmark and do not reach that landmark before three seconds have elapsed.

sec15-card-f03.front: What conditions does the three-second following gap assume, and when must you add extra seconds?
sec15-card-f03.expected_back: The three-second gap assumes favorable road and weather conditions; leave more time when either is poor.

sec15-card-f04.front: What two options does Illinois recommend when another driver follows you too closely?
sec15-card-f04.expected_back: If another vehicle follows too closely, change lanes or gradually pull off so it can pass.

sec15-card-f05.front: At twenty-five miles per hour, roughly how many feet per second do you cover and how long is a three-second gap?
sec15-card-f05.expected_back: At twenty-five miles per hour, the handbook approximates travel as thirty-seven feet per second and a three-second gap as one hundred eleven feet.

sec15-card-f06.front: At thirty-five miles per hour, what approximate distance per second and three-second following gap does the Illinois chart list?
sec15-card-f06.expected_back: At thirty-five miles per hour, the handbook approximates travel as fifty-two feet per second and a three-second gap as one hundred fifty-six feet.

sec15-card-f07.front: At forty-five miles per hour, how many feet do you travel each second and across a three-second gap?
sec15-card-f07.expected_back: At forty-five miles per hour, the stated estimates are sixty-six feet each second and one hundred ninety-eight feet over three seconds.

sec15-card-f08.front: At fifty-five miles per hour, what feet-per-second pace and three-second distance does the Illinois table show?
sec15-card-f08.expected_back: At fifty-five miles per hour, the listed approximations are eighty-one feet per second and two hundred forty-three feet for three seconds.

sec15-card-f09.front: At sixty-five miles per hour, roughly how far do you travel per second and across three seconds?
sec15-card-f09.expected_back: At sixty-five miles per hour, the table gives roughly ninety-six feet per second and two hundred eighty-eight feet for a three-second gap.

sec15-card-f10.front: At seventy miles per hour, what approximate one-second travel and three-second following distance appear in the chart?
sec15-card-f10.expected_back: At seventy miles per hour, the table gives approximately one hundred three feet per second and three hundred nine feet for three seconds.

sec15-card-f11.front: How should weather, traffic, and road surface shape your speed — and why can creeping far too slowly also cause danger?
sec15-card-f11.expected_back: Adjust speed to weather, traffic and road conditions while staying at or below the posted maximum; going too quickly or too slowly can be hazardous.

sec15-card-f12.front: Which six human, mechanical, and environmental factors must your chosen travel speed take into account?
sec15-card-f12.expected_back: Speed selection should account for reaction ability, road condition, tires, brakes, wind and the vehicle’s design and condition.

sec15-card-f13.front: Does drowsiness hurt driving before you actually nod off — and what two trip habits prevent fatigue?
sec15-card-f13.expected_back: Drowsiness impairs safe reactions even without actual sleep, so start rested and take frequent breaks on long trips.

sec15-card-f14.front: What two visual habits help keep your eyes alert and engaged on long drives?
sec15-card-f14.expected_back: Shifting visual focus around the roadway and reading signs can help keep the eyes active during driving.

sec15-card-f15.front: What is the best choice when fog rolls in — and what three adjustments belong if you must drive?
sec15-card-f15.expected_back: Avoid driving in fog when possible; if driving is necessary, switch off cruise control, increase the gap and reduce speed.

sec15-card-f16.front: Which lights belong in fog, how fast may you travel, and how should you react upon spotting another car's lights?
sec15-card-f16.expected_back: In fog use low beams or fog lamps, drive within visible stopping space and slow further when seeing another vehicle’s lamps.

sec15-card-f17.front: Why must you pull off the road and stop in blinding fog instead of creeping forward at five to ten miles per hour?
sec15-card-f17.expected_back: When fog is too dense, leave the roadway and stop rather than continuing at five to ten miles per hour.

sec15-card-f18.front: How should you adjust turn signals and braking timing when driving in fog?
sec15-card-f18.expected_back: Signal well before a foggy-weather turn and brake early for a stop to alert following drivers.

sec15-card-f19.front: When does rain require turning on your headlights in Illinois, and why is initial light rain extra slick?
sec15-card-f19.expected_back: Use headlights when rain requires windshield-wiper operation, and recognize that initial light rain can mix with road contaminants to create a slippery surface.

sec15-card-f20.front: What cruise-control, spacing, and maneuvering changes belong whenever you drive in rain?
sec15-card-f20.expected_back: In rain, disable cruise control, leave more following space and take added care while turning, curving or braking.

sec15-card-f21.front: How do you prevent hydroplaning, and what should your right foot do if an uncontrollable hydroplaning skid starts?
sec15-card-f21.expected_back: Reduce speed to avoid hydroplaning; if a hydroplaning skid cannot be controlled, release the accelerator and allow the skid to run out.

sec15-card-f22.front: Why must you turn around instead of driving across a flooded roadway or underpass viaduct?
sec15-card-f22.expected_back: Do not cross a flooded road or viaduct because water depth and current cannot be judged reliably; turn around and take another route.

sec15-card-f23.front: How should you drive in strong winds, especially when emerging from wind shelter or passing trucks and buses?
sec15-card-f23.expected_back: In strong wind, slow and be ready to correct steering when leaving shelter or meeting a truck or bus.

sec15-card-f24.front: Why does strong wind often demand more than steering grip alone?
sec15-card-f24.expected_back: High winds may accompany rain or sleet, so plan for wet or slippery pavement as well as the wind itself.

sec15-card-f25.front: Which towed vehicles are prohibited on the Illinois toll-road system during high winds?
sec15-card-f25.expected_back: The Illinois toll-road system prohibits hauling house trailers during high winds.

sec15-card-r01.front: Besides slowing down and widening gaps in winter, why can't you trust one stretch of pavement to match the next?
sec15-card-r01.expected_back: In winter slow down, extend following space and expect surface conditions to differ between sunny, shaded and different roadway areas.

sec15-card-r02.front: On which three slick road conditions must cruise control remain turned off?
sec15-card-r02.expected_back: Do not use cruise control on pavement that is wet, snowy or icy.

sec15-card-r03.front: Which four clearing, defrosting, fluid, and lighting steps belong before setting out on a winter drive?
sec15-card-r03.expected_back: Before winter driving, remove snow and ice, clear and defrost all windows, use nonfreezing washer fluid and make headlights and rear lamps visible.

sec15-card-r04.front: Which five vehicle systems must stay in reliable working order for winter driving?
sec15-card-r04.expected_back: Keep winter-driving equipment such as lamps, brakes, wipers, defrosters and radiator in working order.

sec15-card-r05.front: What limit still applies even when your vehicle wears snow tires or permitted tire chains?
sec15-card-r05.expected_back: Snow tires and permitted chains improve traction but do not make ordinary driving speeds safe on poor roads.

sec15-card-r06.front: How should you use your brakes when approaching a winter stop so you can feel available grip?
sec15-card-r06.expected_back: Begin braking early and apply gentle, steady braking to judge available traction when nearing a stop.

sec15-card-r07.front: Which four roadway features stay icy long after surrounding pavement dries out?
sec15-card-r07.expected_back: Approach bridges, shaded areas, overpasses and turns slowly because they can remain icy after nearby pavement has dried.

sec15-card-r08.front: Which three emergency items does Illinois suggest carrying in winter, and where should you stay if stranded?
sec15-card-r08.expected_back: Carry useful winter supplies such as a blanket, food and shovel, and if stranded remain with the vehicle.

sec15-card-r09.front: If you are stranded in winter snow, what exterior part of your vehicle should you keep clear if possible?
sec15-card-r09.expected_back: If possible, keep a stranded vehicle’s exhaust outlet clear of snow and debris.

sec15-card-r10.front: What four actions belong in an expressway acceleration lane before merging into highway traffic?
sec15-card-r10.expected_back: Use the expressway acceleration lane to gain appropriate speed, signal, find a gap and match traffic before merging when safe.

sec15-card-r11.front: Which mirror checks and communication step must come before changing lanes on an expressway?
sec15-card-r11.expected_back: Check both rear and side mirrors and signal before changing expressway lanes.

sec15-card-r12.front: How should you manage forward space, slower travel, and the left lane on an Illinois expressway?
sec15-card-r12.expected_back: Keep ample space behind the vehicle ahead, use the right lane for slower travel and avoid continuous left-lane driving.

sec15-card-r13.front: If mechanical trouble forces an expressway stop, what three warning steps apply — and what walking rule holds?
sec15-card-r13.expected_back: If a problem forces a stop, leave the expressway roadway, raise the hood and activate hazard lamps, and do not walk along the expressway.

sec15-card-r14.front: Because expressway exits can sit on either side, when should you choose your lane, signal, and slow down?
sec15-card-r14.expected_back: Exits can be on either side, so select the correct exit lane, signal and reduce speed in the exit speed-change lane.

sec15-card-r15.front: What must you do if you pass your expressway exit — and why is reversing off-limits?
sec15-card-r15.expected_back: After missing an exit, continue to the next one rather than backing up, which is illegal on an expressway.

sec15-card-r16.front: At a lane drop, how does proper merge timing differ between light traffic and heavy slow congestion?
sec15-card-r16.expected_back: At a lane reduction, merge early if traffic is light; in dense slow traffic use both lanes to the merge point and alternate joining there.

sec15-card-r17.front: How should you maintain your headlights, and how does their beam reach govern nighttime speed?
sec15-card-r17.expected_back: Keep headlights clean and correctly aimed, and do not travel beyond the distance they illuminate.

sec15-card-r18.front: When must headlights run at night, and at what exact distances must you dim high beams for oncoming or overtaken cars?
sec15-card-r18.expected_back: Use headlights from sunset to sunrise and dim high beams five hundred feet before an approaching vehicle or three hundred feet before passing another vehicle.

sec15-card-r19.front: How should you set dashboard brightness, sun visors, and dome lights for sharper night vision?
sec15-card-r19.expected_back: Reduce dashboard brightness, use the visor against glare and avoid other interior lights at night.

sec15-card-r20.front: Which painted stripes help guide your lane position at night, and where must you avoid stopping?
sec15-card-r20.expected_back: Use road-edge and center markings to guide nighttime travel, and avoid stopping on the roadway.

sec15-card-r21.front: How should you approach every rural intersection, even when no warning sign appears?
sec15-card-r21.expected_back: Slow and look both ways at every rural intersection, including locations without a warning sign.

sec15-card-r22.front: When should you shed speed for a curve, what pedal mistake can trigger a skid, and where must your car stay?
sec15-card-r22.expected_back: Slow before entering a curve, avoid abrupt braking that may cause a skid and remain on your side of the center line.

sec15-card-r23.front: If an oncoming vehicle drifts head-on into your lane, what three immediate actions should you take?
sec15-card-r23.expected_back: If a vehicle approaches head-on in your lane, slow, move toward the right and sound the horn.

sec15-card-r24.front: Once tires lose traction and start skidding, how should you use the pedals and steering wheel to recover?
sec15-card-r24.expected_back: A skid begins when tires lose traction; ease off the accelerator or brakes, steer in the skid’s direction until grip returns and then straighten.

sec15-card-r25.front: If your tires drop off the pavement edge onto the shoulder, what five calm steps bring you safely back onto the road?
sec15-card-r25.expected_back: If wheels leave the pavement, hold the wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, brake gently, check rear traffic and return with gentle steering rather than a sudden correction.

sec16-card-f01.front: If smoke starts coming from your vehicle, what four actions must you take — and what should you never attempt yourself?
sec16-card-f01.expected_back: If smoke appears, pull off the road, switch off the engine, move away and call nine one one; do not try to fight the vehicle fire yourself.

sec16-card-f02.front: If your vehicle plunges into water without sinking right away, how should you escape and why?
sec16-card-f02.expected_back: If a vehicle enters water without immediately sinking, try to escape through a window because water pressure may prevent the doors opening.

sec16-card-f03.front: Which lethal gas is present in fuel-burning vehicle exhaust?
sec16-card-f03.expected_back: Fuel-burning vehicle exhaust contains carbon monoxide, which can be fatal.

sec16-card-f04.front: Which physical symptoms signal carbon-monoxide poisoning, and what common illness can it mimic?
sec16-card-f04.expected_back: Carbon-monoxide poisoning can cause headache, dizziness, weakness, stomach upset, vomiting, chest pain or confusion and may resemble influenza.

sec16-card-f05.front: Why is napping inside a running vehicle or idling inside a garage frequently fatal?
sec16-card-f05.expected_back: People sleeping in a running vehicle or leaving it running in a garage can die before noticing carbon-monoxide symptoms.

sec16-card-f06.front: Who inside a car can be harmed by carbon monoxide, and which groups face heightened danger?
sec16-card-f06.expected_back: Everyone in a vehicle can be harmed by carbon monoxide, with particular risk for infants, older people and people with heart, lung or blood disorders.

sec16-card-f07.front: How often should a mechanic inspect your exhaust system, and what home-garage rule applies?
sec16-card-f07.expected_back: The handbook recommends an annual mechanic’s inspection of the exhaust and prohibits running the vehicle in a garage attached to a home.

sec16-card-f08.front: If live utility lines fall across your vehicle in a crash, where should occupants stay — and what single exception applies?
sec16-card-f08.expected_back: If power lines fall on the vehicle, occupants should remain inside until help arrives unless an immediate fire danger requires leaving.

sec16-card-f09.front: If fire forces you out of a vehicle touching downed power lines, how must you clear the car?
sec16-card-f09.expected_back: When fire requires escape from an electrified vehicle, jump clear without touching the vehicle and ground simultaneously.

sec16-card-f10.front: Once you jump clear of an electrified vehicle, how should you land and move fifty feet away?
sec16-card-f10.expected_back: After jumping clear, land with both feet together and hop or shuffle fifty feet away with arms kept near the body.

sec16-card-f11.front: Which three safety rules apply every time you refuel at a gas pump?
sec16-card-f11.expected_back: Switch off the engine, avoid smoking near fuel pumps and stay with the pump while refueling.

sec16-card-f12.front: What sound often precedes a tire blowout, and what four calm actions bring you safely off the road?
sec16-card-f12.expected_back: A thumping noise can warn of a tire blowout; ease off the accelerator, hold the wheel firmly, pull off safely and avoid sudden braking.

sec16-card-f13.front: How should you respond if a wheel or tire separates from your vehicle at speed?
sec16-card-f13.expected_back: Respond to the loss of a wheel or tire using the same controlled response as for a blowout.

sec16-card-f14.front: If your steering fails completely, what pedal, light, and braking steps bring the vehicle down safely?
sec16-card-f14.expected_back: If steering control fails, ease off the accelerator, use hazard lamps, brake very gently and let the vehicle slow to a stop.

sec16-card-f15.front: Why must you never turn off the ignition while rolling during a steering emergency?
sec16-card-f15.expected_back: Do not switch off the ignition on a vehicle with power steering or a steering lock during steering failure because steering assistance or steering ability may be lost.

sec16-card-f16.front: If your brake pedal suddenly sinks to the floor, what should you try first — and what two backups slow you down?
sec16-card-f16.expected_back: If the pedal suddenly goes to the floor, pump it to try to restore pressure; if that fails, use the parking brake and a lower gear to slow.

sec16-card-r01.front: Which backup lights help you get off the road if headlights suddenly go dark — and how should you handle dimming bulbs?
sec16-card-r01.expected_back: For sudden headlamp failure, try hazard, parking or turn-signal lamps and leave the road; dimming lamps call for a service location or pulling off to seek help.

sec16-card-r02.front: If your accelerator sticks down and cannot be freed, what gear and braking response slows the car?
sec16-card-r02.expected_back: If a stuck accelerator cannot be freed, select neutral and brake gently to reduce speed.

sec16-card-r03.front: If your hood flies up or mud blocks your forward windshield view, how do you see to pull off?
sec16-card-r03.expected_back: If the forward view is blocked, lower a side window to see, activate hazard lamps and pull off the roadway.

sec16-card-r04.front: How does Illinois define aggressive driving?
sec16-card-r04.expected_back: Aggressive driving means operating in a way that endangers or is likely to endanger people or property.

sec16-card-r05.front: Which five dangerous moving violations does the manual highlight as examples of potentially aggressive driving?
sec16-card-r05.expected_back: Speeding, disregarding red lights or stop signs, tailgating, shoulder passing and cutting off another vehicle are examples of potentially aggressive driving.

sec16-card-r06.front: Which four retaliatory or hostile behaviors behind the wheel count as aggressive acts?
sec16-card-r06.expected_back: Sudden braking at a tailgater, hostile gestures, shouting and repeated horn or headlight use can be aggressive acts.

sec16-card-r07.front: How should you respond — including where you look — when encountering an angry driver?
sec16-card-r07.expected_back: Do not retaliate or engage an angry driver, and avoid eye contact.

sec16-card-r08.front: How should you secure your cabin and stop behind traffic when an aggressive driver is nearby?
sec16-card-r08.expected_back: Keep doors locked and windows closed near an aggressive driver, and leave enough space ahead to pull away from behind another vehicle.

sec16-card-r09.front: What mindset warning does the Illinois manual give about another driver's potential for aggression?
sec16-card-r09.expected_back: Do not underestimate another driver’s capacity for aggression.

sec16-card-r10.front: How do high-capacity roadways differ from low-capacity roads in traffic volume, lanes, features, and speed?
sec16-card-r10.expected_back: High-capacity roads are designed for heavy traffic and often have multiple lanes and traffic-management features, while low-capacity roads generally serve lighter flows with fewer features and lower speeds.

sec16-card-r11.front: If you break down on a high-capacity highway, what five steps keep you safe while waiting for responders?
sec16-card-r11.expected_back: On a high-capacity road, move as far right or into another safe location as possible, stay buckled inside, activate hazard lamps, call nine one one and wait for responders.

sec16-card-r12.front: What is your first positioning goal during a breakdown on a lower-capacity road?
sec16-card-r12.expected_back: On a lower-capacity road, first move to a safe location clear of passing traffic, using the right shoulder if possible.

sec16-card-r13.front: If you must exit a disabled car on a lower-capacity road and it is safe, which door side and waiting spot belong?
sec16-card-r13.expected_back: If leaving is necessary and safe on a lower-capacity road, exit away from approaching traffic and move to a protected place such as behind a barrier or onto a sidewalk.

sec16-card-r14.front: What three actions apply if you cannot safely exit a disabled vehicle?
sec16-card-r14.expected_back: If a safe exit is unavailable, remain buckled inside, turn on hazard lamps and call nine one one for help.

sec16-card-r15.front: If you break down on an Illinois toll road, how should you position and secure yourself — and which two numbers summon help?
sec16-card-r15.expected_back: On an Illinois toll road, move far onto the right shoulder if possible, remain belted inside, use hazard lamps and call star nine nine nine or nine one one while waiting for assistance.

sec17-card-f01.front: What general equipment standard must every Illinois vehicle meet, and when is driving a vehicle illegal?
sec17-card-f01.expected_back: A vehicle must have working, proper equipment, and driving a vehicle hazardous to people or property is illegal.

sec17-card-f02.front: How many brake systems and wheel brakes must a passenger car have — and what exception applies to motor-driven cycles?
sec17-card-f02.expected_back: A car needs two brake systems and brakes on every wheel; the stated exception for a motor-driven cycle allows one brake.

sec17-card-f03.front: From twenty miles per hour, within how many feet must your main foot brake stop the vehicle?
sec17-card-f03.expected_back: At twenty miles per hour, the foot brake must stop the vehicle within thirty feet.

sec17-card-f04.front: From twenty miles per hour, within what distance must the parking brake stop your car — and what hill test applies?
sec17-card-f04.expected_back: At twenty miles per hour, the parking brake must stop the vehicle within fifty-five feet and must also hold it on a grade.

sec17-card-f05.front: How many headlamps does a car require, and which two lighting or weather conditions mandate turning them on?
sec17-card-f05.expected_back: A car needs two headlamps, used from sunset to sunrise and when weather requires windshield wipers.

sec17-card-f06.front: At what forward visibility distance does the Illinois manual also recommend switching on your headlights?
sec17-card-f06.expected_back: The handbook also recommends headlight use when objects one thousand feet away cannot be seen.

sec17-card-f07.front: At how many feet must you dim high beams before meeting an oncoming vehicle or overtaking one ahead?
sec17-card-f07.expected_back: Dim high beams five hundred feet before meeting an approaching vehicle and three hundred feet before passing another vehicle.

sec17-card-f08.front: How far ahead must a motorcycle or moped headlamp reach, and when must it stay switched on?
sec17-card-f08.expected_back: A motorcycle or moped needs a headlamp that illuminates objects five hundred feet ahead and stays on whenever the vehicle is driven.

sec17-card-f09.front: Does Illinois allow tinted or smoked covers over vehicle lamp lenses?
sec17-card-f09.expected_back: Tinted or smoked lamp lenses are not permitted on a vehicle.

sec17-card-f10.front: How many red rear lamps must a car carry versus a motorcycle or moped, and how far back must they show?
sec17-card-f10.expected_back: A car needs two red rear lamps visible for five hundred feet, while a motorcycle or moped needs one.

sec17-card-f11.front: How far must standard front and rear turn signals be visible, and which three vehicle types are excluded from that entry?
sec17-card-f11.expected_back: The general turn-signal rule requires front and rear signals for each direction visible for three hundred feet, with motorcycles, trailers and semitrailers excluded from that entry.

sec17-card-f12.front: What color lamp must illuminate your rear license plate, from what distance must it read, and when must it turn on?
sec17-card-f12.expected_back: A white plate lamp must make the plate legible from fifty feet and must operate whenever the headlights are on.

sec17-card-f13.front: What lights are required on a vehicle stopped along a highway at night, and what local exception can apply?
sec17-card-f13.expected_back: A vehicle stopped on a highway at night needs front and rear parking lamps unless a local unlit-street-parking exception applies.

sec17-card-f14.front: How many front seat-belt sets must a passenger car have, and which model-year cutoff bars beltless sale or operation?
sec17-card-f14.expected_back: A passenger vehicle needs two front-seat belt sets, and a vehicle manufactured in nineteen sixty-five or later cannot be sold or operated in Illinois without belts.

sec17-card-f15.front: How far behind your car must at least one rearview mirror give a clear view?
sec17-card-f15.expected_back: At least one rearview mirror must provide a view two hundred feet behind the car.

sec17-card-f16.front: What glass standard applies to vehicle windows, and which four hazards must stay off your windshield?
sec17-card-f16.expected_back: Windows must use approved safety glass, and the windshield must be clear of snow, ice, moisture and vision-distorting defects.

sec17-card-f17.front: What obstruction rule applies to the space between the driver and the front or rear windows?
sec17-card-f17.expected_back: Keep glass free of obstructions between the driver and front or rear windows.

sec17-card-f18.front: What is Illinois's rule on windshield tinting, and how deep may the sole allowed top strip extend?
sec17-card-f18.expected_back: Windshield tint is prohibited except for a strip six inches deep extending across its top.

sec17-card-r01.front: Which three weather accumulations must working windshield wipers be able to clear?
sec17-card-r01.expected_back: Working wipers must clear moisture, snow and ice.

sec17-card-r02.front: From what distance must your horn be heard — and who alone may carry sirens, whistles, or bells?
sec17-card-r02.expected_back: A required horn must be audible at two hundred feet, while sirens, whistles and bells are reserved for authorized emergency vehicles.

sec17-card-r03.front: What two outputs must a muffler control, and which exhaust alterations are illegal in Illinois?
sec17-card-r03.expected_back: The exhaust needs a muffler to limit excessive smoke and noise, and noise-increasing cutouts, bypasses or modifications are illegal.

sec17-card-r04.front: Which weight class of vehicles — plus which recreational category — must carry both front and rear bumpers?
sec17-card-r04.expected_back: A front and rear bumper are required on vehicles weighing nine thousand pounds or less and on every recreational vehicle.

sec17-card-r05.front: When cargo sticks out four feet or more past your rear bumper, how must you mark it by day versus night?
sec17-card-r05.expected_back: A load projecting at least four feet behind a vehicle needs a red flag by day and a red lamp visible for five hundred feet at night or in poor visibility.

sec17-card-r06.front: Which two colors are legal for backup lamps, and when must those lamps stay switched off?
sec17-card-r06.expected_back: Backup lamps must be nonglaring white or amber and must not be lit while the vehicle travels forward.

sec17-card-r07.front: How many spotlights may a vehicle carry, and how must you aim one when approaching another vehicle?
sec17-card-r07.expected_back: Only one spotlight is permitted, and when approaching another vehicle it must not point left or more than one hundred feet ahead.

sec17-card-r08.front: At most how many lamps rated at three hundred candlepower may a vehicle burn at once?
sec17-card-r08.expected_back: A vehicle may not burn more than four lamps rated at three hundred candlepower.

sec17-card-r09.front: Aside from turn signals and hazard flashers, who may use flashing or moving lamps on Illinois roads?
sec17-card-r09.expected_back: Flashing or moving lamps other than turn or hazard signals are generally prohibited except on police or designated emergency vehicles.

sec17-card-r10.front: Which vehicles are the only ones allowed to display red lights visible from the front?
sec17-card-r10.expected_back: Front-visible red lights are restricted to police and designated emergency vehicles.

sec17-card-r11.front: How many running-board lights are permitted per side, and what colors and glare standard apply?
sec17-card-r11.expected_back: Running-board lighting is limited to one nonglaring white or amber lamp on each side.

sec17-card-r12.front: What count, glare rule, and color choices govern cowl or fender lights?
sec17-card-r12.expected_back: Cowl or fender lighting is limited to two nonglaring white or amber lamps.

sec17-card-r13.front: Are metal-studded tires generally legal in Illinois — and which vehicles qualify for the November fifteenth to April first exception?
sec17-card-r13.expected_back: Metal-studded tires are generally prohibited, with seasonal exceptions for rural mail vehicles and qualifying disability or disabled-veteran plate vehicles from November fifteenth to April first.

sec17-card-r14.front: Where must a disability-plate vehicle owner live to qualify for Illinois's seasonal studded-tire exception?
sec17-card-r14.expected_back: The disability-plate seasonal studded-tire exception requires the owner to live on a county or township road outside an incorporated area.

sec17-card-r15.front: Which slow work machines are also exempt from Illinois's studded-tire ban, and below what speed?
sec17-card-r15.expected_back: The studded-tire prohibition also has exceptions for listed agricultural equipment and road-building machines moving below ten miles per hour.

sec17-card-r16.front: What does Illinois law say about a moving vehicle's TV/video screen in the driver's view or watching live phone video?
sec17-card-r16.expected_back: A television or video monitor visible from the driver’s seat is prohibited while the vehicle moves, and viewing live phone video while driving is also unlawful.

sec17-card-r17.front: How do equipment rules for lamps, brakes, and turn signals apply to vehicles more than twenty-five years old?
sec17-card-r17.expected_back: Vehicles older than twenty-five years have special requirements for lamps, brakes and turn signals rather than automatically using every ordinary equipment rule.

sec17-card-r18.front: Is possessing or operating a police radar jammer allowed inside any Illinois vehicle?
sec17-card-r18.expected_back: Possessing or using a radar jammer is prohibited in any vehicle.

sec18-card-f01.front: Within how many days after a dealer vehicle sale must paperwork go in, and what documents and separate payments belong?
sec18-card-f01.expected_back: Within twenty days after a vehicle purchase, the dealer must send the agency the transaction application, properly signed title or origin certificate and separate payments for title and plate fees and sales tax.

sec18-card-f02.front: What causes the sales-tax rate on a dealership vehicle purchase to vary in Illinois?
sec18-card-f02.expected_back: Sales tax on a dealer vehicle purchase varies with the city or county where the purchase occurs.

sec18-card-f03.front: When you buy a car from a private seller, what four items must reach the state agency within twenty days?
sec18-card-f03.expected_back: Within twenty days of acquiring a vehicle from a private owner, the agency must receive the application, seller-signed title, title and plate payments and vehicle-use-tax payment.

sec18-card-f04.front: How is private-party vehicle-use tax calculated below fifteen thousand dollars versus at or above fifteen thousand?
sec18-card-f04.expected_back: For a private purchase below fifteen thousand dollars, vehicle-use tax depends on model year; at that price or above it depends on the selling price.

sec18-card-f05.front: Which tax form and state department receive your private-party vehicle-use tax payment?
sec18-card-f05.expected_back: The private-party tax submission requires form R U T fifty and the correct payment to the state revenue department.

sec18-card-f06.front: Along with the application, fees, tax, and bill of sale, what ownership proof does an out-of-state new or used purchase need?
sec18-card-f06.expected_back: An out-of-state purchase needs the transaction application, title and plate fees, tax payment, a bill of sale and either the dealer-signed origin certificate for a new vehicle or assigned title for a used one.

sec18-card-f07.front: What extra document must you include when transferring existing Illinois plates onto an out-of-state vehicle purchase?
sec18-card-f07.expected_back: When transferring plates to an out-of-state purchase, include the recent vehicle-registration identification card.

sec18-card-f08.front: How does vehicle registration differ in legal purpose from an Illinois certificate of title?
sec18-card-f08.expected_back: Registration creates a state vehicle record and permits legal use on Illinois roads, while the Illinois title proves ownership.

sec18-card-f09.front: Do vehicles and mobile homes still require an Illinois title even when they are not registered for road use?
sec18-card-f09.expected_back: Every vehicle and mobile home needs a title even when it is not registered.

sec18-card-f10.front: How often do registration fees renew, and what late penalty triggers more than one month past expiration?
sec18-card-f10.expected_back: Registration fees are annual, and renewal more than one month after expiry carries a twenty-dollar late charge.

sec18-card-f11.front: What annual registration fee does the manual list for a passenger car or qualifying truck up to eight thousand pounds?
sec18-card-f11.expected_back: The handbook lists a one-hundred-fifty-one-dollar annual fee for a passenger vehicle or a qualifying truck weighing no more than eight thousand pounds.

sec18-card-f12.front: How do the listed annual registration fees compare between a motorcycle and an autocycle?
sec18-card-f12.expected_back: The listed motorcycle registration fee is forty-one dollars, while an autocycle registration is seventy-one dollars.

sec18-card-f13.front: What replacement fees does the manual list for one lost plate, two plates, and a replacement registration sticker?
sec18-card-f13.expected_back: The listed replacement charge is six dollars for one plate or nine dollars for two plates, and a replacement sticker is twenty dollars.

sec18-card-f14.front: Why can custom plate totals exceed standard rates, and what can change the handbook's published fee schedule?
sec18-card-f14.expected_back: Personalized, vanity and some other plate types carry additional fees, and legislation can change the published fee schedule.

sec18-card-f15.front: Where must your vehicle-registration card be kept whenever you are driving?
sec18-card-f15.expected_back: Carry the vehicle-registration card in the vehicle or on your person whenever driving.

sec18-card-f16.front: Where must cars, trucks, and vans mount license plates — and what rules govern frames and covers?
sec18-card-f16.expected_back: Passenger vehicles, trucks and vans must show a plate at each end, with frames that leave all plate information visible and no plate covers.

sec18-card-f17.front: Which five vehicle categories display just one license plate mounted on the rear?
sec18-card-f17.expected_back: Motorcycles, mopeds, trailers, semitrailers and apportioned buses use one plate at the rear.

sec18-card-f18.front: Which two commercial truck categories mount their single license plate on the front bumper?
sec18-card-f18.expected_back: Truck tractors and apportioned straight trucks display their single plate at the front.

sec18-card-f19.front: What must you do with the license plates when selling your vehicle in Illinois, and why?
sec18-card-f19.expected_back: On sale, remove the plates and keep them as the seller because Illinois plates stay with their owner rather than the vehicle.

sec18-card-f20.front: Where does an Illinois temporary registration permit mount, how long does it last, and what if metal plates arrive late?
sec18-card-f20.expected_back: A temporary registration permit goes in the rear-plate location and lasts ninety days from issuance, with possible reissuance if plates have not arrived by then.

sec18-card-f21.front: What two steps must you take with your temporary permit once permanent metal plates arrive?
sec18-card-f21.expected_back: Replace the temporary permit with permanent plates when they arrive, then destroy and discard the removed permit.

sec18-card-f22.front: Which four authorized places issue Illinois temporary registration permits?
sec18-card-f22.expected_back: Temporary registration permits are available from licensed dealers, remittance agencies, currency exchanges and agency facilities.

sec18-card-f23.front: Roughly how far ahead of expiration might a courtesy registration-renewal reminder arrive?
sec18-card-f23.expected_back: A courtesy vehicle-renewal reminder may arrive roughly sixty days before registration expires.

sec18-card-f24.front: Through which five methods or locations can Illinois owners renew vehicle registration?
sec18-card-f24.expected_back: Registration can be renewed online, by mail, at an agency facility, through the notice’s telephone service or at participating financial or remittance businesses.

sec18-card-f25.front: Which exact corner of which plate holds your renewal sticker — and what happens if you leave an expired sticker showing?
sec18-card-f25.expected_back: Affix the renewal sticker at the upper-right part of the rear plate promptly; failing to display it after the old sticker expires can lead to a stop and ticket.

sec18-card-f26.front: How long can a printed online-renewal receipt carried in the car cover for a mailed sticker not yet received?
sec18-card-f26.expected_back: An agency receipt kept in the vehicle can temporarily replace an unreceived sticker purchased online before expiry, but only for thirty days after the old registration sticker expires.

sec18-card-r01.front: Who qualifies to have the standard registration renewal fee waived right after returning to the United States?
sec18-card-r01.expected_back: An active-duty member or reservist proving combat service may have the standard registration fee waived for the renewal immediately after returning to the United States.

sec18-card-r02.front: How many days after returning from abroad do qualifying noncombat military and Defense civilian personnel get to register or renew?
sec18-card-r02.expected_back: Qualifying Illinois-resident noncombat military personnel, Armed Forces civilian employees and Defense Department employees serving abroad have forty-five days after return to obtain or renew vehicle registration.

sec18-card-r03.front: At least how many days should you allow after ordering personalized or vanity Illinois plates?
sec18-card-r03.expected_back: The handbook advises allowing at least forty-five days after ordering personalized or vanity plates.

sec18-card-r04.front: Who can receive an annual Illinois plate-fee discount under the Benefit Access Program, and on how many vehicles?
sec18-card-r04.expected_back: Eligible seniors and people with disabilities under the Benefit Access Program may receive one annual plate-fee discount for qualifying passenger or recreational vehicles.

sec18-card-r05.front: What does mandatory Illinois auto liability insurance pay for after a crash?
sec18-card-r05.expected_back: Vehicles operated in Illinois need liability coverage for injury or damage caused to other people or their property.

sec18-card-r06.front: What is Illinois's minimum liability coverage for injury or death of one person in a crash?
sec18-card-r06.expected_back: The listed minimum liability limit for one person’s injury or death in a crash is twenty-five thousand dollars.

sec18-card-r07.front: What is Illinois's minimum liability coverage when two or more people are injured or killed in one crash?
sec18-card-r07.expected_back: The listed liability minimum for injury or death of more than one person in a crash is fifty thousand dollars.

sec18-card-r08.front: What is Illinois's minimum liability coverage for damaging someone else's vehicle or property?
sec18-card-r08.expected_back: The listed minimum for damage to another person’s property is twenty thousand dollars.

sec18-card-r09.front: Does the standard twenty-five, fifty, twenty minimum apply to every vehicle category in Illinois?
sec18-card-r09.expected_back: Some vehicle categories need liability limits above the general minimums.

sec18-card-r10.front: When must you show proof of liability insurance, and what two formats are accepted?
sec18-card-r10.expected_back: Carry liability proof with the driver or vehicle and show it when police request it; the insurance card may be paper or displayed electronically.

sec18-card-r11.front: While waiting on a replacement insurance card, which four backup documents prove active coverage?
sec18-card-r11.expected_back: While replacing a missing insurance card, carry another proof such as a binder, current declarations, certificate or latest payment receipt.

sec18-card-r12.front: Which three enforcement checkpoints verify that Illinois vehicles carry active liability insurance?
sec18-card-r12.expected_back: The agency enforces insurance through random computer checks and traffic citations and requires paper or electronic coverage proof when plates are renewed.

sec18-card-r13.front: What three financial, renewal, and suspension consequences hit drivers caught without required Illinois insurance?
sec18-card-r13.expected_back: Lacking required insurance can bring fines, inability to renew registration and suspension of both driving and registration until proof is supplied.

sec18-card-r14.front: What penalties apply if someone submits false insurance details to the state agency or a renewal remitter?
sec18-card-r14.expected_back: Providing false insurance information to the agency or a renewal remitter can lead to criminal charges and a fine.

sec18-card-r15.front: How do Illinois emissions tests tie into registration renewal, and how do owners learn their test window?
sec18-card-r15.expected_back: Some vehicles need an environmental-agency emissions test before registration renewal, and owners receive notice of the scheduled testing month and year.

sec18-card-r16.front: Which three Illinois counties require emissions testing countywide, and which seven counties are partly covered?
sec18-card-r16.expected_back: The handbook lists all of Cook, DuPage and Lake counties and parts of Kane, Kendall, McHenry, Will, Madison, Monroe and St. Clair as emissions-testing areas.

sec18-card-r17.front: What must you do after relocating away from an Illinois emissions-testing area?
sec18-card-r17.expected_back: Notify the licensing agency after moving out of an emissions-testing area.

sec18-card-r18.front: Which two residency, disability, and title conditions let an individual obtain Illinois disability license plates?
sec18-card-r18.expected_back: An Illinois resident with a permanent disability may obtain disability plates for a vehicle titled to that resident.

sec18-card-r19.front: When may an immediate household family member obtain two sets of disability plates for someone else?
sec18-card-r19.expected_back: A household immediate-family member may obtain two disability-plate sets when the qualifying disabled person owns no vehicle and depends on others for transportation.

sec18-card-r20.front: Which groups outside individual households can also obtain Illinois disability license plates?
sec18-card-r20.expected_back: Eligible organizations transporting people with disabilities may obtain disability plates.

sec18-card-r21.front: Do disability license plates automatically exempt a vehicle from parking-meter fees or meter time limits?
sec18-card-r21.expected_back: Disability license plates do not by themselves waive parking-meter charges or meter time limits.

sec18-card-r22.front: Who must be present and using the vehicle whenever a disability parking placard is displayed in an accessible space?
sec18-card-r22.expected_back: An Illinois resident with a physician-certified disability may receive a placard, used only when that person is present and entering or leaving the vehicle in the accessible space.

sec18-card-r23.front: What disability standard earns a meter-exempt permanent placard, and which meters still charge even with one?
sec18-card-r23.expected_back: A meter-exempt permanent placard requires a qualifying permanent disability that significantly limits meter access and waives charges and time limits only at meters allowing more than thirty minutes.

sec18-card-r24.front: What parking access does an ordinary permanent placard grant — and what meter rules still apply?
sec18-card-r24.expected_back: An ordinary permanent placard allows accessible-space parking but does not waive meter fees or time limits.

sec18-card-r25.front: How long can a temporary disability placard last from the state versus a municipality, and does it waive meters?
sec18-card-r25.expected_back: A temporary disability placard lasts for the physician-certified period, up to six months if the state issues it or ninety days if a municipality issues it, and does not waive meter rules.

sec18-card-r26.front: When may an organization placard be used for accessible parking, and how do parking meters apply?
sec18-card-r26.expected_back: An organization placard supports free disability transportation and accessible-space use while transporting qualifying people, without waiving meter fees or limits.

sec08-card-f01.front: Who is included inside the Illinois handbook's pedestrian category?
sec08-card-f01.expected_back: The handbook’s pedestrian category includes people walking, skating in-line or riding skateboards, including people with physical, hearing or visual disabilities.

sec08-card-f02.front: How should drivers behave whenever people on foot are near the roadway?
sec08-card-f02.expected_back: Drivers should be ready to yield and avoid passing unnecessarily close to people on foot.

sec08-card-f03.front: What must a pedestrian do when crossing outside a marked or unmarked crosswalk?
sec08-card-f03.expected_back: A pedestrian crossing outside a marked or unmarked crosswalk must yield to drivers and should use an available pedestrian bridge or tunnel.

sec08-card-f04.front: Where should pedestrians walk first, and how must they walk if forced onto a two-way road?
sec08-card-f04.expected_back: A pedestrian should use a sidewalk or shoulder when available; when walking on a two-way roadway is necessary, face approaching traffic and stay away from the traveled edge.

sec08-card-f05.front: What rule applies to walking along a highway while impaired by alcohol or drugs?
sec08-card-f05.expected_back: Do not walk on a highway while impaired by alcohol or other drugs.

sec08-card-f06.front: What rights apply to a pedestrian using a guide dog, white cane, wheelchair, or assistive device?
sec08-card-f06.expected_back: A pedestrian using a guide dog, white cane, wheelchair or another assistive device has the same pedestrian rights and must receive the right of way.

sec08-card-f07.front: Which four route and awareness habits should walkers and joggers follow?
sec08-card-f07.expected_back: Walkers and joggers should use provided paths, choose wide shoulders when using roads, face traffic and look and listen for vehicles.

sec08-card-f08.front: What two precautions should walkers and joggers take at night or in poor visibility?
sec08-card-f08.expected_back: At night or in poor visibility, walkers and joggers should choose well-lit areas and wear reflective clothing.

sec08-card-f09.front: How do railway gates, bridge gates, and other safety barriers apply to pedestrians?
sec08-card-f09.expected_back: Pedestrians must comply with railway gates, bridge gates and other barriers.

sec08-card-f10.front: What Illinois rules govern hitchhiking in the roadway and soliciting along highways?
sec08-card-f10.expected_back: Standing in the roadway to hitchhike is illegal, and pedestrians should not solicit money or business on or beside a highway.

sec08-card-f11.front: Under what age, daylight, speed-limit, and traffic conditions may someone skate on a public road?
sec08-card-f11.expected_back: A person at least eighteen may skate on a public roadway from sunrise to sunset when its posted limit is forty-five miles per hour or lower and traffic is not obstructed.

sec08-card-f12.front: Where should drivers expect children near the road and prepare to slow down?
sec08-card-f12.expected_back: Watch for child-hazard locations such as schools, parks, playgrounds and bus stops, and prepare to slow where children are likely.

sec08-card-f13.front: What two driveway and play-area precautions help protect young children?
sec08-card-f13.expected_back: Use exceptional care while backing in a driveway near children, and keep children’s play away from streets, driveways and other hazardous areas.

sec08-card-f14.front: When should parents teach pedestrian rights and responsibilities to children?
sec08-card-f14.expected_back: Parents should teach pedestrian rights and responsibilities to children while they are young.

sec08-card-f15.front: How do a motorcycle's legal status and narrow profile affect traffic safety?
sec08-card-f15.expected_back: Motorcyclists share other road users’ rights and responsibilities, but their small size can make them difficult to detect and can lead drivers to underestimate their speed.

sec08-card-f16.front: How often should you expect motorcycles in traffic, and when must you check extra carefully?
sec08-card-f16.expected_back: Expect motorcycles in traffic throughout the year and check carefully before turning across their path.

sec08-card-f17.front: What must a left-turning driver do when an oncoming motorcycle approaches?
sec08-card-f17.expected_back: When turning left across opposing traffic, yield to motorcycles and wait until the rider’s intent is clear.

sec08-card-f18.front: When may a motorcyclist proceed through an unchanging red light, and what duty applies first?
sec08-card-f18.expected_back: A motorcycle rider may proceed after a red signal fails to change for one hundred twenty seconds, but must first yield to approaching traffic.

sec08-card-f19.front: How much of a traffic lane belongs to a motorcyclist, and may a car share beside it?
sec08-card-f19.expected_back: A motorcyclist is entitled to the entire lane and needs room to maneuver, so a car driver must not share that lane beside the motorcycle.

sec08-card-f20.front: How should you drive while a motorcyclist is overtaking your vehicle?
sec08-card-f20.expected_back: When a motorcycle passes, hold your speed and lane position and allow the rider to complete the pass and return to a proper position.

sec08-card-f21.front: What minimum time cushion and headlight rule apply when following a motorcycle?
sec08-card-f21.expected_back: Follow a motorcycle with a gap of at least three to four seconds, and dim headlights when following it as with other vehicles.

sec08-card-f22.front: How does a motorcycle's dry-pavement stopping distance compare to a car's, and what influences it?
sec08-card-f22.expected_back: On dry pavement a motorcycle can stop sooner than a car, although the rider’s training and experience affect stopping ability.

sec08-card-f23.front: How do wet or icy pavement and strong crosswinds affect a motorcycle?
sec08-card-f23.expected_back: Wet or icy surfaces reduce a motorcycle’s braking and maneuvering ability, while wind gusts can move it significantly across its lane.

sec08-card-f24.front: How can potholes, gravel, oil, debris, or rail tracks affect a motorcycle ahead of you?
sec08-card-f24.expected_back: Debris, potholes, oil, gravel and railway tracks can cause a motorcycle to change position or slow where a car might continue normally.

sec08-card-f25.front: How should you respond upon encountering a crash involving a motorcycle?
sec08-card-f25.expected_back: Use extreme caution and seek emergency medical help after a motorcycle crash.

sec08-card-f26.front: What defines an Illinois autocycle, and what paperwork and license does roadway operation require?
sec08-card-f26.expected_back: An autocycle has three wheels, a steering wheel and non-straddling seating; roadway use requires proper title and registration and a valid Illinois driver’s license.

sec08-card-f27.front: What roadway status do bicycles hold on most streets, and which assisted bikes are included?
sec08-card-f27.expected_back: On most roads, bicyclists have roadway rights and responsibilities, including the right of way; the handbook includes qualifying electric and gas-assisted bicycles in this comparison.

sec08-card-f28.front: May a driver travel, park, idle, or load passengers in an empty marked bicycle lane?
sec08-card-f28.expected_back: A designated bicycle lane cannot be used by a motor vehicle for travel, parking, idling or passenger pickup or drop-off even when no cyclist is present.

sec08-card-f29.front: Why should drivers stay alert beside a marked bicycle lane?
sec08-card-f29.expected_back: A cyclist may need to leave a bicycle lane, and drivers should be ready to move around the rider safely.

sec08-card-f30.front: In which direction do bicycles ride, and when might a rider move toward the center of the lane?
sec08-card-f30.expected_back: Bicycles travel with vehicle traffic, and hazards or a narrow lane may require a rider to move toward the lane’s center.

sec08-card-f31.front: When may cyclists ride two abreast, and when is riding more than two abreast banned?
sec08-card-f31.expected_back: Two cyclists may ride abreast if normal traffic is not impeded; more than two abreast is prohibited outside areas reserved for bicycles.

sec08-card-f32.front: How should you treat a cyclist's right-of-way and personal space on the road?
sec08-card-f32.expected_back: Yield to a cyclist as to another vehicle and never crowd or threaten the rider.

sec08-card-f33.front: How much passing clearance must Illinois drivers give a cyclist, how is it measured, and what if space is tight?
sec08-card-f33.expected_back: Pass a cyclist slowly with at least three feet measured from the vehicle’s side-mirror edge; if that space is unavailable, wait until passing can be done safely.

sec08-card-f34.front: What legal jeopardy can follow passing too close to a cyclist and causing a crash?
sec08-card-f34.expected_back: Passing too close to a cyclist and causing a crash may expose the driver to criminal charges.

sec08-card-f35.front: What three precautions apply when following behind a bicyclist?
sec08-card-f35.expected_back: When following bicycles, leave generous room, be ready to stop quickly and take extra care in bad weather.

sec08-card-f36.front: What headlight rule applies when meeting an oncoming bicyclist after dark?
sec08-card-f36.expected_back: Do not use high beams when meeting an oncoming cyclist at night.

sec08-card-f37.front: How must you handle oncoming cyclists or a cyclist ahead of you in a shared left-turn lane?
sec08-card-f37.expected_back: Before turning left, allow an opposing cyclist through; if sharing a left-turn lane with a cyclist, remain behind until the rider completes the turn.

sec08-card-r01.front: What must you do before turning right when a cyclist approaches on your right?
sec08-card-r01.expected_back: Before turning right, allow a cyclist approaching on the right to continue through the intersection and signal the intended turn.

sec08-card-r02.front: What check and hand habit help avoid striking a cyclist with a parked car's door?
sec08-card-r02.expected_back: Check for cyclists before opening a parked vehicle’s door, and consider reaching with the right hand to help look behind.

sec08-card-r03.front: What pedal requirement and motor wattage limit define a low-speed electric bicycle?
sec08-card-r03.expected_back: A low-speed electric bicycle has usable pedals and an electric motor rated below seven hundred fifty watts.

sec08-card-r04.front: Where may low-speed electric bicycles operate, where are they barred, and what can local towns restrict?
sec08-card-r04.expected_back: Low-speed electric bicycles may use authorized roads, bicycle lanes and paths but not sidewalks, and local authorities may prohibit them on local roads or paths.

sec08-card-r05.front: How does a Class One electric bicycle deliver motor help, and at what speed does it stop?
sec08-card-r05.expected_back: A Class One electric bicycle assists only while the rider pedals and ends assistance at twenty miles per hour.

sec08-card-r06.front: How does a Class Two electric bicycle differ from Class One, and where does its motor cut off?
sec08-card-r06.expected_back: A Class Two electric bicycle can propel itself using its motor, but its motor cannot engage when the bicycle reaches twenty miles per hour.

sec08-card-r07.front: What pedaling rule, speed figure, and minimum rider age apply to a Class Three electric bicycle?
sec08-card-r07.expected_back: The handbook’s Class Three electric-bicycle description requires pedaling for motor engagement, states assistance when reaching twenty-eight miles per hour, and requires a rider aged at least sixteen.

sec08-card-r08.front: What two markings must a scooter carry to be titled and registered in Illinois?
sec08-card-r08.expected_back: A scooter can be titled and registered in Illinois if it has a federal safety-certification label and a vehicle identification number.

sec08-card-r09.front: What traffic rules bind scooter and moped riders, and what equipment is required to carry a passenger?
sec08-card-r09.expected_back: Scooter and moped drivers must follow signs, signals and traffic laws, and carrying a passenger requires a passenger seat and footrest.

sec08-card-r10.front: How does a scooter's engine size around one hundred fifty cubic centimeters determine license class?
sec08-card-r10.memory_hook: Under one-fifty Class L, else M
sec08-card-r10.expected_back: An engine below one hundred fifty cubic centimeters places a scooter in the motor-driven-cycle category requiring a Class L motorcycle license; at least that displacement requires Class M.

sec08-card-r11.front: Which license covers a moped, and what engine-size and shifting limits apply to gas mopeds?
sec08-card-r11.expected_back: A moped may be driven with any valid Illinois driver’s license; a combustion-powered moped cannot exceed fifty cubic centimeters or require manual gear shifting.

sec08-card-r12.front: What weight, wheel, frame, and speed limits define a low-speed electric kick scooter?
sec08-card-r12.expected_back: A low-speed electric scooter weighs less than one hundred pounds, has two or three wheels, handlebars and a standing floorboard, and reaches no more than ten miles per hour using electric and human propulsion.

sec08-card-r13.front: What age, license, and local-permission rules govern operating a low-speed electric scooter?
sec08-card-r13.expected_back: A low-speed electric-scooter operator must be at least eighteen, needs no license and may use a road, trail or sidewalk only where the municipality or park district permits it.

sec08-card-r14.front: How many people may ride a low-speed electric scooter, and what lights or reflectors must it carry?
sec08-card-r14.expected_back: Only one person may ride a low-speed electric scooter, which needs a headlamp and a red rear reflector or lamp.

sec08-card-r15.front: Where should you position your car around a large truck or bus?
sec08-card-r15.expected_back: Stay clear of a large vehicle’s blind spots and keep a position its driver can see in the side mirrors.

sec08-card-r16.front: Why must you watch large-vehicle turn signals and leave open space on the right before a right turn?
sec08-card-r16.expected_back: Watch large-vehicle signals and allow wide turns, including a possible open space on the right just before a truck turns right.

sec08-card-r17.front: Why do large trucks and buses need extra space from surrounding cars?
sec08-card-r17.expected_back: Give large vehicles additional space because their weight and size affect stopping and maneuvering.

sec08-card-r18.front: Why must you dim high beams when following behind a large truck at night?
sec08-card-r18.expected_back: Dim headlights when following a truck at night because bright reflections in its large mirrors can blind its driver.

sec08-card-r19.front: How does the handbook suggest alerting a truck driver before passing, and how should you complete the pass?
sec08-card-r19.expected_back: The handbook suggests a headlight blink to notify a truck driver of a pass, especially at night, and advises finishing promptly rather than remaining beside the truck.

sec08-card-r20.front: What must you do on a four-lane highway when approaching a disabled vehicle flashing hazard lights?
sec08-card-r20.expected_back: On a four-lane highway, move away from a disabled vehicle showing hazard lights when a safe lane change is possible; otherwise slow down and keep the reduced speed until well beyond it.

sec08-card-r21.front: What rules govern pushing a disabled vehicle on a rural highway and clearing it?
sec08-card-r21.expected_back: Do not push a disabled vehicle along a rural highway except in an emergency, and remove it so it does not remain a hazard.

sec08-card-r22.front: What else must be cleared from the pavement when a damaged vehicle is removed?
sec08-card-r22.expected_back: Removing a damaged vehicle from the road also requires removal of its glass and other debris.

sec08-card-r23.front: What hitch hardware, spacing limit, and backup links are required when one vehicle tows another?
sec08-card-r23.expected_back: Towing one vehicle with another requires a drawbar, usually no more than fifteen feet between vehicles, and two connecting chains or cables.

sec08-card-r24.front: After how long on an interstate, expressway, or tollway may police tow an abandoned or disabled car at owner cost?
sec08-card-r24.expected_back: A disabled, unattended or abandoned vehicle must be removed promptly, and police may order towing at the owner’s expense after two hours on an interstate, expressway or toll road.

sec08-card-r25.front: What are the abandoned-vehicle towing time thresholds on non-expressway highways inside versus outside urban areas?
sec08-card-r25.expected_back: The handbook’s towing thresholds for a vehicle left on other highways are ten hours in an urban area and twenty-four hours outside an urban area.

sec08-card-r26.front: What top speed and paperwork requirements apply to a four-wheeled low-speed vehicle?
sec08-card-r26.expected_back: A low-speed vehicle’s maximum speed is twenty-five miles per hour, and it needs title and registration like other vehicles.

sec08-card-r27.front: Which posted speed limits allow low-speed vehicles on public streets?
sec08-card-r27.expected_back: A low-speed vehicle may use a street posted at thirty miles per hour or below unless the municipality prohibits it.

sec08-card-r28.front: Which seven control, glass, restraint, and mirror items must a low-speed vehicle carry?
sec08-card-r28.expected_back: Required low-speed-vehicle equipment includes a parking brake, steering wheel, tires, windshield, belts, a rearview mirror and an exterior driver-side mirror.

sec08-card-r29.front: What reflectors, lamp visibility distances, brake lights, and signals does a low-speed vehicle need?
sec08-card-r29.expected_back: A low-speed vehicle needs rear red reflectors at each side and the middle, a headlamp visible five hundred feet ahead, red rear lamps visible one hundred feet back, brake lamps and turn signals at both ends.

sec08-card-r30.front: Which vehicles creep slowly along rural roads, and what rear emblem marks them?
sec08-card-r30.expected_back: Expect farm equipment, construction equipment and animal-drawn vehicles to move slowly, and look for the orange slow-moving-vehicle emblem required on certain vehicles.

sec08-card-r31.front: What typical speed range do slow-moving vehicles travel, and what danger does that create?
sec08-card-r31.expected_back: Typical slow-moving-vehicle speeds of five to twenty miles per hour can cause a highway-speed driver to close the gap rapidly.

sec08-card-r32.front: What precautions must you take before overtaking slow-moving farm or construction equipment?
sec08-card-r32.expected_back: Stay well behind slow-moving equipment, expect wide turns or entry into unmarked drives and make sure its operator knows the intended pass before attempting it safely.

sec08-card-r33.front: From how far away in daylight must a slow-moving vehicle's high-mounted rear flashing amber light be visible?
sec08-card-r33.expected_back: When lighting is required, the slow-moving vehicle’s high-mounted rear flashing amber signal must be visible for five hundred feet in daylight.

sec08-card-r34.front: Which lane does slow traffic normally use, and why might wide equipment edge into the next lane?
sec08-card-r34.expected_back: Slow traffic uses the right lane except for passing or turning, and a wide slow vehicle may briefly enter an adjoining lane to avoid a roadside obstacle.

sec08-card-r35.front: Where must winter motorists watch for snowmobiles sharing or crossing the road?
sec08-card-r35.expected_back: Use additional care where snowmobile warning signs indicate possible roadway sharing in winter.

sec08-card-r36.front: Which public roads may horseback riders use, and how must they ride?
sec08-card-r36.expected_back: Horseback riders may use public roads other than controlled-access highways and most expressways, traveling with traffic and as far right as possible.

sec08-card-r37.front: Why must you never honk near horses or livestock, and how should you pass riders?
sec08-card-r37.expected_back: Avoid sounding the horn near horses or livestock because it may frighten them; approach or pass riders carefully and be ready to stop.

sec01-card-f01.question_text: What credential is needed to drive legally in Illinois, and what vehicle metric sets the required license class?
sec01-card-f01.teaching_text: Driving a rig heavier than your credential allows counts as operating out of class even when your plastic card is active.

sec01-card-f02.question_text: Which Illinois license class covers basic everyday passenger cars?
sec01-card-f02.teaching_text: Unlike states that label passenger cars Class C or Class E, Illinois assigns everyday cars to Class D.

sec01-card-f03.question_text: Under what conditions may a Class D driver operate a rental truck up to twenty-six thousand pounds inside Illinois?
sec01-card-f03.teaching_text: Hauling commercial freight or crossing state lines falls outside this personal-property moving exception.

sec01-card-f04.question_text: What safety-training step applies when using a Class D license for that personal-property rental truck exception?
sec01-card-f04.teaching_text: Large box trucks handle and brake nothing like sedans, so passing the rental counter's safety material is mandatory.

sec01-card-f05.question_text: Which five passenger-transport vehicle categories trigger special Illinois licensing requirements beyond a basic car license?
sec01-card-f05.teaching_text: Carrying schoolkids, seniors, religious groups, or paying app passengers adds background or permit rules beyond everyday driving.

sec01-card-f06.question_text: When did Illinois stop issuing Temporary Visitor Driver's Licenses, and what may formerly eligible applicants seek instead?
sec01-card-f06.teaching_text: Applicants who once used the visitor credential track now apply directly for a standard Illinois driver's license.
