sec01-card-f07.question_text: What is the general minimum age to earn an Illinois driver's license?
sec01-card-f07.teaching_text: While instruction permits can start earlier in driver ed, full licensing does not open before age sixteen.

sec01-card-f08.question_text: Which three major requirements must a sixteen- or seventeen-year-old finish to get an Illinois license?
sec01-card-f08.teaching_text: Skipping state-approved driver education, coming up short on practice hours, or missing any test blocks teen issuance.

sec01-card-f09.question_text: Who must sign a minor's consent affidavit if a parent or guardian cannot come along to the facility?
sec01-card-f09.teaching_text: Arriving alone without a properly signed minor consent affidavit stops an under-eighteen application at the counter.

sec01-card-f10.question_text: What training is required for a first-time applicant aged eighteen through twenty who never took high-school or commercial driver ed?
sec01-card-f10.teaching_text: Waiting until eighteen to apply does not skip classroom safety training unless you already finished approved teen driver ed.

sec01-card-f11.question_text: Which two commercial or paid-delivery driving jobs are off-limits to drivers under eighteen?
sec01-card-f11.teaching_text: Teen drivers under eighteen cannot take behind-the-wheel property delivery gigs or operate CDL-class rigs.

sec01-card-f12.question_text: Which passenger-carrying vehicles cannot be driven by anyone younger than twenty-one in Illinois?
sec01-card-f12.teaching_text: Illinois reserves high-occupancy for-hire vans, buses, senior shuttles, and child-care transport for drivers twenty-one and up.

sec01-card-f13.question_text: How long can a new Illinois resident drive on a valid out-of-state license after moving in?
sec01-card-f13.teaching_text: If your former state card expires two weeks after your move, that earlier expiration date beats the ninety-day window.

sec01-card-f14.question_text: What license lets a nonresident visitor legally drive while traveling through Illinois?
sec01-card-f14.teaching_text: Tourists and out-of-state travelers need only keep their home jurisdiction's license current and valid while visiting.

sec01-card-f15.question_text: How does Illinois treat out-of-state college students—and their spouses and kids—who hold valid home licenses?
sec01-card-f15.teaching_text: Attending an Illinois university does not force nonresident students or their immediate household to surrender home-state cards.

sec01-card-f16.question_text: Which driving credential rule applies to active-duty Armed Forces members and dependents living with them?
sec01-card-f16.teaching_text: Frequent duty-station moves do not require active service members or live-in spouses and children to re-license locally.

sec01-card-f17.question_text: How long after returning from overseas military duty can an Illinois resident and live-in family use a prior license deferral?
sec01-card-f17.teaching_text: Securing the deferral ahead of deployment gives returning service households roughly four months to renew comfortably.

sec01-card-f18.question_text: Who else serving overseas alongside the military qualifies for that same one-hundred-twenty-day return deferral?
sec01-card-f18.teaching_text: Illinois extends the same four-month return grace period to Armed Forces or Defense Department civilian households with prior deferrals.

sec01-card-f19.question_text: When can a federal employee or service member drive in Illinois without holding an Illinois driver's license?
sec01-card-f19.teaching_text: That exemption disappears the moment you hop into a personal car for off-duty errands.

sec01-card-f20.question_text: Which two temporary roadway equipment operations do not require an Illinois driver's license?
sec01-card-f20.teaching_text: Moving farm tractors short hops between barns and nearby fields or running temporary road machinery stays exempt.

sec01-card-f21.question_text: How soon after a legal name change must you apply for a corrected Illinois card, and what proof is needed?
sec01-card-f21.teaching_text: Don't confuse the thirty-day name-change window with the much shorter ten-day rule for address moves.

sec01-card-f22.question_text: Which exact name gets printed on an Illinois license or identification card?
sec01-card-f22.teaching_text: Nicknames or unrecorded aliases cannot be printed—only names backed by birth, marriage, Social Security, or court records.

sec01-card-f23.question_text: Within how many days of moving must you notify the Secretary of State, and which three channels work?
sec01-card-f23.teaching_text: Exam questions constantly pit the ten-day address deadline against the thirty-day name-change and ninety-day new-resident rules.

sec01-card-f24.question_text: Does reporting an address move automatically mail you a new card, or what does printing the new address take?
sec01-card-f24.teaching_text: Online address updates only refresh computer records, so getting updated plastic in your wallet requires an in-person trip.

sec01-card-f25.question_text: Which five personal details require acceptable documentary proof when applying for an Illinois license or ID?
sec01-card-f25.teaching_text: Leaving home missing even one of the five proof categories stalls your application at the document check desk.

sec01-card-f26.question_text: What handwriting check does the agency perform during verification, and does every visit need the same document count?
sec01-card-f26.teaching_text: First-time credentials demand broader document sets than simple replacements or corrections, while staff compare signatures every time.

sec01-card-f27.question_text: Along with giving a working mailing address and taking a photo, what must an applicant hand over?
sec01-card-f27.teaching_text: Illinois bars holding multiple active state credentials at once, so old permits, IDs, or licenses get turned in.

sec01-card-f28.question_text: Besides bringing acceptable identity documents, what else is still required to actually receive your credential?
sec01-card-f28.teaching_text: Perfect paperwork only clears identity check—you still have to pass applicable tests and pay the state fee.

sec01-card-f29.question_text: What identity details and how many Illinois residency documents does a first-time REAL ID application require?
sec01-card-f29.teaching_text: Bringing only one piece of address mail forces you onto a standard card instead of REAL ID.

sec01-card-f30.question_text: What extra paperwork do you need if your birth certificate or identity record shows an earlier legal name?
sec01-card-f30.teaching_text: Certified marriage, divorce, or adoption papers bridge the gap between your birth record and current legal surname.

sec01-card-r01.question_text: What proofs—and how many residency documents—does a first-time standard Illinois credential require?
sec01-card-r01.teaching_text: Notice the classic test contrast: a standard credential takes one residency proof while REAL ID demands two.

sec01-card-r02.question_text: Can a single acceptable document satisfy more than one identification-document category?
sec01-card-r02.teaching_text: Items like an unexpired passport or current license can check off birth date and signature boxes simultaneously.

sec01-card-r03.question_text: What proof does every duplicate or corrected card need, and when must you add residency proof too?
sec01-card-r03.teaching_text: Printing a brand-new street address on a replacement triggers residency verification on top of signature proof.

sec01-card-r04.question_text: Under what condition are you allowed to order a duplicate Illinois credential online?
sec01-card-r04.teaching_text: Any edit to your personal details requires an in-person document check rather than an online reprint.

sec01-card-r05.question_text: What kind of identification is required to change your name, birth date, Social Security number, or gender on a card?
sec01-card-r05.teaching_text: Staff need an unbroken paper trail connecting the existing state record directly to the updated detail.

sec01-card-r06.question_text: What must an applicant under age sixty bring to replace a stolen Illinois credential free of charge?
sec01-card-r06.teaching_text: Without an official police theft report, applicants under sixty pay the normal duplicate replacement fee.

sec01-card-r07.question_text: Do applicants older than sixty need a police report to get a free duplicate license or ID card?
sec01-card-r07.teaching_text: Illinois waives duplicate fees for cardholders past age sixty without requiring a police theft filing.

sec01-card-r08.question_text: Roughly how early are renewal notices sent, and what happens if no reminder ever reaches your mailbox?
sec01-card-r08.teaching_text: Blaming a lost reminder letter will not excuse an expired license ticket during a traffic stop.

sec01-card-r09.question_text: How early before expiration can you renew a two- or four-year license versus a one-year license?
sec01-card-r09.teaching_text: Shorter one-year senior credentials open renewal six months ahead instead of the full twelve-month window.
sec01-card-r09.must_match_memory_hook: Multi-year one year, annual six months

visual_sync.text_span: Multi-year one year, annual six months

sec01-card-r10.question_text: How long is an ordinary Illinois driver's license valid, and on what date does it expire?
sec01-card-r10.teaching_text: Most adult cards run four-year birthday cycles, though younger and older age brackets follow special terms.

sec01-card-r11.question_text: When does an Illinois driver's license issued to someone under twenty-one expire?
sec01-card-r11.teaching_text: Giving a ninety-day buffer past your twenty-first birthday lets you switch to a horizontal adult card smoothly.

sec01-card-r12.question_text: How often must Illinois drivers aged eighty-seven or older renew their driver's license?
sec01-card-r12.teaching_text: Annual check-ins starting at age eighty-seven ensure vision and behind-the-wheel skills remain safe.

sec01-card-r13.question_text: Which two channels handle standard license renewal, and what extra items go along with renewing?
sec01-card-r13.teaching_text: Safe-driver notices with a PIN unlock online renewal, while facility visits cover required tests, fees, and fresh photos.

sec01-card-r14.question_text: What must a renewal applicant provide if they cannot turn in their current license at the counter?
sec01-card-r14.teaching_text: When your prior plastic card is lost, staff verify handwriting proof to confirm you are the record holder.

sec01-card-r15.question_text: How many residency documents are needed if you update your address while renewing a standard card versus a REAL ID?
sec01-card-r15.teaching_text: Even at renewal, REAL ID keeps its stricter two-document address rule compared with one for a standard license.

sec01-card-r16.question_text: Which document set is needed at renewal when you lack your current card or request profile changes?
sec01-card-r16.teaching_text: Modifying records or renewing without your old card triggers full identity verification plus address proof if moving.

sec01-card-r17.question_text: What must a noncitizen show when renewing an Illinois REAL ID credential?
sec01-card-r17.teaching_text: Federal REAL ID rules tie card validity to active legal presence, requiring updated immigration proof at renewal.

sec01-card-r18.question_text: What temporary credential do you get at the facility after paying and passing tests, and how long is it good?
sec01-card-r18.teaching_text: Illinois no longer prints permanent plastic over the counter, so that ninety-day paper slip covers you until mail arrives.

sec01-card-r19.question_text: How is your permanent Illinois plastic card produced, and how soon does it usually arrive?
sec01-card-r19.teaching_text: Central security verification protects against counterfeit cards and delivers your plastic within roughly three weeks.

sec01-card-r20.question_text: Which two postal settings block delivery of your permanent Illinois license or ID card?
sec01-card-r20.teaching_text: Postal carriers return state security envelopes rather than forwarding them, so pause mail holds until your card arrives.

sec01-card-r21.question_text: What should you do if your permanent Illinois card still has not arrived fifteen business days after your visit?
sec01-card-r21.teaching_text: Following up right after fifteen business days catches returned mail before your ninety-day paper credential runs out.

sec01-card-r22.question_text: What arrest, prison, and license penalties can hit someone caught committing Illinois credential fraud?
sec01-card-r22.teaching_text: Fake ID schemes carry felony-level prison exposure up to five years plus a full year off the road.

sec01-card-r23.question_text: Which five false-information, fake-card, or document-sharing acts are listed as credential-fraud offenses?
sec01-card-r23.teaching_text: Even letting a friend borrow your genuine birth certificate or ID to apply in your name prosecutes you for fraud.

sec01-card-r24.question_text: Which four health or substance factors does an Illinois license application ask you to disclose?
sec01-card-r24.teaching_text: Answering medical and substance questions honestly helps determine whether safe driving requires follow-up clearance.

sec01-card-r25.question_text: When a physician's Medical Report is required, how soon after the doctor signs it must you turn it in?
sec01-card-r25.teaching_text: Letting a signed medical clearance sit past ninety days makes it stale and forces another doctor visit.

sec01-card-r26.question_text: How soon must you notify the Secretary of State after learning of a condition that could cause blackouts or loss of control, and what happens if you stay silent?
sec01-card-r26.teaching_text: Hiding a newly diagnosed seizure or fainting condition can get your driving privileges canceled outright.

sec01-card-r27.question_text: What violations and crashes go onto an Illinois driver's state record, including events outside Illinois?
sec01-card-r27.teaching_text: Interstate reporting compacts send out-of-state speeding or DUI convictions right back onto your Illinois history.

sec01-card-r28.question_text: What does Illinois do when an out-of-state driver commits an Illinois offense requiring immediate action?
sec01-card-r28.teaching_text: Visiting drivers cannot outrun serious Illinois offenses by crossing the border back to their home state.

sec01-card-r29.question_text: Through which three channels can a driver buy a copy of their Illinois driving record?
sec01-card-r29.teaching_text: Checking your own paid abstract confirms court supervisions, points, or driver-ed postings are recorded accurately.

sec02-card-f01.question_text: What three driver details, payment, and requester proof must accompany a written driving-record request?
sec02-card-f01.teaching_text: Leaving out the driver's license number or the requester's own ID stalls written abstract requests in processing.

sec02-card-f02.question_text: Starting at what age are Illinois applicants asked if they want to join the organ and tissue donor registry?
sec02-card-f02.teaching_text: Illinois lets sixteen- and seventeen-year-olds join the First Person Consent donor registry right when applying.

sec02-card-f03.question_text: What military service or discharge proof is required to add the veteran designation to an Illinois credential?
sec02-card-f03.teaching_text: Bringing official separation, retirement, Reserve, or National Guard paperwork verifies eligibility before the badge prints.

sec02-card-f04.question_text: How is voter registration handled during a standard Illinois credential application?
sec02-card-f04.teaching_text: Staff tell standard-card applicants whether their voter record is current and offer an easy update or registration option.

sec02-card-f05.question_text: What happens with voter registration when a REAL ID applicant proves United States citizenship?
sec02-card-f05.teaching_text: Notice the flip from standard cards: citizen REAL ID applicants get registered automatically unless they actively decline.

sec02-card-f06.question_text: How do license-facility voter registrations reach your local election office?
sec02-card-f06.teaching_text: Digital transmission through the state election board routes your application cleanly to your county or city authority.

sec02-card-f07.question_text: May a noncitizen register to vote while applying for an Illinois driver's license?
sec02-card-f07.teaching_text: Qualifying for an Illinois driving credential never confers United States voting eligibility, and false registration carries severe penalties.

sec02-card-f08.question_text: What affirmation details are needed to get a Gold Star Family designation on an Illinois credential?
sec02-card-f08.teaching_text: Naming the service member and confirming qualifying family relationship honors fallen military families accurately.

sec02-card-f09.question_text: For required male applicants aged eighteen through twenty-five, what does signing the credential application do regarding Selective Service?
sec02-card-f09.teaching_text: Your application signature automatically keeps you compliant with federal registration rules for financial aid and federal jobs.

sec02-card-f10.question_text: What helpful personal and health details can Illinois cardholders add to a confidential police and responder database?
sec02-card-f10.teaching_text: First responders arriving at a serious crash can immediately notify family and check critical medical or disability notes.

sec02-card-f11.question_text: How much is the Illinois instruction-permit application fee listed in the handbook?
sec02-card-f11.teaching_text: Paying that twenty-dollar permit fee up front also covers your first license if you earn it before the permit expires.

sec02-card-f12.question_text: What is the listed Illinois driver's-license fee for applicants aged eighteen through twenty?
sec02-card-f12.teaching_text: Because that young-adult license expires three months past twenty-one, the state charges five dollars instead of thirty.

sec02-card-f13.question_text: What license fee does the handbook list for adults aged twenty-one through sixty-eight?
sec02-card-f13.teaching_text: Thirty dollars is the standard four-year adult rate before discounted senior tiers begin at sixty-nine.

sec02-card-f14.question_text: What driver's-license fee applies to Illinois applicants aged sixty-nine through eighty?
sec02-card-f14.teaching_text: Starting at age sixty-nine, the four-year license fee drops sharply from thirty dollars down to five.

sec02-card-f15.question_text: How much is the Illinois driver's-license fee for ages eighty-one through eighty-six?
sec02-card-f15.teaching_text: Remember the clean senior step-down on fee questions: five dollars through eighty, two dollars through eighty-six, then free.

sec02-card-f16.question_text: Which age group is completely exempt from paying an Illinois driver's-license fee?
sec02-card-f16.teaching_text: Even though eighty-seven-plus drivers renew every single year with a road test, the state charges zero fee.

sec02-card-f17.question_text: How much does adding a noncommercial classification outside of renewal cost, and what is excluded from that table line?
sec02-card-f17.teaching_text: Upgrading noncommercial vehicle privileges mid-cycle costs five dollars, whereas commercial CDL tiers follow separate fee schedules.

sec02-card-r01.question_text: What fee does the Illinois handbook list for a school-bus permit?
sec02-card-r01.teaching_text: Watch that distinct four-dollar number on fee questions, since almost every other add-on or duplicate sits at five.

sec02-card-r02.question_text: How much extra does adding or renewing a motorcycle classification tack onto your regular license fee?
sec02-card-r02.teaching_text: Whether you add Class L or M initially or renew it later, five dollars stacks onto your base license cost.

sec02-card-r03.question_text: What are the initial Illinois identification-card fees across age brackets and for persons with disabilities?
sec02-card-r03.teaching_text: Minors pay five dollars and adults through sixty-four pay twenty, while seniors sixty-five-plus and people with disabilities pay zero.
sec02-card-r03.must_match_memory_hook: Five youth, twenty adult, seniors free

visual_sync.text_span: Five youth, twenty adult, seniors free

sec02-card-r04.question_text: What does a duplicate or corrected Illinois license or permit cost ordinarily, and what senior discounts apply?
sec02-card-r04.teaching_text: Replacement licenses mirror the senior age discounts: five dollars normally, two dollars at eighty-one to eighty-six, and free past eighty-seven.
sec02-card-r04.must_match_memory_hook: Five standard, two eighties, eighty-seven free

visual_sync.text_span: Five standard, two eighties, eighty-seven free

sec02-card-r05.question_text: What is the listed fee for a duplicate or corrected ninety-day temporary license or legacy visitor license?
sec02-card-r05.teaching_text: Even replacing a lost or typo-corrected ninety-day paper slip carries a five-dollar fee.

sec02-card-r06.question_text: When is replacing a lost or stolen Illinois license or permit free under age sixty versus at sixty and up?
sec02-card-r06.teaching_text: Notice the lost-versus-stolen split: under sixty needs a full police theft report, whereas sixty-plus gets lost cards free too.
sec02-card-r06.must_match_memory_hook: Police report under sixty, free sixty-plus

visual_sync.text_span: Police report under sixty, free sixty-plus

sec02-card-r07.question_text: How much does it cost to duplicate or correct a temporary ninety-day Illinois identification card?
sec02-card-r07.teaching_text: Temporary paper IDs cost five dollars to reprint or fix, matching temporary driver's licenses.

sec02-card-r08.question_text: What does a duplicate standard identification card cost under eighteen versus ages eighteen through sixty-four?
sec02-card-r08.teaching_text: Replacing a lost adult state ID costs twenty dollars—four times more than replacing a five-dollar driver's license.

sec02-card-r09.question_text: Which two situations waive the duplicate fee for an Illinois identification card?
sec02-card-r09.teaching_text: Bringing a full police report for theft—or simply being at least sixty for loss or theft—zeros out the ID fee.

sec02-card-r10.question_text: How much does a corrected Illinois identification card cost under eighteen, from eighteen through sixty-four, and at sixty-five-plus?
sec02-card-r10.teaching_text: Don't mix up adult ID prices: a lost duplicate costs twenty dollars, while correcting details drops to ten.
sec02-card-r10.must_match_memory_hook: Five youth, ten adult, sixty-five free

visual_sync.text_span: Five youth, ten adult, sixty-five free

sec02-card-r11.question_text: How much do active Armed Forces members and live-in spouses or children pay for duplicate licenses, permits, or IDs?
sec02-card-r11.teaching_text: Active-duty members and dependents living at home receive free duplicate replacements across all three Illinois credential types.

sec02-card-r12.question_text: Why does the handbook advise checking the agency website before visiting for exact credential fees?
sec02-card-r12.teaching_text: State lawmakers periodically revise statutory fees after handbooks go to print, making the website the freshest source.

sec02-card-r13.question_text: Even though duplicate TVDL fees still appear, what changed starting July first, two thousand twenty-four?
sec02-card-r13.teaching_text: Keep in mind that legacy table rows only cover existing cards—new applicants now pursue standard licenses.

sec02-card-r14.question_text: How can eligible Illinois drivers renew a valid license without visiting a facility?
sec02-card-r14.teaching_text: Clean-record drivers who qualify for Safe Driver Renewal save a facility trip by renewing straight through web services.

sec02-card-r15.question_text: Which age group can renew valid ID cards online, and what special ID rule applies at age sixty-five and up?
sec02-card-r15.teaching_text: Senior state IDs issued at sixty-five or older cost nothing and never expire, eliminating future renewals altogether.
sec02-card-r15.must_match_memory_hook: Online twenty-two to sixty-four, seniors nonexpiring

visual_sync.text_span: Online twenty-two to sixty-four, seniors nonexpiring

sec02-card-r16.question_text: Which three additional vehicle, record, or business tasks does the agency's website handle online?
sec02-card-r16.teaching_text: Ordering driving abstracts, renewing registration stickers, and submitting business documents online skips counter lines.

sec02-card-r17.question_text: How can customers reach the agency when they have questions or issues involving administrative hearings?
sec02-card-r17.teaching_text: Suspension or revocation reinstatement questions route directly to hearing specialists through the dedicated email desk.

sec03-card-f01.question_text: Which tests can a license application require, and which two tests are mandatory every time you get or renew a permit?
sec03-card-f01.teaching_text: While license renewals sometimes waive written or road tests, every permit issuance or renewal requires vision and written checks.

sec03-card-f02.question_text: How long does your application fee stay active, and how many tries at each exam does it cover?
sec03-card-f02.teaching_text: Missing a third attempt or letting twelve months pass requires paying a brand-new application fee.

sec03-card-f03.question_text: What events on your driving record can require you to take a written test, a driving test, or both?
sec03-card-f03.teaching_text: Picking up moving tickets or crash involvement removes safe-renewal waivers and brings back counter testing.

sec03-card-f04.question_text: Which three suspicious behaviors during a written test can prompt an examiner warning?
sec03-card-f04.teaching_text: Keeping study guides out, glancing at neighboring screens, or checking a watch or phone flags you immediately.

sec03-card-f05.question_text: What happens to your exam score and wait time if an examiner catches you cheating?
sec03-card-f05.teaching_text: Getting caught cheating wipes out your attempt on the spot and locks you out for a full month.

sec03-card-f06.question_text: How severe is the criminal penalty for taking any part of another person's Illinois license exam?
sec03-card-f06.teaching_text: Impersonating an applicant at a testing station is a crime carrying mandatory jail time of at least one week.

sec03-card-f07.question_text: What can happen to your application if you try to bribe or influence facility staff, driving schools, or examiners?
sec03-card-f07.teaching_text: Offering cash, gifts, or pressure to instructors or state examiners gives the agency grounds to refuse issuance.

sec03-card-f08.question_text: Instead of an on-site vision screening, what specialist report is accepted and how recent must it be?
sec03-card-f08.teaching_text: A Vision Specialist Report signed by an optometrist, ophthalmologist, or physician older than six months will be rejected.

sec03-card-f09.question_text: What is the minimum visual acuity standard in Illinois, with or without corrective lenses?
sec03-card-f09.teaching_text: Hitting twenty over forty—either naturally or wearing your prescription—qualifies you for nighttime as well as daytime driving.

sec03-card-f10.question_text: Which visual-acuity range restricts an Illinois driver to daylight driving only?
sec03-card-f10.teaching_text: Sight softer than twenty over forty up to twenty over seventy keeps you legal during daytime hours only.

sec03-card-f11.question_text: At least how many degrees of peripheral side vision are required to qualify in Illinois?
sec03-card-f11.teaching_text: Wide side awareness lets you spot cross-traffic, cyclists, and merging cars without staring away from your lane.

sec03-card-f12.question_text: What rule applies behind the wheel if you used glasses or contact lenses to pass the vision screening?
sec03-card-f12.teaching_text: Driving without required glasses or contacts violates your license restriction just like driving out of class.

sec03-card-f13.question_text: What extra steps apply to Illinois applicants who use telescopic lenses?
sec03-card-f13.teaching_text: Specialized bioptic or telescopic prescription setups undergo additional state vision checks before driving privileges issue.

sec03-card-f14.question_text: How often does the handbook require a renewal written test, and who gets excused from it?
sec03-card-f14.teaching_text: Keeping zero traffic convictions on your record earns a pass past the eight-year written retest.

sec03-card-f15.question_text: How does the basic written exam test your knowledge of road signs, signals, and markings?
sec03-card-f15.teaching_text: Knowing octagon, pennant, and diamond shapes lets you read snow-covered or faded signs instantly on the exam.

sec03-card-f16.question_text: Which two question styles and four safety topics appear on the Illinois written examination?
sec03-card-f16.teaching_text: Expect both multiple-choice and true-or-false items covering statutes, safe driving, crash avoidance, and required vehicle equipment.

sec03-card-f17.question_text: Where are the distinct exam rules for motorcycles, heavy trucks, and buses covered?
sec03-card-f17.teaching_text: Two-wheeled bikes and commercial rigs use dedicated study manuals tailored to air brakes, weight, or balance.

sec03-card-f18.question_text: Besides every brand-new driver, which renewal age group must always take a behind-the-wheel exam?
sec03-card-f18.teaching_text: Drivers turning or past age eighty-seven complete an annual behind-the-wheel check alongside their free renewal.

sec03-card-r01.question_text: What preparation does the handbook suggest for first-time drivers aged twenty-one or older before applying?
sec03-card-r01.teaching_text: Even though twenty-one-plus beginners are not forced into the six-hour teen-adult course, professional lessons speed up confidence.

sec03-card-r02.question_text: What licensing, equipment, and weight-class rules must your road-test vehicle satisfy?
sec03-card-r02.teaching_text: Showing up in a vehicle outside the weight class on your application stops the examiner from testing you.

sec03-card-r03.question_text: What coverage requirement must you prove for the car used on your driving exam?
sec03-card-r03.teaching_text: Examiners inspect current insurance proof before getting in—no active policy means no road test.

sec03-card-r04.question_text: What plate and sticker setup must an Illinois-registered test car display, and how are out-of-state cars judged?
sec03-card-r04.teaching_text: Missing a front Illinois license plate cancels your road test right in the parking lot.
sec03-card-r04.must_match_memory_hook: Both plates, current sticker, home rules

visual_sync.text_span: Both plates, current sticker, home rules

sec03-card-r05.question_text: Who has to drive the test vehicle into the licensing facility?
sec03-card-r05.teaching_text: Driving yourself to the test site alone without an active license or supervised permit violates the law before testing starts.

sec03-card-r06.question_text: Who may ride inside the car during the Illinois road test, and who is barred from tagging along?
sec03-card-r06.teaching_text: Family members, children, and pets must stay out of the cabin so the drive stays focused.

sec03-card-r07.question_text: What rule applies if you bring children or pets along to the facility on road-test day?
sec03-card-r07.teaching_text: Facility staff cannot babysit unattended kids or animals in the lobby while you are out testing.

sec03-card-r08.question_text: Who has to wear safety belts throughout the Illinois driving examination?
sec03-card-r08.teaching_text: Pulling out of the parking space before both front-seat belts click into place risks failing before hitting the street.

sec03-card-r09.question_text: What two on-road events trigger an automatic failure during the driving examination?
sec03-card-r09.teaching_text: Even if every parking maneuver looked crisp, running a stop sign or cutting off traffic ends the test instantly.

sec03-card-r10.question_text: What cabin checks and adjustments should you complete before putting the road-test car in motion?
sec03-card-r10.teaching_text: Adjusting mirrors, seat reach, and safety belt while parked shows the examiner safe pre-trip habits.

sec03-card-r11.question_text: How far, how fast, and where should you look during the road-test backing maneuver?
sec03-card-r11.teaching_text: Staring only at a backup camera or side mirror instead of turning your head right to look back loses points.

sec03-card-r12.question_text: How do you signal and position the car during the tested left-side alley turnabout?
sec03-card-r12.teaching_text: Signaling your left entry into the alley and backing cleanly into your proper travel lane avoids wrong-way deductions.
sec03-card-r12.must_match_memory_hook: Signal left in, back proper side

visual_sync.text_span: Signal left in, back proper side

sec03-card-r13.question_text: Which uphill and downhill tasks are graded as part of the Illinois road test?
sec03-card-r13.teaching_text: Examiners grade wheel angle and parking-brake setup when parking on hills plus smooth pull-outs without rolling.

sec03-card-r14.question_text: Which five traffic-rule and communication habits count toward road-test vehicle control?
sec03-card-r14.teaching_text: Smooth steering means little unless paired with crisp lane discipline, right-of-way awareness, and early turn signals.

sec03-card-r15.question_text: What two accessible-parking credentials does the agency issue as special services?
sec03-card-r15.teaching_text: Qualifying residents with mobility conditions can obtain either permanent vehicle plates or hangtag placards.

sec03-card-r16.question_text: Who can qualify for reduced license-plate renewal fees through the Benefit Access Program?
sec03-card-r16.teaching_text: Meeting Benefit Access income caps lowers annual registration sticker costs for seniors sixty-five-plus and residents with disabilities.

sec03-card-r17.question_text: How should a deaf or hard-of-hearing applicant arrange interpreter assistance for licensing?
sec03-card-r17.teaching_text: Scheduling interpreter support before your trip ensures smooth communication throughout counter checks and testing.

sec03-card-r18.question_text: Who can request an in-person oral written exam, and on which days of the week is it offered?
sec03-card-r18.teaching_text: Showing up on Friday or Saturday misses oral testing windows, which run in person Monday through Thursday.

sec04-card-f01.question_text: How many minimum classroom hours and instructor behind-the-wheel hours make up an approved Illinois driver-ed course?
sec04-card-f01.teaching_text: Test items often swap six and ten hours, so separate six instructor hours from your ten night-practice hours.

sec04-card-f02.question_text: What driver-education enrollment proof must a fifteen- through seventeen-year-old bring to get an instruction permit?
sec04-card-f02.teaching_text: Teens under seventeen years and three months cannot grab a permit without proof of current or upcoming driver ed.
sec04-card-f02.must_match_memory_hook: Enrolled now or starting thirty days

visual_sync.text_span: Enrolled now or starting thirty days

sec04-card-f03.question_text: For ages fifteen through seventeen, how long is an instruction permit valid, and how long must you hold it before licensing?
sec04-card-f03.teaching_text: Don't confuse the two-year card lifespan with the mandatory nine-consecutive-month holding period before licensing.

sec04-card-f04.question_text: At what exact age can an Illinois teen apply for an instruction permit without taking driver education?
sec04-card-f04.teaching_text: Nine months past seventeen and three months lands right on your eighteenth birthday when adult licensing opens.

sec04-card-f05.question_text: Which two exams are required for a permit, and how long do those passing scores stay good?
sec04-card-f05.teaching_text: Passing vision and written tests up front keeps those scores valid for the life of your unexpired permit.

sec04-card-f06.question_text: What school-led driving activity does your instruction permit authorize?
sec04-card-f06.teaching_text: Holding the active permit makes your six hours of on-street driving with a certified instructor legal.

sec04-card-f07.question_text: Outside driver-ed lessons, what age, license, experience, and seating rules apply to a permit supervisor?
sec04-card-f07.teaching_text: Even a twenty-one-year-old adult cannot supervise if they only earned their own license six months ago.

sec04-card-f08.question_text: Does finishing driver education let a permit holder drive solo, or what rule stays in place?
sec04-card-f08.teaching_text: Completing classroom and instructor hours never converts a permit into solo privileges—adult front-seat supervision continues.

sec04-card-f09.question_text: How many supervised practice hours—and how many at night—must an under-eighteen applicant complete beyond driver ed?
sec04-card-f09.teaching_text: Those fifty family-supervised hours—including ten after dark—stack on top of your six driver-ed car hours.

sec04-card-f10.question_text: How are Illinois licenses formatted visually for drivers younger than twenty-one?
sec04-card-f10.teaching_text: Vertical portrait cards with special underage markers let officers and clerks spot under-twenty-one status at a glance.

sec04-card-f11.question_text: Which documents, logs, and certificates must an applicant under eighteen bring on licensing day?
sec04-card-f11.teaching_text: Forgetting the signed fifty-hour driving log or minor consent sheet stalls licensing even after nine clean months.

sec04-card-f12.question_text: What additional paperwork rule applies when a young driver asks for a REAL ID license?
sec04-card-f12.teaching_text: Graduated licensing never relaxes federal REAL ID standards—teens still need citizenship proof and two residency documents.

sec04-card-f13.question_text: What must reach and post to your Illinois driving record before the facility can issue your teen license?
sec04-card-f13.teaching_text: Heading to the counter before your school transmits completion electronically forces a return trip once it posts.

sec04-card-f14.question_text: What happens if your birthday lands on a state spot-check date even after passing your school instructor's road test?
sec04-card-f14.teaching_text: Randomly selected birthdates audit cooperative testing quality, requiring a second behind-the-wheel run with a state examiner.

sec04-card-f15.question_text: When does a teen avoid paying an extra license-application fee when upgrading from an instruction permit?
sec04-card-f15.teaching_text: Finishing within your twenty-four-month permit window lets the initial twenty-dollar permit payment cover your license.

sec04-card-f16.question_text: What high-school course grades can exempt a student from taking the state facility road test?
sec04-card-f16.teaching_text: Earning an A or B across accredited classroom and behind-the-wheel driver ed unlocks cooperative school road testing.

sec04-card-f17.question_text: Whose two signatures must appear on a Cooperative Driver Testing Certificate after you pass the school road exam?
sec04-card-f17.teaching_text: Presenting a certificate signed only by the teacher—without a parent or guardian signature—gets rejected at the counter.

sec04-card-f18.question_text: When does a Cooperative Driver Testing Certificate expire, and can it ever be extended?
sec04-card-f18.teaching_text: Letting your instruction permit lapse voids the school road-test waiver permanently and sends you into facility testing.

sec04-card-f19.question_text: Which four exceptions allow a school dropout under eighteen to still receive the driver-education completion notation?
sec04-card-f19.teaching_text: Illinois ties teen licensing to staying in school unless you hold a GED, passed eight recent courses, enrolled alternatively, or got written consents.

sec04-card-f20.question_text: Whose written approvals are required to use the dropout-consent exception?
sec04-card-f20.teaching_text: Parental approval alone is not enough—the regional superintendent must also sign off in writing.

sec04-card-f21.question_text: Who has authority to waive dropout licensing restrictions when enforcing them hurts the student's best interest?
sec04-card-f21.teaching_text: School district leaders can grant hardship waivers when family work or special needs justify licensing.

sec04-card-f22.question_text: What course must a first-time eighteen- through twenty-year-old finish if they never held a license or took teen driver ed?
sec04-card-f22.teaching_text: Turning eighteen skips the fifty-hour parent log, yet Illinois still mandates six hours of adult safety coursework.

sec04-card-f23.question_text: What provider rule governs classroom or online six-hour adult courses, and what happens with uncertified courses?
sec04-card-f23.teaching_text: Buying a random cheap web course outside the Secretary of State's certified list wastes money and blocks your license.

sec04-card-f24.question_text: Which age span and how many progressive stages make up Illinois graduated licensing, and what governs moving up?
sec04-card-f24.teaching_text: Clean driving conduct moves teens smoothly from Permit to Initial to Full licensing, whereas violations freeze advancement.

sec04-card-r01.question_text: What are the Illinois nighttime driving curfews during the permit phase on weeknights versus weekends?
sec04-card-r01.teaching_text: Even with an adult riding shotgun, permit practice shuts down at ten Sunday-Thursday and eleven Friday-Saturday—or earlier locally.

sec04-card-r02.question_text: What minimum holding months, total practice hours, night hours, and coach age apply during the permit phase?
sec04-card-r02.teaching_text: Every piece—nine months held, fifty logged hours, ten after dark, and a licensed coach twenty-one-plus—is verified.
sec04-card-r02.must_match_memory_hook: Nine months, fifty hours, ten night

visual_sync.text_span: Nine months, fifty hours, ten night

sec04-card-r03.question_text: Which three types of violations or dispositions cannot appear during your nine-month permit phase?
sec04-card-r03.teaching_text: Even getting court supervision instead of a conviction resets or stalls your clean nine-month permit clock.

sec04-card-r04.question_text: How many passengers may ride in the front and back seats during the permit phase?
sec04-card-r04.teaching_text: Only your supervising coach sits up front while back-seat passengers cannot outnumber working safety belts.

sec04-card-r05.question_text: Until what age are Illinois drivers banned from all wireless phone use—even hands-free—and what is the lone exception?
sec04-card-r05.teaching_text: Notice the age trap: passenger caps end at eighteen, whereas the total Bluetooth and hands-free ban runs until nineteen.

sec04-card-r06.question_text: Which nighttime driving restrictions apply to sixteen- and seventeen-year-old initial license holders?
sec04-card-r06.teaching_text: Earning your initial solo license keeps the exact same weeknight ten o'clock and weekend eleven o'clock curfews.

sec04-card-r07.question_text: How many conviction-free months must an initial license holder log before turning eighteen, and what happens after a ticket?
sec04-card-r07.teaching_text: Picking up a conviction at seventeen and ten months pushes initial teen restrictions right past your eighteenth birthday.

sec04-card-r08.question_text: For the first twelve licensed months or until eighteen, how many passengers under twenty are allowed, and which relatives are exempt?
sec04-card-r08.teaching_text: Notice Illinois caps non-family riders under age twenty—not eighteen—while siblings, stepsiblings, and your children do not count.

sec04-card-r09.question_text: Once that initial twelve-month young-passenger window ends, what cabin seating limit still applies?
sec04-card-r09.teaching_text: Graduating past the one-friend cap still restricts occupancy to one front passenger and one belt per rear rider.

sec04-card-r10.question_text: What happens to age restrictions in the full eighteen-to-twenty phase, and which wireless rule still lingers at eighteen?
sec04-card-r10.teaching_text: Even on a clean full license at eighteen, Bluetooth or hands-free phone calls stay illegal until your nineteenth birthday.
sec04-card-r10.must_match_memory_hook: Age limits lift, under-nineteen phone stays

visual_sync.text_span: Age limits lift, under-nineteen phone stays

sec04-card-r11.question_text: Who can cancel a sixteen- or seventeen-year-old's Illinois driver's license at any time and for any reason?
sec04-card-r11.teaching_text: Because minor licensing depends on written parental consent, the adult who signed can pull that permission anytime.

sec04-card-r12.question_text: If a parent withdraws consent, when and how can the teen regain an Illinois license?
sec04-card-r12.teaching_text: Restoring driving privileges is never automatic—you must wait for fresh consent or turn eighteen, reapply, retest, and pay fees.

sec04-card-r13.question_text: How can a parent or guardian check an under-eighteen teen's driving record online without paying?
sec04-card-r13.teaching_text: Using the state-issued personal identification number lets parents monitor teen tickets or supervisions online for free.

sec04-card-r14.question_text: How can an under-twenty-one permit holder and parent verify online whether high-school driver ed has posted?
sec04-card-r14.teaching_text: Checking with your permit number before leaving home prevents showing up at the facility before your school grade posts.

sec04-card-r15.question_text: Which two family resources does the agency offer to help parents and teens agree on driving rules?
sec04-card-r15.teaching_text: Putting curfew, car-care, and passenger expectations in writing up front prevents family misunderstandings once solo driving begins.

sec04-card-r16.question_text: How is court supervision restricted for drivers under twenty-one, and what class must they complete to get it?
sec04-card-r16.teaching_text: Drivers under twenty-one cannot stack repeat court supervisions on serious tickets and must finish traffic safety school.

sec04-card-r17.question_text: Who must appear in court alongside a driver under eighteen seeking court supervision for a ticket?
sec04-card-r17.teaching_text: Minors cannot quietly mail in a fine for supervision—a parent or legal guardian has to stand before the judge too.

sec04-card-r18.question_text: How long can court supervision for certain alcohol offenses delay a minor's full graduated license?
sec04-card-r18.teaching_text: Even without an outright conviction, alcohol-related court supervision pushes full licensing back nine months.

sec04-card-r19.question_text: What happens to a driver under twenty-one convicted of two or more moving violations within twenty-four months?
sec04-card-r19.teaching_text: While older adults need three convictions inside twelve months, under-twenty-one drivers lose their license after just two inside two years.

sec04-card-r20.question_text: After a young-driver suspension, what extra class might reinstatement require, and are hardship permits guaranteed?
sec04-card-r20.teaching_text: Suspended young drivers often face remedial classes and reinstatement fees with zero guarantee of a work driving permit.

sec04-card-r21.question_text: For an under-twenty-one vehicle occupant caught with alcohol, what suspension hits for court supervision versus a conviction?
sec04-card-r21.teaching_text: Notice this hits any underage occupant—even a passenger—with three months off for supervision or at least six if convicted.

sec04-card-r22.question_text: What license penalty can hit an under-eighteen permit or initial-license driver caught breaking nighttime curfew?
sec04-card-r22.teaching_text: Driving past ten on weeknights or eleven on weekends risks losing your teen license, not just paying a fine.

sec04-card-r23.question_text: What licensing block can hit an under-eighteen driver charged after a serious-injury or fatal crash, even with zero alcohol?
sec04-card-r23.teaching_text: Pending charges from a severe injury or fatal crash let the state block issuing or renewing a minor's license.

sec04-card-r24.question_text: How does an unresolved court traffic ticket affect someone under eighteen applying for a license?
sec04-card-r24.teaching_text: Any open citation sitting in traffic court freezes teen license issuance until the case is resolved.

sec05-card-f01.question_text: Which four groups of officials must drivers obey when they direct traffic?
sec05-card-f01.teaching_text: Human traffic directors override normal signs and lights around crashes, roadwork, fires, and school crossings.

sec05-card-f02.question_text: How should you pull over for a police stop, and what if the right shoulder is unsafe?
sec05-card-f02.teaching_text: Slowing smoothly with your turn signal shows compliance while rolling ahead to a wide spot protects both you and the officer.

sec05-card-f03.question_text: What braking mistakes and hazardous locations should you avoid during a police traffic stop?
sec05-card-f03.teaching_text: Slamming the brakes in a live lane or stopping on bridges, curves, or beside barriers traps passing traffic.

sec05-card-f04.question_text: Once stopped for police, what should you do with your body and hands while waiting?
sec05-card-f04.teaching_text: Keeping both hands clearly visible on the steering wheel reassures the approaching officer that nobody is reaching for a weapon.

sec05-card-f05.question_text: Which side of your car might an officer approach, and when may you step out?
sec05-card-f05.teaching_text: Officers often walk up the passenger side to stay clear of fast highway lanes, and popping your door open looks confrontational.

sec05-card-f06.question_text: How should you handle retrieving your license or phone-based insurance proof during a traffic stop?
sec05-card-f06.teaching_text: Announcing that your wallet or phone is in a console or pocket prevents sudden movements from looking dangerous.

sec05-card-f07.question_text: Which three valid items are legally required to operate a motor vehicle in Illinois?
sec05-card-f07.teaching_text: Driving with any one of the big three missing or expired turns a routine stop into citations or worse.

sec05-card-f08.question_text: What should you do if you cannot confirm whether an unmarked vehicle pulling you over is real police?
sec05-card-f08.teaching_text: Driving below the speed limit with flashers on while dialing nine-one-one or heading somewhere populated shows good faith while protecting you.

sec05-card-f09.question_text: Is switching on your dome light appropriate during a nighttime police stop?
sec05-card-f09.teaching_text: Illuminating a dark cabin helps the officer see your hands clearly and lowers tension on dark roads.

sec05-card-f10.question_text: Does signing an Illinois traffic ticket mean you are pleading guilty?
sec05-card-f10.teaching_text: Refusing to sign gains nothing on the roadside, because your signature merely confirms you received the citation paperwork.

sec05-card-f11.question_text: Where should a disputed traffic ticket be argued, and how must you behave if arrested?
sec05-card-f11.teaching_text: Arguing on the shoulder never erases a citation, whereas traffic court gives you a formal judge hearing.

sec05-card-f12.question_text: What identifying details must an officer give on request, and how are misconduct concerns handled?
sec05-card-f12.teaching_text: Asking calmly for a name and badge number lets you report improper conduct later through official agency channels.

sec05-card-f13.question_text: What driver details must be recorded during every Illinois traffic stop, even without a ticket?
sec05-card-f13.teaching_text: Illinois transparency rules require officers to document every stop regardless of whether it ends in a warning or citation.

sec05-card-f14.question_text: What phone uses does Illinois ban behind the wheel, and at what age is hands-free allowed?
sec05-card-f14.teaching_text: Drivers under nineteen cannot even use Bluetooth or voice-activated calls while driving, making nineteen a top exam cutoff.

sec05-card-f15.question_text: When is an electronic earpiece legal while driving in Illinois, and how are hearing aids treated?
sec05-card-f15.teaching_text: Covering both ears blocks sirens and horns, so only a one-sided phone earpiece or medical hearing aid is legal.

sec05-card-f16.question_text: Even with legal hands-free gear, what does the Illinois handbook advise before placing a call?
sec05-card-f16.teaching_text: Phone conversations split mental attention away from traffic hazards even when both hands stay on the wheel.

sec05-card-f17.question_text: Does holding a phone in your hand on speakerphone count as legal hands-free driving?
sec05-card-f17.teaching_text: Holding the device four inches from your chin ties up a hand and earns the exact same handheld ticket.

sec05-card-f18.question_text: Are live video streaming, video calls, or scrolling social media legal while driving in Illinois?
sec05-card-f18.teaching_text: Glancing at live video feeds or group calls pulls your eyes completely off brake lights ahead.

sec05-card-f19.question_text: Under which three specific situations may a driver legally use a handheld phone?
sec05-card-f19.teaching_text: Sitting at an ordinary red traffic light is not an exception, whereas reporting emergencies or sitting in Park during a blockage is.

sec05-card-f20.question_text: Beyond a traffic fine, what severe legal consequences can follow a distracted-driving crash?
sec05-card-f20.teaching_text: Hurting another road user while looking at a phone can escalate from a civil ticket straight to criminal prosecution and prison.

sec05-card-f21.question_text: Who must wear a safety belt in Illinois, and do air bags change that rule?
sec05-card-f21.teaching_text: Front and back seats alike require belts from age eight upward, while younger riders need proper child restraints.

sec05-card-f22.question_text: Who must buckle and adjust the seat belt if a passenger's medical condition or disability prevents them?
sec05-card-f22.teaching_text: Before shifting out of Park, the driver must step in and adjust restraints for anyone physically unable to do it alone.

sec05-card-f23.question_text: Who holds legal responsibility for making sure every passenger obeys Illinois belt and child-restraint laws?
sec05-card-f23.teaching_text: Unbuckled friends in the back seat put legal responsibility squarely on the person behind the wheel.

sec05-card-f24.question_text: Where across your body should the lap portion of a seat belt rest?
sec05-card-f24.teaching_text: Wearing a lap strap high over your soft stomach can cause severe internal organ injuries during crash deceleration.

sec05-card-f25.question_text: How should your shoulder belt fit, and which two shortcuts must you never take?
sec05-card-f25.teaching_text: Tucking the strap behind your back or under your arm lets your upper body slam forward or crush ribs in a wreck.

sec05-card-f26.question_text: How are air bags designed to work in relation to safety belts?
sec05-card-f26.teaching_text: Without a belt holding you in position, your body flies into an inflating bag at explosive speed.

sec05-card-f27.question_text: How many inches of space does the handbook recommend between the driver and the steering-wheel air bag?
sec05-card-f27.teaching_text: Sitting at least ten inches back gives the air bag room to inflate fully before cushioning short, older, or pregnant drivers.

sec05-card-f28.question_text: How should front-seat passengers adjust their seat relative to the dashboard air bag?
sec05-card-f28.teaching_text: Maximizing distance from the dash with a slight recline if needed softens impact if the front bag deploys.

sec05-card-f29.question_text: Up through what age does the Illinois handbook recommend securing children in the back seat, and why?
sec05-card-f29.teaching_text: Front air bags deploy at adult chest height and force, which can severely or fatally injure children twelve and younger.

sec05-card-f30.question_text: What two steps are required if a child under eight has no choice except riding ahead of an active air bag?
sec05-card-f30.teaching_text: When a pickup truck or full back row leaves no rear spot, sliding the seat all the way back adds vital air-bag buffer.

sec05-card-f31.question_text: May a rear-facing infant seat ever be placed in front of an active air bag?
sec05-card-f31.teaching_text: A rear-facing shell sits inches from the dash, where an inflating bag strikes the back of the baby's head with lethal force.

sec05-card-f32.question_text: Until what age must children use a child restraint, and what belt type must pair with a booster seat?
sec05-card-f32.teaching_text: A belt-positioning booster cannot hold a child upright on its own without both lap and shoulder straps routing across them.

sec05-card-f33.question_text: When may a child ride in the back seat using only a lap belt without a booster?
sec05-card-f33.teaching_text: Older cars lacking rear shoulder straps get a narrow exception once the child weighs above forty pounds.

sec05-card-f34.question_text: Until what age, weight, or height must Illinois children ride in a rear-facing restraint?
sec05-card-f34.teaching_text: Supporting a toddler's fragile neck rear-facing until age two or the forty-pound or forty-inch threshold drastically cuts spinal trauma.

sec05-card-f35.question_text: When is driving the maximum limit appropriate, and what limits how slowly you may drive?
sec05-card-f35.teaching_text: Speed laws cut both ways by banning full speed in slick weather and banning creeping slowly enough to impede normal flow.

sec05-card-f36.question_text: What is the default Illinois speed limit on rural interstates and tollways when no other limit is posted?
sec05-card-f36.teaching_text: Memorize Illinois's top statutory tier of seventy for unposted interstates and toll roads before urban reductions kick in.

sec05-card-f37.question_text: What default speed limit applies on an Illinois four-lane highway unless signs state otherwise?
sec05-card-f37.teaching_text: Don't mix up seventy-mile-per-hour interstates with non-interstate four-lane highways, which cap five miles lower at sixty-five.

sec05-card-r01.question_text: What is the default Illinois speed limit on other highways and rural roads without posted signs?
sec05-card-r01.teaching_text: Two-lane country highways have driveways, farm equipment, and undivided oncoming lanes that cap default speed at fifty-five.

sec05-card-r02.question_text: Unless posted otherwise, what default speed limit governs Illinois cities and towns?
sec05-card-r02.teaching_text: Sidewalks, parked cars, and frequent cross streets make thirty miles per hour the standard urban baseline across Illinois.

sec05-card-r03.question_text: What is the default maximum speed inside an Illinois alley unless another limit is posted?
sec05-card-r03.teaching_text: Blind garage doors, trash bins, and pedestrians stepping straight into narrow lanes require a crawl of fifteen or slower.

sec05-card-r04.question_text: What speed limit, hours, and conditions apply in a posted Illinois school zone?
sec05-card-r04.teaching_text: Illinois's school-zone test favorite requires all three triggers together on school days from six-thirty morning until four afternoon with children present.

sec05-card-r05.question_text: Can cities or counties set speed limits that differ from Illinois's statutory defaults?
sec05-card-r05.teaching_text: Statutory defaults only fill in unposted stretches, so always obey local speed plaques when towns raise or lower a corridor.

sec05-card-r06.question_text: Which road features and changing conditions require slowing below normal cruising speed?
sec05-card-r06.teaching_text: Blind crests, tight bends, narrow roads, foul weather, and heavy foot traffic shrink your sight distance faster than dry straightaways.

sec05-card-r07.question_text: What five safety duties apply when approaching or driving through an Illinois construction zone?
sec05-card-r07.teaching_text: Combining lower speed, zero handheld wireless use, yielding to crews, and moving a lane away keeps roadside workers alive.

sec05-card-r08.question_text: Does a posted Illinois work-zone speed limit still apply at midnight when no workers are on site?
sec05-card-r08.teaching_text: Shifted barriers and uneven lanes stay hazardous overnight, so work-zone speed limits enforce every hour until you clear the zone.

sec05-card-r09.question_text: What physical roadway changes show up inside work zones, and when must you slow even further?
sec05-card-r09.teaching_text: Pinched barrels, sharp pavement lip drop-offs, and heavy rigs leave tiny steering margins, demanding extra slowing around live workers.

sec05-card-r10.question_text: What must you do when approaching a stationary emergency or maintenance vehicle flashing warning lights?
sec05-card-r10.teaching_text: Vacating the adjacent lane and easing speed creates a lifesaving buffer for troopers, tow operators, and highway crews on the shoulder.

sec05-card-r11.question_text: How must you pass a stopped emergency scene if heavy traffic makes changing lanes impossible?
sec05-card-r11.teaching_text: Never force a dangerous sideswipe into occupied lanes; instead drop speed significantly and hold it until completely past every responder.
sec05-card-r11.must_match_memory_hook: Cannot move over, slow way down

visual_sync.text_span: Cannot move over, slow way down

sec05-card-r12.question_text: Within what distance of an emergency scene does Illinois restrict taking photos or using wireless phones?
sec05-card-r12.teaching_text: Rubbernecking to film a crash takes eyes off brake lights and flaggers right where lanes bottleneck around responders.
sec05-card-r12.must_match_memory_hook: No phones within five hundred feet

visual_sync.text_span: No phones within five hundred feet

sec05-card-r13.question_text: How must you react when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights or a siren?
sec05-card-r13.teaching_text: Clearing toward the right curb promptly opens a predictable center corridor for high-speed ambulances and fire engines.

sec05-card-r14.question_text: What should you do if an emergency vehicle approaches while you are already stopped at a two-way intersection?
sec05-card-r14.teaching_text: Trying to pull forward into a busy two-way box to make room often blocks the exact turn path the ambulance needs.

sec05-card-r15.question_text: When, if ever, may you drive your vehicle across a fire hose laid on the street?
sec05-card-r15.teaching_text: Crushing a pressurized supply line cuts water pressure instantly to firefighters working inside a burning building.

sec05-card-r16.question_text: How do vehicles in an Illinois funeral procession identify themselves, and who gets right-of-way?
sec05-card-r16.teaching_text: Letting the entire lit procession clear intersections intact prevents separating family cars traveling together.

sec05-card-r17.question_text: What three maneuvers are prohibited around an organized funeral procession?
sec05-card-r17.teaching_text: Slicing between cars, sneaking in for red-light priority, or overtaking without a dedicated passing lane breaks Illinois law.

sec05-card-r18.question_text: What vehicle penalty can a local town impose on a driver who recklessly interferes with a funeral procession?
sec05-card-r18.teaching_text: Municipalities have authority to tow and impound cars whose drivers aggressively disrupt a funeral cortege.

sec05-card-r19.question_text: After coming to a full stop for an allowed right turn on red, which three road users must you yield to?
sec05-card-r19.teaching_text: Scanning only for oncoming cars misses cyclists in the curb lane and pedestrians stepping off the right corner.

sec05-card-r20.question_text: Where in priority order must you halt at a stop sign or flashing red light?
sec05-card-r20.teaching_text: Follow the painted bar first, then before the crosswalk, or finally at the point with a clear view if nothing is painted.

sec05-card-r21.question_text: Under what street layout and duties is a left turn on red permitted in Illinois?
sec05-card-r21.teaching_text: Turning left on red is legal only between two one-way streets where cross traffic flows left, after a complete stop and yield.

sec05-card-r22.question_text: Who goes first at a four-way stop, and how are ties broken between different roads?
sec05-card-r22.teaching_text: Rewarding the first full stop and giving ties to the right-side driver prevents simultaneous launches.

sec05-card-r23.question_text: At an intersection with no signs or lights, who yields when two cars arrive from different streets together?
sec05-card-r23.teaching_text: Approaching an unsigned residential crossroad demands easing speed early and yielding to anyone arriving on your right.

sec05-card-r24.question_text: What must you do before entering an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow arrow?
sec05-card-r24.teaching_text: Flashing yellow means opposing lanes hold green, so wait behind the conflict zone until both traffic and crosswalks clear.

sec05-card-r25.question_text: Who must a left-turning driver yield to, and what happens if the light turns red after entering on green?
sec05-card-r25.teaching_text: If you lawfully pulled into the intersection on green waiting for oncoming cars, complete your turn safely once traffic stops for red.

sec05-card-r26.question_text: How does your required action at a merge sign differ from your duty at a yield sign?
sec05-card-r26.teaching_text: Merge zones call for blending smoothly to match highway flow, whereas yield triangles require slowing or stopping completely to prevent conflict.

sec05-card-r27.question_text: Does a fresh green light let you pull into vehicles still clearing the intersection?
sec05-card-r27.teaching_text: Launching the instant your light turns green causes crashes with late-clearing left turners or cross traffic.

sec05-card-r28.question_text: What two steps are mandatory before pulling onto a street from a driveway, alley, building, or private road?
sec05-card-r28.teaching_text: Rolling out of parking garages or alleys without a full halt surprises both sidewalk walkers and fast curb-lane traffic.

sec05-card-r29.question_text: Who must yield at an unsigned T-intersection where one street dead-ends into a continuing road?
sec05-card-r29.teaching_text: Drivers on the terminating stem must turn, so traffic continuing straight along the top bar of the T gets priority.

sec05-card-r30.question_text: When must you hold back even if your signal is green at an intersection or marked crosswalk?
sec05-card-r30.teaching_text: Pulling into backed-up traffic traps your tail inside the box or across the crosswalk after the light changes.

sec05-card-r31.question_text: What action is required for someone in a marked crosswalk or children near a school-zone crosswalk on school days?
sec05-card-r31.teaching_text: Illinois requires a complete stop rather than a slow roll around occupied marked crosswalks and active school crossings.

sec05-card-r32.question_text: When must you yield to a pedestrian crossing in an unmarked crosswalk at an unsignalized corner?
sec05-card-r32.teaching_text: Even without white stripes, anyone walking across your side of an unsignalized street holds legal right-of-way.

sec05-card-r33.question_text: Must you still yield to pedestrians when turning after a stop sign, flashing red, or red light?
sec05-card-r33.teaching_text: Completing your mandatory vehicle stop never clears you to cut off someone stepping across your destination street.

sec05-card-r34.question_text: Who keeps right-of-way if a pedestrian started crossing legally before the traffic signal changed?
sec05-card-r34.teaching_text: Slower walkers caught mid-street when your light turns green keep full priority until they reach the curb.

sec05-card-r35.question_text: How must you treat pedestrians at alleys, driveways, building exits, and flashing-yellow-arrow corners?
sec05-card-r35.teaching_text: Curb cuts and permissive turn arrows cross live pedestrian paths where walkers expect turning cars to wait.

sec05-card-r36.question_text: Which categories of pedestrian disabilities specifically receive right-of-way protection from Illinois drivers?
sec05-card-r36.teaching_text: A walker may not hear your engine, spot your turn signal, or move quickly, demanding patience and full yielding.

sec06-card-f01.question_text: What must you confirm about the oncoming lane before passing on a two-lane road?
sec06-card-f01.teaching_text: Pulling into the opposing lane without clear long-range sightlines turns an ordinary pass into a head-on trap.

sec06-card-f02.question_text: What mirror cue and oncoming-car distance tell you when to finish returning to the right lane?
sec06-card-f02.teaching_text: Cutting back before seeing both headlights in your rearview clips their bumper, while waiting past two hundred feet crowds oncoming traffic.

sec06-card-f03.question_text: What speed rule applies to your vehicle while another driver is passing you?
sec06-card-f03.teaching_text: Accelerating alongside an overtaking car traps them out in the oncoming lane far longer than they judged.

sec06-card-f04.question_text: Is flashing your turn signal to wave a trailing driver past you legal in Illinois?
sec06-card-f04.teaching_text: Turn signals exist solely to announce your own turns or lane moves, never to vouch for oncoming clearance.

sec06-card-f05.question_text: May you ever drive off the pavement or main traveled roadway to pass on either side?
sec06-card-f05.teaching_text: Gravel edges and soft shoulders grab right-side tires unpredictably and kick debris or spin your car back across traffic.

sec06-card-f06.question_text: How much side clearance must you leave when passing someone walking on the road or shoulder?
sec06-card-f06.teaching_text: Mirror overhang and wind blast from a passing car easily clip someone walking along an uncurbed rural shoulder.

sec06-card-f07.question_text: What minimum clearance applies when passing a bicycle, even if the rider is on a shoulder or bike lane?
sec06-card-f07.teaching_text: Painted bike stripes never create a physical wall, so Illinois still requires a full three-foot cushion around every rider.

sec06-card-f08.question_text: When may an ordinary driver legally pass on the right, and what surface remains off-limits?
sec06-card-f08.teaching_text: You may pass a left-turning car or use multi-lane or one-way streets only when full paved lane width exists without touching the shoulder.

sec06-card-f09.question_text: Which pavement marking and roadside sign forbid passing on a two-lane two-way road?
sec06-card-f09.teaching_text: Engineers paint solid yellow stripes and post pennants where sight distance drops below safe overtaking range.

sec06-card-f10.question_text: Why must you stay in your lane on hills and curves along a two-lane two-way road?
sec06-card-f10.teaching_text: Crests and bends hide oncoming vehicles closing at combined highway speed with nowhere for either car to escape.

sec06-card-f11.question_text: Within what distance of an intersection or railroad crossing is passing banned on a two-lane two-way road?
sec06-card-f11.teaching_text: Cars turning out of cross streets or braking for tracks create sudden conflicts inside the final hundred feet.

sec06-card-f12.question_text: When does approaching a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel trigger a hundred-foot no-passing rule?
sec06-card-f12.teaching_text: Abutments, tunnel mouths, and narrow bridge walls cut off visibility and eliminate shoulder escape room.

sec06-card-f13.question_text: Which two stopped vehicles must you never overtake at a crossing or roadside stop?
sec06-card-f13.teaching_text: Pulling around a halted car at a crosswalk or a loading school bus puts you straight into hidden pedestrians or children.

sec06-card-f14.question_text: How does Illinois treat passing inside construction zones and school zones?
sec06-card-f14.teaching_text: All Illinois roadwork areas plus unincorporated and posted municipal school zones ban overtaking to protect crews and students.

sec06-card-f15.question_text: Which half of the roadway do drivers generally use, and what common situations create exceptions?
sec06-card-f15.teaching_text: Keeping right separates opposing streams except during lawful passing, one-way travel, marked multi-lane setups, or directed detours.

sec06-card-f16.question_text: What must you do before steering left of center to get around an obstruction in your lane?
sec06-card-f16.teaching_text: Having a fallen branch or stalled car in your lane never forces oncoming drivers to yield their half of the road.

sec06-card-f17.question_text: Is crossing the centerline allowed when turning left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway?
sec06-card-f17.teaching_text: Illinois explicitly carves out midblock left turns into and out of alleys and driveways from the keep-right rule.

sec06-card-f18.question_text: Which stopped vehicles or roadside conditions justify moving left away from the right lane?
sec06-card-f18.teaching_text: Giving wide berth to emergency responders, disabled cars, or shoulder roadwork keeps workers out of mirror range.

sec06-card-f19.question_text: What is the primary purpose of the left lane on Illinois interstates, and when may you stay in it?
sec06-card-f19.teaching_text: Left freeway lanes exist for overtaking unless nobody trails behind you or traffic, weather, hazards, or emergency vehicles require it.

sec06-card-f20.question_text: Which lane should slower traffic stay in, and what two maneuvers allow leaving it?
sec06-card-f20.teaching_text: Camping below traffic speed in inner lanes forces faster drivers to pass on the right unless you are overtaking or turning left.

sec06-card-f21.question_text: Is darting back and forth between lanes to move faster than surrounding traffic legal?
sec06-card-f21.teaching_text: Slaloming through tight highway gaps cuts off braking buffers and surprises drivers checking mirrors.

sec06-card-f22.question_text: Who is exempt from following the posted arrow direction on an Illinois one-way street?
sec06-card-f22.teaching_text: Civilian drivers must always follow ONE WAY signs, while active emergency rigs using lights or sirens can counter-flow to reach scenes.

sec06-card-f23.question_text: May you drive across an unpaved median strip or median barrier on a divided road?
sec06-card-f23.teaching_text: Cutting across grass medians risks bogging tires or rolling into fast opposing lanes.

sec06-card-f24.question_text: Where are you legally allowed to get onto or off a controlled-access highway?
sec06-card-f24.teaching_text: Controlled-access expressways ban makeshift shoulder cutoffs so merges happen strictly at engineered ramps.

sec06-card-f25.question_text: Where is backing up completely banned, and when is reversing legal on ordinary streets?
sec06-card-f25.teaching_text: Backing on an expressway lane or shoulder invites high-speed rear-end crashes, while local backing is legal only when clear.

sec06-card-f26.question_text: When may you open a vehicle door on the traffic side, and how long can it stay open?
sec06-card-f26.teaching_text: Leaving a street-side door swung open blocks bike lanes and travel lanes longer than needed to hop in or out.

sec06-card-f27.question_text: Which hand does the Illinois handbook recommend using to open your driver-side door, and why?
sec06-card-f27.teaching_text: Reaching across your chest with your far hand naturally pivots your head toward approaching cyclists and cars.

sec06-card-f28.question_text: How does Illinois law treat street sideshows that block traffic for stunts or speed contests?
sec06-card-f28.teaching_text: Shutting down intersections for donuts, exhibitions, or unauthorized drag races violates Illinois traffic statutes.

sec06-card-f29.question_text: How far ahead must you signal continuously in business or residential districts versus other roads?
sec06-card-f29.teaching_text: Faster rural and highway speeds cover ground twice as quickly, doubling your advance blinker requirement from one hundred to two hundred feet.

sec06-card-f30.question_text: Which electric turn signal must you activate before making a turn?
sec06-card-f30.teaching_text: Signaling the wrong way or forgetting to cancel an old blinker misleads waiting cross-street drivers into pulling out.

sec06-card-r01.question_text: How do you signal a right turn, left turn, and slow or stop using your left arm?
sec06-card-r01.teaching_text: Every hand signal uses your left arm out the window so trailing drivers can read turns or braking when a bulb burns out.

sec06-card-r02.question_text: How should you position, signal, yield, and scan when starting a right turn?
sec06-card-r02.teaching_text: Setting up in the proper curb lane while yielding to walkers and checking left-side cross traffic keeps right turns crisp.

sec06-card-r03.question_text: How close to the curb should you track during a right turn, and which lane do you enter?
sec06-card-r03.teaching_text: Swinging wide into outer lanes during a right turn clips cars legally turning left from the opposite approach.

sec06-card-r04.question_text: Which two road users need extra attention around right-turn corners?
sec06-card-r04.teaching_text: Large buses and semis swing wide to clear curbs, while cyclists ride straight up right-side bike lanes beside turning cars.

sec06-card-r05.question_text: What signaling, yielding, and scanning steps are required before making a left turn?
sec06-card-r05.teaching_text: Left turns cross oncoming lanes and crosswalks simultaneously, requiring a full scan of every approach before committing.

sec06-card-r06.question_text: How should your front wheels point while waiting to turn left, and which lane should you finish in?
sec06-card-r06.teaching_text: Pre-angling your tires left means a rear-end tap shoves your car straight into oncoming traffic.

sec06-card-r07.question_text: What head check is required before shifting from a right lane into a left lane?
sec06-card-r07.teaching_text: Side mirrors leave a blind pocket off your rear quarter panel that only a quick head turn catches.

sec06-card-r08.question_text: What sequence of head check and signaling applies before moving into a right-hand lane?
sec06-card-r08.teaching_text: Passenger-side blind spots are wider than driver-side ones, making a right-shoulder glance before sliding over essential.

sec06-card-r09.question_text: How many feet of clear visibility are required for a U-turn near a curve or hill, and can towns ban them?
sec06-card-r09.teaching_text: Swinging around near a crest or bend takes several seconds, requiring five hundred feet of clear view in every direction.

sec06-card-r10.question_text: What can flashing both turn signals simultaneously warn other drivers about?
sec06-card-r10.teaching_text: Dual amber flashers alert approaching drivers from afar that your vehicle is stationary or having mechanical trouble.

sec06-card-r11.question_text: Which two kinds of left-turn maneuvers is a shared two-way left-turn lane built to handle?
