sec06-card-r11.teaching_text: Shared center lanes let drivers turn left into or out of driveways as well as approach corners without blocking through traffic.

sec06-card-r12.question_text: What three temporary guides must you watch closely when turning or changing lanes inside roadwork?
sec06-card-r12.teaching_text: Construction shifts lanes away from familiar permanent stripes, so cones, temporary signs, and fresh markings govern.

sec06-card-r13.question_text: Which way does roundabout traffic circulate around the center island, and can roundabouts have multiple lanes?
sec06-card-r13.teaching_text: Every rotary flows counterclockwise to the right of the center island, whether designed with one lane or several.

sec06-card-r14.question_text: Who must drivers yield to when entering or exiting a roundabout?
sec06-card-r14.teaching_text: Both entry and exit legs cross pedestrian and bike paths alongside circulating cars inside the ring.

sec06-card-r15.question_text: How should you handle speed, turn direction, and lane discipline through a roundabout?
sec06-card-r15.teaching_text: Drifting across striped circular lanes mid-roundabout sideswipes drivers curving alongside you toward the same exit.

sec06-card-r16.question_text: How should you choose and announce your exit from a roundabout?
sec06-card-r16.teaching_text: Picking your exit before entering and clicking your right blinker as it nears keeps circular traffic smooth.

sec06-card-r17.question_text: What must you check for before changing lanes or peeling out of a multi-lane roundabout?
sec06-card-r17.teaching_text: Curved roundabout geometry hides outer-lane vehicles outside standard flat mirror angles right beside your passenger door.

sec06-card-r18.question_text: On an Illinois four-lane road, must oncoming drivers stop for a school bus halted in the opposite direction?
sec06-card-r18.teaching_text: Illinois's classic exam distinction exempts opposite-direction traffic on roads with at least four lanes, while same-direction lanes always stop.

sec06-card-r19.question_text: Outside the four-lane oncoming rule, where must you stop for a school bus loading or unloading riders?
sec06-card-r19.teaching_text: School-bus stop laws reach beyond public two-lane streets right onto private roads and campus parking lots.

sec06-card-r20.question_text: How far ahead do school-bus warning lights begin flashing in town versus rural areas before the stop arm extends?
sec06-card-r20.teaching_text: Flashing lights give trailing and oncoming cars early notice at one hundred feet in town or two hundred in country zones.

sec06-card-r21.question_text: Once required to stop for a school bus, when may you start moving again?
sec06-card-r21.teaching_text: Rolling forward while red lights still flash risks hitting a late child darting back across the street.

sec06-card-r22.question_text: What three mandatory penalties hit a driver convicted of illegally passing a stopped school bus?
sec06-card-r22.teaching_text: Exam distractors often list just a fine, forgetting that even a first offense costs your driving privileges and mandates court-assigned service hours.

sec06-card-r23.question_text: What happens if your car illegally passes a school bus while someone else was driving and you refuse to name them?
sec06-card-r23.teaching_text: Stop-arm cameras capture license plates, forcing non-driving owners to identify the operator or lose vehicle registration for three months.

sec06-card-r24.question_text: Who always holds right-of-way at highway-rail intersections?
sec06-card-r24.teaching_text: Locomotives and track maintenance rigs cannot swerve and need huge stopping distances, giving rail traffic priority every time.

sec06-card-r25.question_text: Within what distance range must you stop at a railroad crossing when signals, gates, signs, flaggers, or trains warn you?
sec06-card-r25.teaching_text: Halting between fifteen and fifty feet keeps your bumper safely clear of overhanging freight cars and crossing arms.

sec06-card-r26.question_text: What must you check before driving across a multi-track railroad crossing?
sec06-card-r26.teaching_text: A passing freight train easily hides a fast passenger train approaching from the opposite direction on parallel rails.

sec06-card-r27.question_text: How should you handle a railroad crossing that has no gates or lights—or only a crossbuck?
sec06-card-r27.teaching_text: Without automated flashers or bells, cracking awareness with slower speed, eyes, and ears is your sole warning system.

sec06-card-r28.question_text: What traffic space must exist on the far side before you drive onto railroad tracks?
sec06-card-r28.teaching_text: Entering tracks behind a stopped traffic queue can pin your vehicle helplessly across live rails if lights start flashing.

sec06-card-r29.question_text: Which three categories of commercial or public vehicles must stop at most railroad crossings?
sec06-card-r29.teaching_text: Expect buses, passenger-for-hire vans, and hazmat tankers ahead of you to brake to a stop even when crossing lights are dark.

sec06-card-r30.question_text: If your car stalls or gets trapped on railroad tracks, how should everyone evacuate and which angle do you run?
sec06-card-r30.teaching_text: Train impacts hurl shattered metal forward down the tracks, so angling away in the direction the locomotive comes from keeps everyone behind flying debris.

sec07-card-f01.question_text: Where do you find the railroad's emergency telephone number if a vehicle or hazard blocks the tracks?
sec07-card-f01.teaching_text: Calling the blue Emergency Notification System sign right at the crossing post lets dispatchers halt trains faster than general routing.

sec07-card-f02.question_text: What train expectation should you hold at every track, and what must you verify after one train passes?
sec07-card-f02.teaching_text: Freight and commuter schedules vary constantly, and pulling out right behind a caboose risks meeting a hidden second train.

sec07-card-f03.question_text: When must you wait before starting across railroad tracks even if no train is visible?
sec07-card-f03.teaching_text: Stopping behind a red light with your tail overhanging the rails leaves you trapped if gates suddenly drop.

sec07-card-f04.question_text: How should a driver with a manual transmission handle gears when crossing railroad tracks?
sec07-card-f04.teaching_text: Missing a gear or stalling the clutch midway across rough rails can strand your vehicle directly in a train's path.

sec07-card-f05.question_text: Why must you never try to beat a train—and what vehicles ahead should you expect to stop at tracks?
sec07-card-f05.teaching_text: Locomotives close faster than eyes judge, and buses or hazmat trucks ahead will brake to a halt at crossings.

sec07-card-f06.question_text: Where must you bring your vehicle to a stop when pulling out of an urban alley, building, or driveway?
sec07-card-f06.teaching_text: Halting before the concrete walkway keeps your hood from sweeping into pedestrians hidden behind brick building corners.

sec07-card-f07.question_text: Once stopped at an urban alley or driveway exit, what yielding and signaling steps follow?
sec07-card-f07.teaching_text: Both foot traffic on the sidewalk and every vehicle on the street hold priority over someone entering from private access.

sec07-card-f08.question_text: How should you secure the transmission and brakes when parking on a hill?
sec07-card-f08.teaching_text: Gravity strains transmission pawls on steep grades, so setting the parking brake adds essential mechanical backup.

sec07-card-f09.question_text: What four-step sequence applies before pulling out from a parked spot on an incline?
sec07-card-f09.teaching_text: Signaling and checking blind spots before pulling away from a sloped curb prevents rolling or merging into live traffic.

sec07-card-f10.question_text: Which way must you angle your front tires when parked facing downhill next to a curb?
sec07-card-f10.teaching_text: Turning into the curb lets the concrete edge chock your front tire immediately if the car creeps forward.

sec07-card-f11.question_text: Which way must you angle your front tires when parked facing uphill beside a curb?
sec07-card-f11.teaching_text: Turning away from the curb lets the back of your front tire catch cleanly against the curb lip if the car rolls back.

sec07-card-f12.question_text: How should you turn your wheels when parking uphill or downhill on a road without a curb?
sec07-card-f12.teaching_text: Without a raised curb to stop a tire, angling toward the shoulder steers a runaway car off the road rather than into traffic.

sec07-card-f13.question_text: Which wheels go beside the curb and within how many inches when parallel parking on a two-way street?
sec07-card-f13.teaching_text: Two-way streets require right-hand curb parking within one foot so your car faces traffic flow and clears the lane.

sec07-card-f14.question_text: Which curb may you use when parking on an Illinois one-way street, and how close must you park?
sec07-card-f14.teaching_text: One-way traffic allows left-curb or right-curb parking within twelve inches as long as your nose points with traffic flow.

sec07-card-f15.question_text: Beyond displaying disability plates or a placard, who must actually be with the vehicle to use an accessible stall?
sec07-card-f15.teaching_text: Borrowing a relative's placard while running errands alone violates Illinois law unless the authorized holder enters or exits the car.

sec07-card-f16.question_text: May a driver with valid disability plates or a placard park on the diagonal stripes next to an accessible stall?
sec07-card-f16.teaching_text: Diagonal access aisles keep wheelchair lifts and ramps usable, making them strictly off-limits even to placard holders.

sec07-card-f17.question_text: Which vehicles are legally allowed to occupy a designated electric-vehicle charging space?
sec07-card-f17.teaching_text: Parking a gas-only vehicle in a signed EV charging bay blocks plug access and triggers parking enforcement.

sec07-card-r01.question_text: Where around walkways, intersections, curb-parked cars, and safety zones is stopping or double-parking banned?
sec07-card-r01.teaching_text: Blocking sidewalks, crosswalks, intersections, or safety-zone curb gaps traps pedestrians and transit riders in live lanes.

sec07-card-r02.question_text: How does Illinois treat stopping, standing, or parking in marked, buffered, or barrel-protected bike lanes?
sec07-card-r02.teaching_text: Pulling into a bike lane for deliveries or quick drop-offs forces cyclists to swerve suddenly into fast motor traffic.

sec07-card-r03.question_text: When is stopping beside or across from street construction or an obstruction illegal?
sec07-card-r03.teaching_text: Parking opposite roadwork narrows the remaining pavement into an impassable choke point.

sec07-card-r04.question_text: Which five elevated, enclosed, rail, or high-speed facilities ban stopping, standing, and parking?
sec07-card-r04.teaching_text: Confined spans, tracks, tunnels, and controlled-access highways lack safe clearance for stationary vehicles.

sec07-card-r05.question_text: Are you allowed to stop, stand, or park between the roadways or in a crossover of a divided highway?
sec07-card-r05.teaching_text: Center medians and paved turnarounds are reserved strictly for emergency operations rather than roadside stops.

sec07-card-r06.question_text: Outside town districts, what visibility, lights, and lane space are required if an emergency forces a roadway stop?
sec07-card-r06.teaching_text: Pull completely off rural pavement whenever practical, and in emergencies ensure two hundred feet of sightline both ways with flashers.

sec07-card-r07.question_text: How do posted no-stopping or no-parking signs relate to statewide parking bans?
sec07-card-r07.teaching_text: Lack of a sign never makes blocking a hydrant or crosswalk legal, and posted signs add extra local restrictions.

sec07-card-r08.question_text: Does sitting inside your running car make standing across a driveway or within fifteen feet of a hydrant legal?
sec07-card-r08.teaching_text: Illinois bans both standing and parking across driveways or inside fifteen feet of a fire hydrant even with a driver aboard.

sec07-card-r09.question_text: Which two locations share Illinois's twenty-foot standing-and-parking clearance rule?
sec07-card-r09.teaching_text: Pair fire-station driveways and intersection crosswalks together in memory since both require twenty feet of open curb.

sec07-card-r10.question_text: How far must standing or parked cars stay from a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal?
sec07-card-r10.teaching_text: Keeping thirty feet open in front of intersection controls ensures approaching drivers spot red lights and stop octagons clearly.

sec07-card-r11.question_text: Within how many feet of the nearest railroad rail is parking prohibited in Illinois?
sec07-card-r11.teaching_text: Fifty feet of open sightline near tracks keeps parked vehicles from hiding approaching trains or warning flashers.

sec07-card-r12.question_text: What lighting rules apply to a vehicle parked along a highway between sunset and sunrise?
sec07-card-r12.teaching_text: Front and rear parking lights mark your vehicle's outline in the dark while dimmed headlights prevent blinding oncoming drivers.

sec07-card-r13.question_text: What does Illinois law say about dropping objects from an overpass or elevated spot toward moving traffic?
sec07-card-r13.teaching_text: Even small objects dropped onto highway windshields carry lethal impact force at road speed.

sec07-card-r14.question_text: What is the lone situation where driving a vehicle onto a sidewalk is legal?
sec07-card-r14.teaching_text: Sidewalks belong strictly to foot traffic except at curb cuts where a driveway crosses into private property.

sec07-card-r15.question_text: What two limits restrict how you load cargo and seated passengers inside a vehicle?
sec07-card-r15.teaching_text: Piling boxes in windows blinds your mirrors, and packing extra riders beyond available seat belts leaves someone unrestrained.

sec07-card-r16.question_text: May passengers ride inside a towed house trailer while it travels on a street or highway?
sec07-card-r16.teaching_text: Towed campers lack crash-tested occupant restraints and direct communication with the driver up front.

sec07-card-r17.question_text: At what distance outside your moving vehicle does a loud sound system become illegal on an Illinois highway?
sec07-card-r17.teaching_text: Blasting music audible seventy-five feet away drowns out approaching sirens, train horns, and emergency warnings.

sec09-card-f01.question_text: How does alcohol affect driving skills even before reaching the legal intoxication threshold?
sec09-card-f01.teaching_text: Waiting until you feel buzzed ignores how your very first drink already blurs vision and delays braking.

sec09-card-f02.question_text: Which four bodily samples can chemical testing analyze to measure blood-alcohol concentration?
sec09-card-f02.teaching_text: Officers are not restricted to roadside breathalyzers when lab blood or urine samples measure exact concentration.

sec09-card-f03.question_text: At what blood-alcohol percentage is driving illegal per se, and what if impairment shows below that?
sec09-card-f03.teaching_text: Blowing under the per-se threshold never shields you from conviction when unsafe driving proves alcohol impairment.

sec09-card-f04.question_text: Which three personal factors can alter how strongly someone reacts to alcohol?
sec09-card-f04.teaching_text: Empty stomachs, shifting tolerance, or allergy pills make yesterday's single drink hit much harder tonight.

sec09-card-f05.question_text: What actually clears alcohol's effects, and do food, coffee, or cold showers speed that up?
sec09-card-f05.teaching_text: Black coffee and cold water merely produce a wide-awake impaired driver while your liver works at fixed speed.

sec09-card-f06.question_text: What cannabis concentration thresholds prohibit driving on Illinois highways?
sec09-card-f06.teaching_text: Memorize both Illinois numbers carefully: five nanograms in whole blood versus ten in another bodily substance.

sec09-card-f07.question_text: Does lawful medical or adult-use recreational cannabis allow driving while impaired?
sec09-card-f07.teaching_text: Holding a state medical card or buying from a licensed dispensary gives zero immunity behind the wheel.

sec09-card-f08.question_text: How must cannabis be packaged when transported inside a motor vehicle?
sec09-card-f08.teaching_text: Loose or unsealed packaging inside the cabin violates Illinois transport law even when the driver is sober.

sec09-card-f09.question_text: Who is prohibited from consuming cannabis inside a motor vehicle?
sec09-card-f09.teaching_text: Unlike narrow charter-vehicle alcohol exceptions, Illinois bans passenger cannabis use inside motor vehicles completely.

sec09-card-f10.question_text: What tests must a stopped driver submit to when an officer reasonably suspects cannabis impairment?
sec09-card-f10.teaching_text: Reasonable suspicion during a traffic stop legally triggers standardized roadside balance checks and validated chemical tests.

sec09-card-f11.question_text: What happens to your license if you refuse or fail required roadside cannabis testing?
sec09-card-f11.teaching_text: Declining field sobriety or validated cannabis testing costs your driving privilege through administrative suspension.

sec09-card-f12.question_text: What two penalties can follow cannabis-impaired driving or illegal vehicle transport for a registered patient?
sec09-card-f12.teaching_text: Violating vehicle cannabis rules strips both your driver's license and a medical patient card for two years.

sec09-card-f13.question_text: Which legal medications can impair safe driving ability?
sec09-card-f13.teaching_text: Over-the-counter antihistamines and cough syrups cause drowsiness and blurred focus rivaling alcohol.

sec09-card-f14.question_text: Why is combining even a small amount of alcohol with other drugs hazardous?
sec09-card-f14.teaching_text: Synergistic drug interactions amplify sedation and dizzy spells far beyond what either substance causes alone.

sec09-card-f15.question_text: How long does an Illinois DUI conviction stay on your driving record, and what penalties can apply?
sec09-card-f15.teaching_text: An Illinois DUI conviction never ages off your driving file and threatens plates, freedom, and finances.

sec09-card-f16.question_text: What chemical-testing consent do you automatically give simply by driving on Illinois roadways?
sec09-card-f16.teaching_text: Operating on public Illinois pavement legally commits you to breath, blood, urine, or bodily-substance testing.

sec09-card-f17.question_text: When must police request alcohol or drug testing after a collision?
sec09-card-f17.teaching_text: Whenever probable cause of impairment meets serious injury or death, officers are required to demand chemical testing.

sec09-card-f18.question_text: May a tested driver arrange extra chemical testing, and who pays for it?
sec09-card-f18.teaching_text: After completing police testing, you can hire your own qualified clinician for an independent sample at your cost.

sec09-card-f19.question_text: When can a convicted impaired driver owe up to five hundred dollars for blood-testing costs?
sec09-card-f19.teaching_text: Refusing breath testing or triggering drug-related blood draws shifts up to five hundred dollars in lab fees onto you.

sec09-card-f20.question_text: How long is the statutory summary suspension for failing a chemical test for alcohol, cannabis, or unlawful drugs?
sec09-card-f20.teaching_text: Failing a first-offender chemical test triggers a six-month administrative summary suspension separate from criminal court.

sec09-card-f21.question_text: How long is the ordinary suspension for refusing chemical testing?
sec09-card-f21.teaching_text: Notice Illinois doubles administrative loss from six months for failing to twelve full months for refusing.

sec09-card-f22.question_text: What prior record within five years classifies a driver as a second offender for summary suspension?
sec09-card-f22.teaching_text: Prior supervision, out-of-state refusal, summary suspension, or conviction inside five years strips first-offender status.

sec09-card-f23.question_text: What summary suspension lengths hit a five-year second offender for test refusal versus test failure?
sec09-card-f23.teaching_text: Exam questions contrast first and repeat numbers: repeat refusal jumps to three years while repeat failure hits one year.

sec09-card-f24.question_text: How can prosecutors use a driver's refusal to take a chemical test?
sec09-card-f24.teaching_text: Declining a breath or blood test does not hide guilt; prosecutors present that refusal to the jury.

sec09-card-f25.question_text: What receipt does a validly licensed driver get at DUI arrest, and when does summary suspension begin?
sec09-card-f25.teaching_text: Officers confiscate your plastic card immediately, leaving forty-five driving days before day forty-six locks privileges.

sec09-card-f26.question_text: What two steps must happen before a summary suspension actually terminates?
sec09-card-f26.teaching_text: Waiting out the calendar months alone leaves you legally suspended until reinstatement fees clear your file.

sec09-card-f27.question_text: What administrative penalty follows refusing chemical testing after a crash involving serious injury or death?
sec09-card-f27.teaching_text: Refusing testing after a severe injury or fatal crash triggers full revocation rather than a simple suspension.

sec09-card-r01.question_text: How does a criminal DUI conviction relate to a statutory summary suspension or revocation?
sec09-card-r01.teaching_text: Administrative summary loss and criminal court DUI penalties run on parallel tracks and can both hit you.

sec09-card-r02.question_text: What minimum revocation periods apply to a first DUI, a second within twenty years, and a third?
sec09-card-r02.teaching_text: Each repeat conviction multiplies how many years you stay off the road before even requesting a hearing.

sec09-card-r03.question_text: What license consequence follows a fourth or subsequent DUI conviction in Illinois?
sec09-card-r03.teaching_text: Reaching a fourth impaired-driving conviction permanently ends standard Illinois licensing for life.

sec09-card-r04.question_text: What higher BAC figure or passenger age triggers enhanced DUI punishment?
sec09-card-r04.teaching_text: Double the legal zero-point-zero-eight threshold or endangering a passenger under sixteen brings sharply stiffer sentences.

sec09-card-r05.question_text: What steps can restoring driving privileges after an impaired-driving revocation require?
sec09-card-r05.teaching_text: Unlike a routine suspension, revocation forces you to prove sobriety and safety at a formal administrative hearing.

sec09-card-r06.question_text: How long must financial-responsibility insurance remain on file after a DUI conviction?
sec09-card-r06.teaching_text: Letting mandatory financial-responsibility coverage lapse at any point during those three years re-suspends your license.

sec09-card-r07.question_text: How does Illinois handle an Illinois resident's impaired-driving conviction or test refusal in another state?
sec09-card-r07.teaching_text: An out-of-state DUI or refusal follows you home and triggers comparable administrative action on your Illinois record.

sec09-card-r08.question_text: What permit and vehicle device allow an eligible first-time offender to drive during summary suspension?
sec09-card-r08.teaching_text: Installing an approved breath-alcohol ignition interlock keeps you from starting the engine with alcohol on your breath.

sec09-card-r09.question_text: Who pays for the monitoring permit, interlock installation, and monthly monitoring unless found indigent?
sec09-card-r09.teaching_text: Permit, hardware installation, and monthly data-monitoring bills add hundreds of out-of-pocket dollars onto DUI costs.

sec09-card-r10.question_text: What events does the breath interlock report back to the monitoring agency?
sec09-card-r10.teaching_text: Every failed breath sample or wiring bypass attempt logs digitally and alerts state officials.

sec09-card-r11.question_text: What may a first-time offender decline, and what crime occurs if they drive during suspension anyway?
sec09-card-r11.teaching_text: Sitting out the suspension without an interlock is legal, whereas sneaking one drive after opting out is a felony.

sec09-card-r12.question_text: Which crash outcomes, offense counts, or prior fatal records elevate impaired driving to Aggravated DUI?
sec09-card-r12.teaching_text: Causing injury or death, racking up a third DUI, or carrying prior reckless-homicide history triggers felony-tier charges.

sec09-card-r13.question_text: Which passenger-transport roles or missing credentials also elevate impaired driving to Aggravated DUI?
sec09-card-r13.teaching_text: Driving impaired with kids on a school bus, in a rideshare or taxi, or without valid license or insurance escalates charges.

sec09-card-r14.question_text: Who is barred from drinking alcohol in a vehicle, and which four passenger vehicles are exempted?
sec09-card-r14.teaching_text: Drivers may never drink, and passenger exceptions apply strictly to non-school charters, RVs, mini motorhomes, and limos.

sec09-card-r15.question_text: What rule governs an opened alcoholic-beverage container inside a vehicle?
sec09-card-r15.teaching_text: Even an un-sipped bottle with a broken seal inside the passenger area violates Illinois open-container law.

sec09-card-r16.question_text: How can impaired motorboat operation affect your highway driver's license?
sec09-card-r16.teaching_text: Refusing or failing chemical tests after an injury or fatal motorboat crash can suspend your road driving privileges.

sec09-card-r17.question_text: What alcohol duty binds parents or guardians on property, vehicles, or boats they control?
sec09-card-r17.teaching_text: Letting minors drink at home, in cars, or on boats brings steep criminal liability, especially if injury follows.

sec09-card-r18.question_text: What three consequences can hit someone caught driving while suspended or revoked for DUI or serious crashes?
sec09-card-r18.teaching_text: Getting caught behind the wheel during a DUI or fatal hit-and-run revocation can cost your car through forfeiture.

sec09-card-r19.question_text: May you drive in another state while suspended or revoked in Illinois for serious offenses?
sec09-card-r19.teaching_text: Crossing state lines never lifts an Illinois revocation, and any out-of-state arrest reports straight back.

sec09-card-r20.question_text: What rule governs letting a visibly or knowingly impaired friend drive your car?
sec09-card-r20.teaching_text: Handing your keys to an impaired friend endangers everyone on the road and exposes you legally.

sec09-card-r21.question_text: What three penalties can follow a conviction for supplying alcohol to someone under twenty-one?
sec09-card-r21.teaching_text: Notice that furnishing alcohol to minors can suspend your own driver's license even when no car was involved.

sec09-card-r22.question_text: How long is the minimum license revocation for a first DUI conviction under age twenty-one?
sec09-card-r22.teaching_text: Compare carefully: an adult first DUI revokes at least one year, whereas under twenty-one doubles to two years.

sec09-card-r23.question_text: What minimum suspension hits a driver under twenty-one caught operating with any trace of alcohol?
sec09-card-r23.teaching_text: Illinois's Zero Tolerance law suspends drivers under twenty-one for at least three months on any detectable alcohol.

sec09-card-r24.question_text: How does an underage conviction or supervision for buying, holding, or drinking alcohol affect driving privileges?
sec09-card-r24.teaching_text: Getting cited at a party on foot for underage possession or drinking still suspends your Illinois license.

sec09-card-r25.question_text: What education and testing can be required to get your license back after a suspension before age twenty-one?
sec09-card-r25.teaching_text: Young drivers suspended before twenty-one must pass remedial driver education and may retake the entire license test.

sec09-card-r26.question_text: Why does the handbook direct readers to check the current impaired-driving fact book or official website?
sec09-card-r26.teaching_text: Legislators tighten impaired-driving statutes regularly, so checking current Secretary of State publications ensures accurate details.

sec10-card-f01.question_text: Where should you pull over after encountering or being involved in a crash?
sec10-card-f01.teaching_text: Clearing drivable vehicles into a bright public spot prevents secondary highway pileups while keeping everyone visible.

sec10-card-f02.question_text: What two urgent actions are required when someone is injured in a crash?
sec10-card-f02.teaching_text: Dialing emergency dispatch immediately gets trained paramedics rolling while reasonable assistance supports hurt occupants.

sec10-card-f03.question_text: Which two warning tools should you use at a crash scene to alert approaching traffic?
sec10-card-f03.teaching_text: Flashing four-ways and roadside flares give fast-approaching drivers extra distance to brake or change lanes.

sec10-card-f04.question_text: Which five contact, licensing, and vehicle details should you collect from people involved in a crash?
sec10-card-f04.teaching_text: Writing down license numbers and plate tags alongside contact info prevents mix-ups when filing reports or claims.

sec10-card-f05.question_text: What happens if you miss or fail to pay a minor-violation ticket's initial court date?
sec10-card-f05.teaching_text: Clerks set a second appearance at least thirty days out and send notice through available contact info.

sec10-card-f06.question_text: What is the consequence of missing that second scheduled court date?
sec10-card-f06.teaching_text: Skipping a second court date enters a guilty conviction without you there and posts straight onto your license.

sec10-card-f07.question_text: How does Illinois treat failure-to-appear suspensions imposed from January twenty-twenty through December twenty-twenty-four?
sec10-card-f07.teaching_text: Statutory reforms wiped away failure-to-appear license suspensions falling inside that specific five-year calendar window.

sec10-card-f08.question_text: What two steps are required to lift a failure-to-appear suspension imposed before January first, two thousand twenty?
sec10-card-f08.teaching_text: Older pre-twenty-twenty suspensions stay active until you both settle the underlying court case and pay reinstatement.

sec10-card-f09.question_text: Who must accompany a driver younger than eighteen to a mandatory traffic court appearance?
sec10-card-f09.teaching_text: Showing up solo under age eighteen will not satisfy a mandatory traffic hearing without a parent or guardian.

sec10-card-f10.question_text: How may an Illinois driver handle a citation in another compact state, and what if they break promised compliance?
sec10-card-f10.teaching_text: Signing a roadside promise to comply lets you drive home, yet ignoring it later suspends your Illinois license.

sec10-card-f11.question_text: When does an insured crash require an official report regardless of fault?
sec10-card-f11.teaching_text: Modern bumper sensors easily pass fifteen hundred dollars on minor taps, requiring a report even when faultless.

sec10-card-f12.question_text: What lower property-damage threshold triggers a mandatory crash report when any vehicle is uninsured?
sec10-card-f12.teaching_text: Exam questions contrast both thresholds constantly: over fifteen hundred insured versus over five hundred if anyone lacks insurance.

sec10-card-f13.question_text: When does a crash involving a school bus require an official report?
sec10-card-f13.teaching_text: Heightened student-safety oversight triggers mandatory reporting whenever a school bus crash causes injury or property damage.

sec10-card-f14.question_text: When must a crash within fifty feet of a school bus be reported even if the bus wasn't hit?
sec10-card-f14.teaching_text: Striking someone waiting to board or stepping away within fifty feet of a school bus triggers bus-zone reporting.

sec10-card-r01.question_text: How quickly must you notify police and report a crash, and where if no officer comes?
sec10-card-r01.teaching_text: Know the tight thirty-minute reporting rule, plus heading to the nearest station or calling rural sheriff or state police.

sec10-card-r02.question_text: Who must file the crash report when the driver is physically unable and a passenger was riding?
sec10-card-r02.teaching_text: When injuries keep the driver from reporting, Illinois law shifts that legal reporting duty onto an able passenger.

sec10-card-r03.question_text: What maximum fine and jail sentence can follow failing to report a vehicle crash?
sec10-card-r03.teaching_text: Skipping a required crash report carries criminal misdemeanor exposure far costlier than any insurance deductible.

sec10-card-r04.question_text: How do license sanctions differ for leaving an injury or fatal crash versus damage over one thousand dollars?
sec10-card-r04.teaching_text: Fleeing hurt victims triggers full license revocation alongside felony danger, while fleeing thousand-dollar damage suspends privileges.

sec10-card-r05.question_text: Where must you stop after hitting unattended property, and what four details go on your note if no owner is found?
sec10-card-r05.teaching_text: Include your plate number alongside name, address, and phone so the absent owner can verify vehicle identity.

sec10-card-r06.question_text: What two official steps are still required after leaving a note on damaged unattended property?
sec10-card-r06.teaching_text: Tucking a paper slip under a wiper blade never replaces calling police and completing required crash reports.

sec10-card-r07.question_text: What must an at-fault uninsured driver post after a crash, and who sets the amount?
sec10-card-r07.teaching_text: Without liability insurance to cover victims, the state transportation department calculates a cash or bond security deposit.

sec10-card-r08.question_text: Whose privileges can be suspended if required uninsured-crash security is not posted?
sec10-card-r08.teaching_text: Both the at-fault driver's license and the vehicle owner's registration tags can stay suspended until claims settle.

sec10-card-r09.question_text: How long must financial-responsibility insurance be maintained to end a safety-responsibility suspension?
sec10-card-r09.teaching_text: Clearing a safety-responsibility suspension requires continuous monitored coverage for three full years from initial filing.

sec10-card-r10.question_text: What suspension length, fee, and permit rule hit a mandatory-insurance conviction?
sec10-card-r10.teaching_text: Driving uninsured locks you out for at least three months with a hundred-dollar fee and zero hardship-permit relief.

sec10-card-r11.question_text: Which four judgment, crash, supervision, or conviction histories require financial-responsibility proof?
sec10-card-r11.teaching_text: Unpaid crash judgments, uninsured-crash suspensions, insurance court supervision, or three insurance convictions all trigger strict monitoring.

sec10-card-r12.question_text: Which three forms can financial-responsibility proof take, and how does an insurance certificate reach the state?
sec10-card-r12.teaching_text: Your insurance carrier transmits the official certificate directly to the state rather than handing you a casual card.

sec10-card-r13.question_text: What happens if required monitored financial-responsibility insurance is canceled or not renewed?
sec10-card-r13.teaching_text: Insurers notify the state electronically whenever a monitored policy drops, triggering immediate license suspension.

sec10-card-r14.question_text: At what age may completing an eight-hour defensive-driving course qualify a driver for an insurance discount?
sec10-card-r14.teaching_text: Drivers fifty-five and up can earn lower liability premiums after completing an approved eight-hour refresher course.

sec11-card-f01.question_text: How long can certain Illinois revocations, suspensions, denials, and cancellations stay on your driving record?
sec11-card-f01.teaching_text: Assuming every violation drops off after a few years misses that major license withdrawals can follow your record forever.

sec11-card-f02.question_text: What two penalties apply if you get caught driving while your Illinois license is suspended or revoked?
sec11-card-f02.teaching_text: Getting behind the wheel while sidelined stretches out your time off the road and adds criminal jail exposure.

sec11-card-f03.question_text: How does license revocation affect your driving privileges, and when is the earliest standard window to reapply?
sec11-card-f03.teaching_text: Unlike a fixed-term suspension, revocation wipes out privileges indefinitely with zero automatic return after twelve months.

sec11-card-f04.question_text: What happens to your license if you are convicted of a moving violation that causes a fatal crash?
sec11-card-f04.teaching_text: Any moving ticket tied to a deadly collision triggers instant revocation rather than minor warning points.

sec11-card-f05.question_text: Beyond revoking a repeat offender's driver's license, what action can the state also take on their vehicle?
sec11-card-f05.teaching_text: Freezing vehicle registration alongside driver revocation keeps habitual violators from simply handing keys around or sneaking out.

sec11-card-f06.question_text: What license action applies to aggravated impaired driving or driving under alcohol, cannabis, or other drugs?
sec11-card-f06.teaching_text: Illinois treats cannabis and drug impairment with the same license-revoking force as alcohol DUI convictions.

sec11-card-f07.question_text: How does Illinois penalize a driver's license for aggravated police flight, aggravated reckless driving, or street racing?
sec11-card-f07.teaching_text: Running from officers or drag racing on public streets moves straight past suspension into full license revocation.

sec11-card-f08.question_text: What license consequence follows auto or parts theft, or using a vehicle to commit a felony?
sec11-card-f08.teaching_text: Even when no traffic rule is broken, turning a car into a felony tool strips your driving privilege.

sec11-card-f09.question_text: What license penalty can result from making, selling, equipping, or helping someone use an unauthorized fake ID or license?
sec11-card-f09.teaching_text: Supplying, printing, or helping pass fake credentials carries full driver's-license revocation even before anyone drives.

sec11-card-f10.question_text: What license action applies to lying to the state agency, vehicle-linked gang offenses, or fleeing an injury crash?
sec11-card-f10.teaching_text: Fleeing an injury crash or lying on state paperwork destroys trust in a driver and triggers revocation.

sec11-card-f11.question_text: Can reckless conduct with a vehicle that injures or endangers people trigger license revocation?
sec11-card-f11.teaching_text: Endangering bystanders or passengers through reckless vehicle behavior crosses the threshold into indefinite license loss.

sec11-card-f12.question_text: How many reckless-driving convictions in twelve months—or what degree of crash harm—triggers license revocation?
sec11-card-f12.teaching_text: Either stacking three reckless convictions inside a year or causing permanent life-altering injury costs your license.

sec11-card-f13.question_text: Which two deadly scenarios fall under Illinois's reckless-homicide revocation category?
sec11-card-f13.teaching_text: Causing a fatality recklessly or while already barred for aggravated DUI carries severe reckless-homicide revocation.

sec11-card-f14.question_text: What license action follows a conviction for illegally passing a school bus and causing a fatal crash?
sec11-card-f14.teaching_text: Passing a stopped bus normally brings suspension, whereas causing a deadly crash escalates straight to revocation.

sec11-card-f15.question_text: How does a suspension differ from revocation, and what is required to drive again once the fixed term ends?
sec11-card-f15.teaching_text: Privileges never snap back automatically on day one after suspension until you pay reinstatement fees and clear requirements.

sec11-card-f16.question_text: How many unpaid automated red-light or speed-camera tickets in a municipality can trigger a license suspension?
sec11-card-f16.teaching_text: Ignoring mailed camera citations lets municipal fines pile up to five and freeze your driving privileges.

sec11-card-f17.question_text: What license action can follow if you fail to slow down or move over in a work zone and cause damage or injury?
sec11-card-f17.teaching_text: Highway crews work inches from live traffic, so ignoring speed drops or lane shifts brings license loss after a crash.

sec11-card-f18.question_text: How can a court ruling over a child-visitation dispute affect your Illinois driver's license?
sec11-card-f18.teaching_text: Non-driving family court orders still carry the power to suspend state driving privileges until compliance returns.

sec11-card-f19.question_text: Does refusing a post-arrest alcohol or drug test outside Illinois still affect your Illinois driver's license?
sec11-card-f19.teaching_text: Interstate reporting means refusing chemical testing in another state follows you home to suspend your Illinois license.

sec11-card-f20.question_text: What happens to your license if you commit a drug or sex offense while operating or controlling a car?
sec11-card-f20.teaching_text: Even sitting in direct physical control of a parked vehicle during those offenses puts your license under suspension.

sec11-card-f21.question_text: Which missed traffic-court appearance date cutoff remains listed as an Illinois suspension ground?
sec11-card-f21.teaching_text: Older unresolved citations dated prior to January two thousand twenty can still hold a suspension over your record.

sec11-card-f22.question_text: How many convictions for ignoring an active railroad-crossing warning signal trigger a license suspension?
sec11-card-f22.teaching_text: Trying to beat crossing gates or flashing red lights risks catastrophic train impacts and suspends repeat violators.

sec11-card-f23.question_text: Which two authorities can direct Illinois to suspend a driver's license over unpaid child support?
sec11-card-f23.teaching_text: Both circuit judges and the state child-support agency can freeze driving privileges when payments fall behind.

sec11-card-f24.question_text: What license penalty applies when failing to slow down and move over for a stopped emergency vehicle causes damage or injury?
sec11-card-f24.teaching_text: Failing to give roadside responders speed and lane relief triggers license suspension when property damage or injury results.

sec11-card-f25.question_text: How does Illinois penalize borrowing, altering, lending out a license, or helping with a fraudulent application?
sec11-card-f25.teaching_text: Even letting a friend borrow your genuine card for underage entry puts your own driving privilege in suspension.

sec11-card-r01.question_text: Can an underage vehicle occupant face license suspension for illegally possessing, buying, or drinking alcohol?
sec11-card-r01.teaching_text: Under-twenty-one alcohol violations inside a vehicle hit your driving privileges even when nobody is charged with DUI.

sec11-card-r02.question_text: How do illegal alcohol-transportation suspension rules compare between drivers twenty-one and older versus drivers under twenty-one?
sec11-card-r02.teaching_text: Adults trigger suspension on a second illegal transport in twelve months, whereas underage drivers face action right away.

sec11-card-r03.question_text: When can failing to file required financial-responsibility insurance suspend your Illinois license?
sec11-card-r03.teaching_text: After court supervision for no insurance or three uninsured tickets, skipping mandatory coverage filings freezes your license.

sec11-card-r04.question_text: Which two uninsured-driving situations are listed grounds for suspending your Illinois license?
sec11-card-r04.teaching_text: Getting caught uninsured on a routine stop or owing crash damages without coverage both suspend driving privileges.

sec11-card-r05.question_text: Accumulating how many unpaid railroad-crossing violations can suspend your driver's license?
sec11-card-r05.teaching_text: Stacking five unpaid crossing fines triggers an administrative license suspension on top of the court penalties.

sec11-card-r06.question_text: Which two school-bus violations can get your Illinois driver's license suspended?
sec11-card-r06.teaching_text: Either one officer-cited failure to stop for loading kids or five unpaid bus-camera citations suspends your license.

sec11-card-r07.question_text: When does a repeat work-zone speeding ticket trigger license suspension in Illinois?
sec11-card-r07.teaching_text: Getting caught speeding twice inside two years while road crews are present moves beyond heavy fines to suspension.

sec11-card-r08.question_text: What can happen to your license if you refuse or neglect to file a required crash report?
sec11-card-r08.teaching_text: Ignoring mandatory collision paperwork after an accident puts your driving privilege at risk of state suspension.

sec11-card-r09.question_text: How many moving-violation convictions trigger license suspension for adults versus drivers arrested under age twenty-one?
sec11-card-r09.teaching_text: Drivers under twenty-one get tighter limits—two tickets over twenty-four months suspends them instead of three in twelve.

sec11-card-r10.question_text: Beyond a steep fine, what license action can result from illegally parking in a disability-reserved stall?
sec11-card-r10.teaching_text: Taking a reserved accessible stall without authorization can cost your driver's license, not just parking-ticket money.

sec11-card-r11.question_text: What blood alcohol range triggers an Illinois zero-tolerance suspension for a driver younger than twenty-one?
sec11-card-r11.teaching_text: Even trace alcohol below the adult DUI mark suspends an underage driver under Illinois zero-tolerance enforcement.

sec11-card-r12.question_text: Why does the state cancel a license or permit, and when can the holder apply again?
sec11-card-r12.teaching_text: Cancellation fixes eligibility errors or defects rather than punishing driving, allowing a fresh application once requirements are met.

sec11-card-r13.question_text: What happens if the state orders you to take a driver reexamination and you skip or fail it?
sec11-card-r13.teaching_text: Until you appear and demonstrate safe driving skills on a required retest, your credential gets canceled.

sec11-card-r14.question_text: Which two application or eligibility problems are listed grounds for canceling an Illinois credential?
sec11-card-r14.teaching_text: Obtaining a card with false paperwork or lacking legal eligibility voids the credential through formal cancellation.

sec11-card-r15.question_text: What does a license denial block, and what age group faces denial for specified traffic convictions?
sec11-card-r15.teaching_text: Denial delays when a young driver can step up to apply for a license—and sometimes even a permit.

sec11-card-r16.question_text: How does a mandatory-revocation conviction affect a minor's ability to apply for a permit or license?
sec11-card-r16.teaching_text: Serious revocation-grade convictions lock a minor out of both learner permits and driver's licenses until turning eighteen.

sec11-card-r17.question_text: If a minor gets a denial for driving without a valid credential, what happens to license eligibility versus permit privileges?
sec11-card-r17.teaching_text: Supervised learning on a permit stays open—and any existing license drops back to permit-only status until eighteen.
sec11-card-r17.must_match_memory_hook: No license til eighteen, permit stays

visual_sync.text_span: No license til eighteen, permit stays

sec11-card-r18.question_text: How long does a minor's denial for a serious moving violation last, and how does it treat permit privileges?
sec11-card-r18.teaching_text: Whichever milestone arrives first ends the license freeze, while supervised permit driving remains allowed throughout.

sec11-card-r19.question_text: Can a pending charge from a serious-injury or fatal crash block license issuance or renewal even when zero alcohol was involved?
sec11-card-r19.teaching_text: Sober drivers still face blocked issuance or renewal when charged after a crash causing severe injury or death.

sec11-card-r20.question_text: What travel limits and minimum age apply to an Illinois restricted driving permit?
sec11-card-r20.teaching_text: Restricted relief never allows casual social trips—only approved schedules and routes for essentials starting at age sixteen.

sec11-card-r21.question_text: What device and compliance rules govern a monitoring permit for an eligible first-time impaired-driving offender?
sec11-card-r21.teaching_text: Summary-suspension relief works only in an interlock-equipped car when you stay alcohol-free and never touch the device.

sec11-card-r22.question_text: What is the minimum age to qualify for an Illinois monitoring-device driving permit?
sec11-card-r22.teaching_text: Drivers under eighteen cannot obtain breath-interlock monitoring relief during an Illinois summary suspension.

sec11-card-r23.question_text: When can an occupational driving permit be used, and which group of drivers is excluded from it?
sec11-card-r23.teaching_text: Watch the distinction: non-commercial professional drivers suspended for three moving tickets may qualify, whereas commercial drivers cannot.

sec11-card-r24.question_text: Who can qualify for an Illinois probationary license, and what program goes along with it?
sec11-card-r24.teaching_text: Adult drivers suspended for three tickets in twelve months must pair probationary driving privileges with driver-improvement coursework.

sec11-card-r25.question_text: What authorization is required before a family-financial-responsibility driving permit can be issued?
sec11-card-r25.teaching_text: Following a support or visitation suspension, the licensing counter cannot grant driving relief without court or department authorization.

sec12-card-f01.question_text: What are the three main categories of road signs, and what two visual cues distinguish them?
sec12-card-f01.teaching_text: Knowing standard sign silhouettes and background colors lets you recognize rules and hazards even under snow or glare.

sec12-card-f02.question_text: Where in exact fallback order must you come to a full stop at an eight-sided red sign before yielding?
sec12-card-f02.teaching_text: Rolling past the painted line or creeping across the crosswalk before stopping counts as running a stop control.

sec12-card-f03.question_text: How must you obey a portable or temporary stop sign set up by road authorities?
sec12-card-f03.teaching_text: Portable octagons placed during power outages or roadwork carry identical legal stopping authority as permanent posts.

sec12-card-f04.question_text: When a crossing guard or work-zone flagger holds up a stop paddle, when may you start moving again?
sec12-card-f04.teaching_text: Treating a handheld paddle like a brief stop-and-go sign endangers children or crew members still crossing.

sec12-card-f05.question_text: What shape and colors identify a yield sign, and who gets priority when you face one?
sec12-card-f05.teaching_text: Downward-pointing red-and-white triangles tell you cross traffic and pedestrians hold priority over your approach.

sec12-card-f06.question_text: What shape, color, and markings identify an advance railroad-crossing warning sign?
sec12-card-f06.teaching_text: Circular yellow signs serve exclusively as early heads-up alerts that highway-rail grade tracks lie ahead.

sec12-card-f07.question_text: How far before rural tracks can a round railroad warning stand, and what four actions should follow?
sec12-card-f07.teaching_text: High rural speeds need early warning so you can slow down, crack a window to listen, and stop.

sec12-card-f08.question_text: Which three background colors can appear on diamond warning signs, and how should you respond?
sec12-card-f08.teaching_text: Whether permanent yellow, pedestrian yellow-green, or work-zone orange, every diamond alerts you to ease off the gas.

sec12-card-f09.question_text: What unique five-sided sign shape and color scheme alerts drivers to a school zone or school crossing?
sec12-card-f09.teaching_text: Shaped like an old schoolhouse roof, pentagon signs stand out immediately even before you read the symbol.

sec12-card-f10.question_text: How do you tell an advance school-zone sign apart from a sign marking the exact school crosswalk?
sec12-card-f10.teaching_text: Without the downward-pointing arrow you are entering the general school area; with it, kids step out right here.

sec12-card-f11.question_text: Where on the roadway is a yellow three-sided no-passing pennant mounted, and what does it mark?
sec12-card-f11.teaching_text: Placing the sideways triangle on the left edge keeps it visible even when a tall truck blocks right-side posts.

sec12-card-f12.question_text: Which two broad sign functions can square and rectangular road signs serve?
sec12-card-f12.teaching_text: Because both speed laws and highway directions use four-sided boards, background color tells them apart.

sec12-card-f13.question_text: What common meaning connects red regulatory signs like stop, yield, do-not-enter, and wrong-way?
sec12-card-f13.teaching_text: Red on traffic signs signals immediate legal prohibitions or right-of-way stops where ignoring the rule causes severe crashes.

sec12-card-f14.question_text: What two roles do black-and-white road signs fill on Illinois streets and highways?
sec12-card-f14.teaching_text: Speed limits and turn rules share the black-and-white palette with numbered route shields, so check the shape.

sec12-card-f15.question_text: What general message does a standard yellow background communicate on a road sign?
sec12-card-f15.teaching_text: Standard yellow warns of curves, merges, or slippery pavement ahead so you adjust speed before reaching them.

sec12-card-f16.question_text: What specific types of people-focused crossings and zones use fluorescent yellow-green warning signs?
sec12-card-f16.teaching_text: High-visibility fluorescent yellow-green stands out in dawn or dusk light wherever pedestrians, cyclists, or children gather.

sec12-card-f17.question_text: What type of temporary roadside hazard does an orange sign background warn you about?
sec12-card-f17.teaching_text: Spotting orange ahead tells you lanes may narrow, workers may stand nearby, and fines rise sharply.

sec12-card-f18.question_text: What three types of travel navigation details appear on green highway guide signs?
sec12-card-f18.teaching_text: Reading green overhead boards early lets you move into your exit or route lane without last-second swerves.

sec12-card-f19.question_text: What kind of information do blue highway guide signs point drivers toward?
sec12-card-f19.teaching_text: Hospitals, fuel, food, lodging, and rest areas appear on blue panels so travelers find help off exits.

sec12-card-r01.question_text: What destinations do brown-background road signs direct travelers toward?
sec12-card-r01.teaching_text: Separating parks, campgrounds, and historic sites onto brown boards keeps recreational turns distinct from highway exit signs.

sec12-card-r02.question_text: When highway responders post fluorescent pink warning signs, what kind of situation lies ahead?
sec12-card-r02.teaching_text: Unlike planned orange roadwork, fluorescent coral-pink alerts drivers to sudden crashes, floods, or emergency detours.

sec12-card-r03.question_text: How does a regulatory sign differ legally from an advisory or guide sign?
sec12-card-r03.teaching_text: Disobeying a regulatory sign breaks traffic law directly rather than merely skipping a helpful travel suggestion.

sec12-card-r04.question_text: How does right-of-way order work after stopping at an all-way stop intersection?
sec12-card-r04.teaching_text: Tracking who came to a complete halt first prevents hesitation standoffs and rolling collisions inside the box.

sec12-card-r05.question_text: When must a yield sign be treated as a full stop?
sec12-card-r05.teaching_text: Coasting through a busy yield approach without stopping for cross traffic or walkers causes a right-of-way crash.

sec12-card-r06.question_text: What does a square red-and-white Do Not Enter sign prohibit, and where is it critically placed?
sec12-card-r06.teaching_text: Driving past Do Not Enter at a highway exit ramp puts you nose-to-nose against fast freeway traffic.

sec12-card-r07.question_text: What should you prepare to do when you pass a Speed Zone Ahead sign?
sec12-card-r07.teaching_text: Easing off the accelerator early lets you match the lower town or school limit right at the boundary.

sec12-card-r08.question_text: When is driving slower than a posted freeway minimum speed limit legally allowed?
sec12-card-r08.teaching_text: Crawling below minimum speed on clear dry pavement creates a rear-end hazard; only bad weather or traffic excuses slowing.

sec12-card-r09.question_text: What urgent mistake does a red rectangular Wrong Way sign tell you that you have made?
sec12-card-r09.teaching_text: Seeing Wrong Way means you already passed the entrance barrier and must pull over safely before oncoming cars arrive.

sec12-card-r10.question_text: What universal symbol inside a regulatory sign tells you the pictured maneuver or vehicle is banned?
sec12-card-r10.teaching_text: Instant symbol recognition tells you turns, U-turns, bicycles, or trucks are barred even before reading any words.

sec12-card-r11.question_text: Why do paved crossovers in highway medians carry No U-Turn signs for everyday drivers?
sec12-card-r11.teaching_text: Slow civilian turnarounds from the fast left lane trigger high-speed freeway pileups, so crossovers stay emergency-only.

sec12-card-r12.question_text: What do No Right Turn and No Left Turn symbol signs forbid at an intersection or driveway?
sec12-card-r12.teaching_text: Turning into a prohibited arrow often sends you straight down a one-way street or across protected transit lanes.

sec12-card-r13.question_text: How must you travel when entering or driving along a street posted with One Way arrow signs?
sec12-card-r13.teaching_text: Every lane on a one-way street flows together, so turning against the arrow creates immediate head-on danger.

sec12-card-r14.question_text: What roadway feature and pavement markings match an overhead or roadside two-way left-turn lane sign?
sec12-card-r14.teaching_text: Yellow outer-and-inner striping paired with curved white arrows reserves the middle lane strictly for left turns.

sec12-card-r15.question_text: Which two normally legal red-light turns are both blocked when a No Turn on Red sign is posted?
sec12-card-r15.teaching_text: Drivers remember right-on-red bans easily, yet forget the exact same sign cancels one-way-to-one-way left turns on red.

sec12-card-r16.question_text: What layout ahead does an Approaching Divided Highway sign alert cross-street drivers to expect?
sec12-card-r16.teaching_text: Knowing a raised island separates opposing lanes stops you from accidentally turning left onto the wrong side.

sec12-card-r17.question_text: How must you steer past a traffic island, median nose, or center obstacle marked with a Keep Right sign?
sec12-card-r17.teaching_text: Passing left of a divided median nose puts your car head-on into opposing traffic lanes.

sec12-card-r18.question_text: Who must move into the right lane when a Slower Traffic Keep Right sign is posted?
sec12-card-r18.teaching_text: Camping in left lanes below surrounding flow forces faster drivers into risky right-side weaves and tailgating.

sec13-card-f01.question_text: Why do certain signalized intersections post a Stop Here on Red sign?
sec13-card-f01.teaching_text: Offset crosswalks, rail tracks, or tight truck-turning corners need a set-back stopping line so cars stay clear.

sec13-card-f02.question_text: What does a Road Closed sign tell every approaching driver?
sec13-card-f02.teaching_text: Driving around a Road Closed barricade can drop you into washed-out pavement, open trenches, or live work equipment.

sec13-card-f03.question_text: What maneuver does a rectangular Do Not Pass sign forbid, and what pavement striping often pairs with it?
sec13-card-f03.teaching_text: Roadside Do Not Pass posts back up solid yellow centerlines so snow-covered pavement never hides a blind zone.

sec13-card-f04.question_text: What does a Pass With Care sign mark, and does it guarantee you can overtake right away?
sec13-card-f04.teaching_text: Leaving a restricted zone lifts the legal ban, yet oncoming traffic or wet visibility can still block overtaking.

sec13-card-f05.question_text: How are dedicated bicycle lanes striped along a block, near an intersection corner, and for extra visibility?
sec13-card-f05.teaching_text: Dotted corner lines mark the conflict zone where right-turning drivers and straight-riding cyclists must watch each other.

sec13-card-f06.question_text: What shape do most hazard warning signs use, and how do yellow, orange, and yellow-green split up duties?
sec13-card-f06.teaching_text: Pairing diamond geometry with color lets your eyes separate permanent hazards, temporary roadwork, and pedestrian crossings instantly.

sec13-card-f07.question_text: Why should you scan both sides of the street when passing a pedestrian crosswalk warning sign?
sec13-card-f07.teaching_text: Marked pedestrian crossings often cut across mid-block trails or campuses where drivers are not expecting corner traffic.

sec13-card-f08.question_text: What purpose does a yellow flashing light mounted with a pedestrian crossing sign serve?
sec13-card-f08.teaching_text: Blinking amber lights draw your eyes to high-foot-traffic crossings early so walkers never catch you at full speed.

sec13-card-f09.question_text: What actions do school warning signs call for, and who may direct traffic at the crosswalk?
sec13-card-f09.teaching_text: Young students can dart unpredictably off curbs, and crossing guards or officers hold legal authority to halt lanes.

sec13-card-f10.question_text: Under what conditions or posted cues do Illinois reduced school-zone speed signs take effect?
sec13-card-f10.teaching_text: Never assume one fixed clock window everywhere because local plaques, flashing beacons, and visible children govern enforcement.

sec13-card-f11.question_text: How should you react to Stop Ahead, Yield Ahead, or Signal Ahead diamonds when you cannot see the intersection yet?
sec13-card-f11.teaching_text: Trees, curves, or hills often hide the red light or octagon until you are too close to brake smoothly.

sec13-card-f12.question_text: Why do rural highways and fast roads place advance warning signs much farther ahead of intersections?
sec13-card-f12.teaching_text: Braking distance climbs dramatically at fifty-five miles per hour, requiring early heads-up signs well upstream.

sec13-card-f13.question_text: What road situations ahead do crossroad, side-road, and T-junction warning diamonds alert you to?
sec13-card-f13.teaching_text: Spotting a hidden rural side road on a yellow diamond prepares your foot to cover the brake early.

sec13-card-f14.question_text: What two pieces of guidance do a curve-arrow diamond and its small square plaque underneath give you?
sec13-card-f14.teaching_text: Matching the small advisory plaque speed before entering the bend keeps tire traction from breaking loose mid-curve.

sec13-card-f15.question_text: What does a yellow Exit speed sign posted along a highway off-ramp tell you?
sec13-card-f15.teaching_text: Expressway off-ramps tighten into sharp loops fast, and carrying freeway speed onto the ramp risks rollovers.

sec13-card-f16.question_text: Why must you reduce speed when passing a Slippery When Wet warning sign in rain?
sec13-card-f16.teaching_text: Rain mixes with road oil on bridges and polished asphalt, cutting tire traction and stretching stopping distance.

sec13-card-f17.question_text: When should you slow down after seeing a truck-on-hill downgrade warning sign, and why?
sec13-card-f17.teaching_text: Gravity builds momentum rapidly on long, steep, or winding grades and can overheat brakes if you wait.

sec13-card-f18.question_text: What change in roadway width does a Narrow Bridge diamond warn you to expect ahead?
sec13-card-f18.teaching_text: Shoulders often vanish between bridge railings, requiring centered steering and extra caution around wide oncoming trucks.

sec13-card-f19.question_text: What does a lane-reduction warning tell you is happening ahead, and what two roles must drivers prepare for?
sec13-card-f19.teaching_text: Whether your lane ends or continues, smooth flow depends on ending-lane drivers signaling and open-lane drivers spacing out.

sec13-card-f20.question_text: When traffic is light approaching a lane drop, when does Illinois advise moving into the continuing lane?
sec13-card-f20.teaching_text: With plenty of open gaps around you, sliding into the through lane early avoids last-second cone squeezes.

sec13-card-r01.question_text: How should drivers use both lanes when traffic backs up heavily approaching a lane reduction?
sec13-card-r01.teaching_text: Filling both lanes to the merge point and alternating one-by-one shortens backups and keeps speeds uniform.

sec13-card-r02.question_text: What specific pavement change ahead does a Road Narrows warning sign indicate?
sec13-card-r02.teaching_text: Sudden edge drop-offs and tighter oncoming clearance leave less room for lane wander on rural two-lane roads.

sec13-card-r03.question_text: Which side of a two-lane, two-way highway holds the yellow No Passing Zone pennant?
sec13-card-r03.teaching_text: Mounting the pennant on the left places it directly in a prospective passer's line of sight.

sec13-card-r04.question_text: What happens ahead at a Merge warning diamond, and how should drivers in both streams respond?
sec13-card-r04.teaching_text: Safe highway merges take teamwork—either adjusting speed to open a gap or matching pace to enter cleanly.

sec13-card-r05.question_text: How does the Illinois handbook advise an expressway driver to help a vehicle entering from an on-ramp?
sec13-card-r05.teaching_text: Easing off the gas slightly opens a safe pocket when moving left is blocked by adjacent traffic.

sec13-card-r06.question_text: Which two kinds of road-alignment hazards can a horizontal arrow or chevron change-in-direction board mark?
sec13-card-r06.teaching_text: Large directional arrows right at the bend or bridge rail visually guide your eyes when alignment shifts sharply.

sec13-card-r07.question_text: How does a divided highway separate opposing lanes, and where are Divided Highway diamond warnings placed?
sec13-card-r07.teaching_text: Warning diamonds appear both before a median island starts and before it ends so you steer around median noses.

sec13-card-r08.question_text: What transition is happening when you pass a yellow diamond showing opposing up-and-down arrows?
sec13-card-r08.teaching_text: Forgetting your median barrier just ended can trick you into pulling into the left lane straight toward oncoming cars.

sec13-card-r09.question_text: What four adjustments should you make as soon as you spot an orange Workers Ahead diamond?
sec13-card-r09.teaching_text: Workers and heavy machines operate inches behind cones, leaving zero margin for speeding or hugging work barriers.

sec13-card-r10.question_text: What two jobs do orange cones, barrels, and barricades perform inside a construction zone?
sec13-card-r10.teaching_text: Temporary channelizing gear replaces normal lane paint around open trenches, equipment, and shifted lanes.

sec13-card-r11.question_text: Why are steady or flashing lights mounted atop work-zone barrels and barricades?
sec13-card-r11.teaching_text: Unlit temporary lane shifts blend into dark wet asphalt at night until amber warning lights outline the path.

sec13-card-r12.question_text: What do large illuminated arrow boards tell approaching drivers in a work zone?
sec13-card-r12.teaching_text: Bright lit arrows can be seen far back in traffic so drivers shift lanes smoothly before reaching barrels.

sec13-card-r13.question_text: How must you respond when you pass an orange Flagger Ahead symbol or text sign?
sec13-card-r13.teaching_text: Work-zone flaggers control alternating one-lane traffic around blind equipment, so ignoring their paddle risks a head-on crash.

sec13-card-r14.question_text: What kind of live updates appear on portable electronic highway message boards, and how should you treat them?
sec13-card-r14.teaching_text: Road crews update portable digital boards in real time as queues build or lanes shift ahead.

sec13-card-r15.question_text: How should you react upon spotting an orange-and-red triangle on the back of a slow-moving vehicle?
sec13-card-r15.teaching_text: Tractors and horse-drawn buggies crawl far below highway speed, creating a rapid closing-speed trap if you brake late.

sec13-card-r16.question_text: What navigation details do guide signs provide, and how do their shapes vary?
sec13-card-r16.teaching_text: While direction panels use wide rectangles, interstate, federal, and county route shields use distinct silhouettes.

sec13-card-r17.question_text: How do numbered route shields and their small helper plaques guide drivers along highways?
sec13-card-r17.teaching_text: Pairing an interstate, U.S., or Illinois shield with cardinal direction or arrow plaques keeps highway turns unmistakable.

sec13-card-r18.question_text: What three visual elements on hazardous-materials placards identify dangerous cargo on trucks or containers?
sec13-card-r18.teaching_text: Diamond cargo placards let responders and nearby drivers recognize explosives, flammables, or toxins from a safe distance.

sec13-card-r19.question_text: What should you do if you encounter a crash involving a truck displaying hazardous-materials placards?
sec13-card-r19.teaching_text: Approaching a wrecked hazmat rig exposes you to invisible toxic fumes, chemical spills, or sudden blast hazards.

sec13-card-r20.question_text: Why should you get medical care if you feel sick hours after being near a hazardous-materials incident?
sec13-card-r20.teaching_text: Inhaled fumes or chemical contact may not cause symptoms right at the scene, making prompt medical evaluation critical.

sec14-card-f01.question_text: Who can legally override traffic signals and markings, and what shortcut around a red light is illegal?
sec14-card-f01.teaching_text: Cutting through a corner gas station or parking lot to dodge a red light breaks Illinois signal-evasion law.

sec14-card-f02.question_text: In what exact position order do red, yellow, and green lenses appear on vertical and horizontal traffic lights?
sec14-card-f02.teaching_text: Standardized lens positions let drivers with color-vision differences read red at the top or far left instantly.

sec14-card-f03.question_text: How must drivers treat a dark or nonworking intersection traffic light when no officer is directing traffic?
sec14-card-f03.teaching_text: Never blow through a blacked-out main-street signal assuming cross-street drivers will stop for you.

sec14-card-f04.question_text: Where must you stop at a steady red light, and what two things are required before going straight?
sec14-card-f04.teaching_text: Even after green appears, waiting until cross traffic clears the box prevents broadside crashes with late runners.

sec14-card-f05.question_text: What must you do first—and what must be absent—before turning right at a steady red signal?
sec14-card-f05.teaching_text: Rolling through a right turn on red without halting behind the line endangers pedestrians stepping off the curb.

sec14-card-f06.question_text: Under what specific street layout is a left turn on a steady red light permitted in Illinois?
sec14-card-f06.teaching_text: Turning left on red from or onto a two-way street crosses oncoming lanes and remains illegal.

sec14-card-f07.question_text: What transition does a steady yellow traffic light announce, and what entry rule applies when red illuminates?
sec14-card-f07.teaching_text: Flooring the gas to beat a stale yellow often puts your front bumper across the line after red hits.

sec14-card-f08.question_text: Who still has the right-of-way even after your traffic signal turns green?
sec14-card-f08.teaching_text: A fresh green light gives permission to proceed safely, never a license to crowd walkers finishing their crossing.

sec14-card-f09.question_text: How must you handle a flashing red signal light at an intersection?
sec14-card-f09.teaching_text: Come to a complete stop first, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, and pull out only when clear.

sec14-card-f10.question_text: How should you drive through an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow signal?
sec14-card-f10.teaching_text: Cross-street drivers usually face stop signs or flashing red, yet easing speed lets you spot anyone misjudging your gap.

sec14-card-f11.question_text: Does a lit directional arrow let you drive immediately if pedestrians or vehicles are still clearing the intersection?
sec14-card-f11.teaching_text: Even protected green arrows require letting anyone already inside the crosswalk or box clear out safely.

sec14-card-f12.question_text: What does a steady red arrow forbid, and which turns remain allowed after stopping and yielding if unposted?
sec14-card-f12.teaching_text: Unlike states that ban all turns on red arrows, Illinois permits right or one-way-to-one-way left turns unless signed otherwise.

sec14-card-f13.question_text: What change in signal phase does a steady yellow arrow warn turning drivers to expect?
sec14-card-f13.teaching_text: Protected turning priority is wrapping up, so prepare to stop before a red light or arrow appears.

sec14-card-f14.question_text: What does a flashing yellow turn arrow permit you to do?
sec14-card-f14.teaching_text: Oncoming through traffic typically has a green light during a flashing yellow arrow, so wait for a safe gap.

sec14-card-f15.question_text: What movement does an upward-pointing green arrow allow compared with a left- or right-pointing green arrow?
sec14-card-f15.teaching_text: Turning from a lane controlled by a straight-up green arrow violates lane-use rules and cuts off adjacent traffic.

sec14-card-f16.question_text: What does an illuminated white walking-person pedestrian signal authorize?
sec14-card-f16.teaching_text: Turning drivers sharing that green phase must scan the crosswalk and yield to pedestrians stepping off the curb.

sec14-card-f17.question_text: How does a flashing orange raised-hand pedestrian signal apply to someone on the curb versus someone already crossing?
sec14-card-f17.teaching_text: Countdown flashing hands clear the street before cross traffic gets green, so curb-side walkers wait while mid-street walkers finish.

sec14-card-f18.question_text: What does a steady, non-flashing orange raised hand tell pedestrians at a crosswalk?
sec14-card-f18.teaching_text: Stepping into lanes against a solid orange hand puts pedestrians directly in front of green-light cross traffic.

sec14-card-f19.question_text: What does a lit red X suspended over a reversible highway or bridge lane mean?
sec14-card-f19.teaching_text: Reversible lanes switch flow by rush hour, so driving under an overhead red X risks a head-on collision.

sec14-card-f20.question_text: What should you do when you see a steady overhead yellow X above your lane?
sec14-card-f20.teaching_text: Reversible lane direction is about to flip to red, requiring a prompt, signaled lane change out.

sec14-card-f21.question_text: What single use does a flashing yellow overhead lane-control arrow allow?
sec14-card-f21.teaching_text: Both directions may share that reversible center lane for left turns, so never use it for through cruising.

sec14-card-f22.question_text: Does a downward-pointing green overhead lane-control arrow let you ignore intersection stop signs or red lights ahead?
sec14-card-f22.teaching_text: Overhead green arrows only confirm your lane flows forward—every intersection signal and speed sign still applies.

sec14-card-f23.question_text: How do solid white and solid yellow pavement edge lines tell you which side of a divided road is which?
sec14-card-f23.teaching_text: Seeing yellow on your right instead of your left at night instantly warns you are driving the wrong way.

sec14-card-f24.question_text: What direction is traffic moving in adjacent lanes separated by white lane lines?
sec14-card-f24.teaching_text: White between lanes confirms neighbors move with you rather than oncoming, guiding one-way and highway positioning.

sec14-card-r01.question_text: What lane movements are permitted across a dashed or broken white pavement line?
sec14-card-r01.teaching_text: Always mirror-check, clear your blind spot, and signal before moving across dashed white lines into another lane.

sec14-card-r02.question_text: What rule applies to crossing a single solid white line between same-direction lanes?
sec14-card-r02.teaching_text: Single solid white lines buffer intersection turn pockets and bike lanes where late weaving causes sideswipes.

sec14-card-r03.question_text: Are you allowed to change lanes across a double solid white pavement line?
sec14-card-r03.teaching_text: Double white barriers wall off express lanes, tunnels, or tight merges where crossing over is strictly illegal.

sec14-card-r04.question_text: What traffic flow relationship do yellow centerline markings always indicate?
sec14-card-r04.teaching_text: Any lane to the left of a yellow centerline carries oncoming vehicles heading straight toward your front bumper.

sec14-card-r05.question_text: When may you cross a single broken yellow centerline to pass a slower vehicle?
sec14-card-r05.teaching_text: Dashed yellow paint confirms open road geometry, yet you still need clear sight distance and zero no-pass zones.

sec14-card-r06.question_text: For what specific turns are you legally allowed to cross double solid yellow centerlines?
sec14-card-r06.teaching_text: Double yellow bans overtaking slower traffic, yet never traps you from turning left into or out of driveways.

sec14-card-r07.question_text: What two narrow exceptions allow crossing a solid yellow line painted on your side of the center?
sec14-card-r07.teaching_text: Starting a brand-new pass across solid yellow is illegal, though safely tucking back in or entering a driveway remains lawful.

sec14-card-r08.question_text: When a centerline pairs one broken yellow stripe with one solid yellow stripe, which lane is allowed to pass?
sec14-card-r08.teaching_text: Look right next to your left tire—broken yellow nearest you permits safe passing, whereas solid yellow locks you in.

sec14-card-r09.question_text: When a road provides a marked two-way center left-turn lane, may you turn left from the regular through lane instead?
