sec14-card-r09.teaching_text: Stopping in the fast through lane to turn left while an empty center turn lane sits beside you causes rear-end crashes.

sec14-card-r10.question_text: Which maneuvers are legally allowed inside a shared two-way left-turn lane?
sec14-card-r10.teaching_text: Never use the shared middle lane to overtake backed-up traffic or cruise down the block.

sec14-card-r11.question_text: How must your front bumper line up with a painted white stop line at a stop sign or red light?
sec14-card-r11.teaching_text: Stopping with your front wheels on the line pushes your nose into the pedestrian buffer or turning truck sweep.

sec14-card-r12.question_text: About how far ahead of the crosswalk is a white stop line typically painted on city streets?
sec14-card-r12.teaching_text: That four-foot setback shields pedestrians, strollers, and wheelchairs from overhanging bumpers at busy city corners.

sec14-card-r13.question_text: How are marked crosswalks painted across a roadway, and who holds right-of-way inside them?
sec14-card-r13.teaching_text: High-visibility diagonal bars make crossings stand out from afar so drivers yield before crowding pedestrians.

sec14-card-r14.question_text: Do marked pedestrian crosswalks appear only at street corners?
sec14-card-r14.teaching_text: Mid-block crossings carry identical pedestrian right-of-way as corner intersections, especially where roadside crossing signs stand.

sec14-card-r15.question_text: What do diagonal yellow or white pavement stripes warn you to steer around?
sec14-card-r15.teaching_text: Driving onto striped gore or island zones risks slamming into raised curbs, bridge piers, or attenuator barrels.

sec14-card-r16.question_text: Besides upright street signs, how can cities and towns mark zones where parking is banned?
sec14-card-r16.teaching_text: Looking only for metal posts while ignoring painted curbs or fire-lane stencils leads to tickets and tows.

sec14-card-r17.question_text: Up to how many feet ahead of railroad tracks can a round yellow advance-warning sign be posted?
sec14-card-r17.teaching_text: Rural highway speeds cover hundreds of feet quickly, so the circular warning gives early braking distance.

sec14-card-r18.question_text: What roles do the solid yellow centerline and the wide white transverse line play right before railroad tracks?
sec14-card-r18.teaching_text: Passing near tracks risks meeting a train or oncoming car, while stopping behind the white bar clears lowering gates.

sec14-card-r19.question_text: How must you treat a white X-shaped railroad crossbuck, and what does the smaller plaque underneath tell you?
sec14-card-r19.teaching_text: Knowing multiple tracks cross ahead warns you a second hidden train may arrive right behind the first.

sec14-card-r20.question_text: After a train clears a crossing, when may you proceed if the red warning lights are still flashing?
sec14-card-r20.teaching_text: Pulling onto tracks the instant a caboose clears while lights keep flashing can put you under a second oncoming train.

sec14-card-r21.question_text: What two conditions must finish before crossing gated railroad tracks, and what gate maneuvers are strictly forbidden?
sec14-card-r21.teaching_text: Weaving around lowered arms or racing descending gates gambles your life against fast, unstoppable freight momentum.

sec14-card-r22.question_text: What details can automated railroad-crossing cameras capture, and what two penalties can follow?
sec14-card-r22.teaching_text: Even without an officer nearby, crossing-camera evidence records your plate and time to trigger steep fines or suspension.

sec14-card-r23.question_text: What two critical pieces of information appear on the railroad emergency-notification sign posted at every crossing?
sec14-card-r23.teaching_text: Calling the posted railroad dispatch number with the unique crossing identifier lets operators halt approaching trains immediately.

sec15-card-f01.question_text: How should you anticipate other drivers' moves, and what principle guides you if a crash becomes unavoidable?
sec15-card-f01.teaching_text: Staying calm instead of freezing lets you steer toward bushes or a glancing blow rather than a head-on impact.

sec15-card-f02.question_text: How do you use a fixed roadside landmark to measure Illinois's three-second following rule?
sec15-card-f02.teaching_text: Reaching that signpost or shadow before finishing a full three-second count proves you are tailgating.

sec15-card-f03.question_text: What conditions does the three-second following gap assume, and when must you add extra seconds?
sec15-card-f03.teaching_text: Rain, snow, darkness, or rough pavement stretch braking runs well past what a dry three-second cushion covers.

sec15-card-f04.question_text: What two options does Illinois recommend when another driver follows you too closely?
sec15-card-f04.teaching_text: Moving into another lane or easing off the roadway clears aggressive bumper-riders ahead of you instead of behind you.

sec15-card-f05.question_text: At twenty-five miles per hour, roughly how many feet per second do you cover and how long is a three-second gap?
sec15-card-f05.teaching_text: Even on a quiet neighborhood street, three seconds equals more than six car lengths of stopping room.

sec15-card-f06.question_text: At thirty-five miles per hour, what approximate distance per second and three-second following gap does the Illinois chart list?
sec15-card-f06.teaching_text: Stepping up just ten miles per hour adds forty-five extra feet to your minimum three-second cushion.

sec15-card-f07.question_text: At forty-five miles per hour, how many feet do you travel each second and across a three-second gap?
sec15-card-f07.teaching_text: Covering sixty-six feet every second means a two-second phone glance eats over one hundred thirty feet blind.

sec15-card-f08.question_text: At fifty-five miles per hour, what feet-per-second pace and three-second distance does the Illinois table show?
sec15-card-f08.teaching_text: Two hundred forty-three feet approaches the length of a football field between your front bumper and lead taillights.

sec15-card-f09.question_text: At sixty-five miles per hour, roughly how far do you travel per second and across three seconds?
sec15-card-f09.teaching_text: At nearly a hundred feet every second, tight freeway packs leave zero margin when lead brake lights flash.

sec15-card-f10.question_text: At seventy miles per hour, what approximate one-second travel and three-second following distance appear in the chart?
sec15-card-f10.teaching_text: Over three hundred feet — an entire football field — separates safe interstate following from bumper-riding at seventy.

sec15-card-f11.question_text: How should weather, traffic, and road surface shape your speed — and why can creeping far too slowly also cause danger?
sec15-card-f11.teaching_text: Speeding past road grip causes skids, while crawling needlessly slow on clear highways triggers sudden rear-end closures.

sec15-card-f12.question_text: Which six human, mechanical, and environmental factors must your chosen travel speed take into account?
sec15-card-f12.teaching_text: Worn brakes, gusting crosswinds, or tired reflexes lengthen stopping distance even when the speedometer reads under the sign.

sec15-card-f13.question_text: Does drowsiness hurt driving before you actually nod off — and what two trip habits prevent fatigue?
sec15-card-f13.teaching_text: Heavy eyelids slow braking decisions long before microsleep hits, making pre-trip sleep and regular rest stops essential.

sec15-card-f14.question_text: What two visual habits help keep your eyes alert and engaged on long drives?
sec15-card-f14.teaching_text: Moving your gaze across mirrors, edges, and road signs breaks the hypnotic highway stare that lulls drivers.

sec15-card-f15.question_text: What is the best choice when fog rolls in — and what three adjustments belong if you must drive?
sec15-card-f15.teaching_text: Disabling cruise control keeps your right foot poised to lift smoothly the instant hazy taillights loom ahead.

sec15-card-f16.question_text: Which lights belong in fog, how fast may you travel, and how should you react upon spotting another car's lights?
sec15-card-f16.teaching_text: Spotting faint headlamps or taillights ahead in fog could mean a stopped or turning vehicle right in your lane.

sec15-card-f17.question_text: Why must you pull off the road and stop in blinding fog instead of creeping forward at five to ten miles per hour?
sec15-card-f17.teaching_text: Creeping down live lanes at five miles per hour turns your trunk into an invisible wall for faster traffic.

sec15-card-f18.question_text: How should you adjust turn signals and braking timing when driving in fog?
sec15-card-f18.teaching_text: Flashing blinkers and brake lights extra early gives fog-delayed drivers behind you precious feet to react.

sec15-card-f19.question_text: When does rain require turning on your headlights in Illinois, and why is initial light rain extra slick?
sec15-card-f19.teaching_text: Light opening drizzle mixes with road oil and grime into a slick glaze right when visibility drops.

sec15-card-f20.question_text: What cruise-control, spacing, and maneuvering changes belong whenever you drive in rain?
sec15-card-f20.teaching_text: Wet asphalt cuts cornering and braking grip while cruise control can spin wet tires before you react.

sec15-card-f21.question_text: How do you prevent hydroplaning, and what should your right foot do if an uncontrollable hydroplaning skid starts?
sec15-card-f21.teaching_text: Releasing the accelerator lets water clear from beneath your treads naturally so the skid runs out without spinning.

sec15-card-f22.question_text: Why must you turn around instead of driving across a flooded roadway or underpass viaduct?
sec15-card-f22.teaching_text: Standing water hides washed-out pavement and swift currents deep enough to stall engines or sweep cars away.

sec15-card-f23.question_text: How should you drive in strong winds, especially when emerging from wind shelter or passing trucks and buses?
sec15-card-f23.teaching_text: Leaving an overpass, tree line, or semi trailer exposes your car side to sudden crosswind shoves.

sec15-card-f24.question_text: Why does strong wind often demand more than steering grip alone?
sec15-card-f24.teaching_text: Gale gusts frequently strike alongside driving rain or sleet, combining lateral shoves with reduced tire traction.

sec15-card-f25.question_text: Which towed vehicles are prohibited on the Illinois toll-road system during high winds?
sec15-card-f25.teaching_text: Tall, slab-sided house trailers catch crosswinds like sails and can overturn across live tollway lanes.

sec15-card-r01.question_text: Besides slowing down and widening gaps in winter, why can't you trust one stretch of pavement to match the next?
sec15-card-r01.teaching_text: Sun-warmed blacktop can turn instantly into glare ice beneath tree shadows or wind-chilled overpasses.

sec15-card-r02.question_text: On which three slick road conditions must cruise control remain turned off?
sec15-card-r02.teaching_text: Manual pedal control lets you lift off instantly the split-second a tire loses bite on slick pavement.

sec15-card-r03.question_text: Which four clearing, defrosting, fluid, and lighting steps belong before setting out on a winter drive?
sec15-card-r03.teaching_text: Starting out through a tiny scraped peephole or with snow-caked taillights invites collisions before your first turn.

sec15-card-r04.question_text: Which five vehicle systems must stay in reliable working order for winter driving?
sec15-card-r04.teaching_text: Freezing cold exposes weak radiators, streaky wipers, and uneven brakes right when stopping margins shrink.

sec15-card-r05.question_text: What limit still applies even when your vehicle wears snow tires or permitted tire chains?
sec15-card-r05.teaching_text: Overconfident drivers on snow tires still slide off icy curves when they try driving dry-weather speeds.

sec15-card-r06.question_text: How should you use your brakes when approaching a winter stop so you can feel available grip?
sec15-card-r06.teaching_text: Starting gentle, steady braking well ahead reveals slick ice early while leaving space to ease smoothly down.

sec15-card-r07.question_text: Which four roadway features stay icy long after surrounding pavement dries out?
sec15-card-r07.teaching_text: Cold air circulates both above and underneath elevated bridge and overpass decks, freezing moisture first and thawing last.

sec15-card-r08.question_text: Which three emergency items does Illinois suggest carrying in winter, and where should you stay if stranded?
sec15-card-r08.teaching_text: Staying inside your visible vehicle with warm gear beats wandering lost in blinding subzero windchill.

sec15-card-r09.question_text: If you are stranded in winter snow, what exterior part of your vehicle should you keep clear if possible?
sec15-card-r09.teaching_text: A snow-plugged tailpipe forces deadly, odorless carbon monoxide backward into the passenger cabin while idling for heat.

sec15-card-r10.question_text: What four actions belong in an expressway acceleration lane before merging into highway traffic?
sec15-card-r10.teaching_text: Reaching highway flow speed on the ramp lets you slip seamlessly into a gap without forcing panic braking.

sec15-card-r11.question_text: Which mirror checks and communication step must come before changing lanes on an expressway?
sec15-card-r11.teaching_text: High expressway speeds close gaps rapidly, so checking both mirror views before signaling prevents high-speed sideswipes.

sec15-card-r12.question_text: How should you manage forward space, slower travel, and the left lane on an Illinois expressway?
sec15-card-r12.teaching_text: Camping continuously in the left passing lane clogs traffic flow and provokes dangerous right-side overtaking.

sec15-card-r13.question_text: If mechanical trouble forces an expressway stop, what three warning steps apply — and what walking rule holds?
sec15-card-r13.teaching_text: Walking along a high-speed expressway shoulder exposes pedestrians to distracted seventy-mile-per-hour drift.

sec15-card-r14.question_text: Because expressway exits can sit on either side, when should you choose your lane, signal, and slow down?
sec15-card-r14.teaching_text: Waiting until you enter the deceleration lane to brake keeps main expressway lanes flowing smoothly behind you.

sec15-card-r15.question_text: What must you do if you pass your expressway exit — and why is reversing off-limits?
sec15-card-r15.teaching_text: Backing up on an expressway or shoulder is strictly illegal and sets up catastrophic high-speed collisions.

sec15-card-r16.question_text: At a lane drop, how does proper merge timing differ between light traffic and heavy slow congestion?
sec15-card-r16.teaching_text: Using both lanes up to the merge point and alternating turns in slow congestion cuts backup length dramatically.

sec15-card-r17.question_text: How should you maintain your headlights, and how does their beam reach govern nighttime speed?
sec15-card-r17.teaching_text: Dirty or misaimed bulbs shrink your lit stopping zone while blinding oncoming traffic.

sec15-card-r18.question_text: When must headlights run at night, and at what exact distances must you dim high beams for oncoming or overtaken cars?
sec15-card-r18.teaching_text: Illinois tests both numbers constantly — five hundred feet facing oncoming headlamps and three hundred feet behind taillights.

sec15-card-r19.question_text: How should you set dashboard brightness, sun visors, and dome lights for sharper night vision?
sec15-card-r19.teaching_text: Bright interior dome or gauge glare shrinks your pupils and reflects across windshield glass after dark.

sec15-card-r20.question_text: Which painted stripes help guide your lane position at night, and where must you avoid stopping?
sec15-card-r20.teaching_text: Reflective edge and center lines anchor your path past oncoming glare, while stopping on dark lanes invites rear-end hits.

sec15-card-r21.question_text: How should you approach every rural intersection, even when no warning sign appears?
sec15-card-r21.teaching_text: Tall cornfields, brush, or dips hide fast cross-road pickups at unsigned country corners.

sec15-card-r22.question_text: When should you shed speed for a curve, what pedal mistake can trigger a skid, and where must your car stay?
sec15-card-r22.teaching_text: Entering too hot and stabbing the brakes mid-turn unloads rear grip and slides you across the centerline.

sec15-card-r23.question_text: If an oncoming vehicle drifts head-on into your lane, what three immediate actions should you take?
sec15-card-r23.teaching_text: Always escape toward the right shoulder — swerving left risks colliding if the distracted driver snaps back right.

sec15-card-r24.question_text: Once tires lose traction and start skidding, how should you use the pedals and steering wheel to recover?
sec15-card-r24.teaching_text: Lifting off gas and brake while steering where the rear slides restores rolling grip before you counter-steer straight.

sec15-card-r25.question_text: If your tires drop off the pavement edge onto the shoulder, what five calm steps bring you safely back onto the road?
sec15-card-r25.teaching_text: Yanking the wheel sharply at speed against a pavement lip slingshots cars sideways into oncoming traffic.

sec16-card-f01.question_text: If smoke starts coming from your vehicle, what four actions must you take — and what should you never attempt yourself?
sec16-card-f01.teaching_text: Vehicle fires spread explosively through fuel and wiring, so step well clear and call nine one one instead of fighting flames.

sec16-card-f02.question_text: If your vehicle plunges into water without sinking right away, how should you escape and why?
sec16-card-f02.teaching_text: Outside water pressure pins car doors shut almost immediately, making an open or broken side window your lifeline.

sec16-card-f03.question_text: Which lethal gas is present in fuel-burning vehicle exhaust?
sec16-card-f03.teaching_text: Carbon monoxide has no color or smell, allowing lethal levels to build silently inside enclosed cabins or garages.

sec16-card-f04.question_text: Which physical symptoms signal carbon-monoxide poisoning, and what common illness can it mimic?
sec16-card-f04.teaching_text: Mistaking sudden cabin headaches, dizziness, or nausea for ordinary flu delays getting fresh air before unconsciousness hits.

sec16-card-f05.question_text: Why is napping inside a running vehicle or idling inside a garage frequently fatal?
sec16-card-f05.teaching_text: Carbon monoxide overcomes sleeping occupants or fills enclosed garages before anyone wakes up to notice warning signs.

sec16-card-f06.question_text: Who inside a car can be harmed by carbon monoxide, and which groups face heightened danger?
sec16-card-f06.teaching_text: While exhaust fumes poison every passenger, babies, seniors, and anyone with heart, lung, or blood conditions succumb fastest.

sec16-card-f07.question_text: How often should a mechanic inspect your exhaust system, and what home-garage rule applies?
sec16-card-f07.teaching_text: Rusted muffler pinholes leak fumes upward, and running an engine in an attached garage seeps gas indoors.

sec16-card-f08.question_text: If live utility lines fall across your vehicle in a crash, where should occupants stay — and what single exception applies?
sec16-card-f08.teaching_text: Rubber tires help isolate the cabin until utility crews cut power, whereas stepping out completes a lethal circuit.

sec16-card-f09.question_text: If fire forces you out of a vehicle touching downed power lines, how must you clear the car?
sec16-card-f09.teaching_text: Touching the metal body and the ground at the same instant sends high-voltage current straight through your body.

sec16-card-f10.question_text: Once you jump clear of an electrified vehicle, how should you land and move fifty feet away?
sec16-card-f10.teaching_text: Keeping both feet tight together while hopping or shuffling prevents voltage differences across wide steps from shocking you.

sec16-card-f11.question_text: Which three safety rules apply every time you refuel at a gas pump?
sec16-card-f11.teaching_text: Shutting the engine off, skipping flames, and staying beside the nozzle prevent vapor flash fires and spills.

sec16-card-f12.question_text: What sound often precedes a tire blowout, and what four calm actions bring you safely off the road?
sec16-card-f12.teaching_text: Thumping rubber pulls hard toward the flat side, and slamming the brakes locks wheels into a spin.

sec16-card-f13.question_text: How should you respond if a wheel or tire separates from your vehicle at speed?
sec16-card-f13.teaching_text: Holding the wheel firmly, easing off the throttle, and skipping hard braking keeps a three-wheel car upright.

sec16-card-f14.question_text: If your steering fails completely, what pedal, light, and braking steps bring the vehicle down safely?
sec16-card-f14.teaching_text: Hard braking without steering control can pitch the car sideways across lanes instead of coasting down straight.

sec16-card-f15.question_text: Why must you never turn off the ignition while rolling during a steering emergency?
sec16-card-f15.teaching_text: Shutting the key off kills power-steering assist or clicks the steering-column lock shut while still rolling.

sec16-card-f16.question_text: If your brake pedal suddenly sinks to the floor, what should you try first — and what two backups slow you down?
sec16-card-f16.teaching_text: Rapid pumping can build enough residual hydraulic pressure to bite before you combine downshifting with the parking brake.

sec16-card-r01.question_text: Which backup lights help you get off the road if headlights suddenly go dark — and how should you handle dimming bulbs?
sec16-card-r01.teaching_text: Hazard, parking, or turn blinkers throw just enough glow to guide you onto the shoulder before total darkness.

sec16-card-r02.question_text: If your accelerator sticks down and cannot be freed, what gear and braking response slows the car?
sec16-card-r02.teaching_text: Moving the selector to neutral disconnects surging engine power from the wheels immediately while keeping power steering alive.

sec16-card-r03.question_text: If your hood flies up or mud blocks your forward windshield view, how do you see to pull off?
sec16-card-r03.teaching_text: Rolling down the driver window lets you sight along the pavement edge while four-way flashers warn traffic behind.

sec16-card-r04.question_text: How does Illinois define aggressive driving?
sec16-card-r04.teaching_text: Any deliberate traffic behavior that puts surrounding lives or vehicles in danger crosses into aggressive operation.

sec16-card-r05.question_text: Which five dangerous moving violations does the manual highlight as examples of potentially aggressive driving?
sec16-card-r05.teaching_text: Combining excessive speed with red-light running, shoulder passes, or sharp cutoffs strips nearby drivers of reaction space.

sec16-card-r06.question_text: Which four retaliatory or hostile behaviors behind the wheel count as aggressive acts?
sec16-card-r06.teaching_text: Slamming brakes on a tailgater or flashing beams and gestures escalates minor traffic friction into road rage.

sec16-card-r07.question_text: How should you respond — including where you look — when encountering an angry driver?
sec16-card-r07.teaching_text: Refusing to stare back or trade gestures starves road rage of the personal confrontation angry drivers seek.

sec16-card-r08.question_text: How should you secure your cabin and stop behind traffic when an aggressive driver is nearby?
sec16-card-r08.teaching_text: Locked doors, rolled-up windows, and room to steer around the car ahead keep you from being boxed in.

sec16-card-r09.question_text: What mindset warning does the Illinois manual give about another driver's potential for aggression?
sec16-card-r09.teaching_text: Assuming a furious stranger will stay reasonable can trap you in an escalating confrontation.

sec16-card-r10.question_text: How do high-capacity roadways differ from low-capacity roads in traffic volume, lanes, features, and speed?
sec16-card-r10.teaching_text: Knowing which road class you are on determines whether staying belted inside or stepping behind a barrier is safer.

sec16-card-r11.question_text: If you break down on a high-capacity highway, what five steps keep you safe while waiting for responders?
sec16-card-r11.teaching_text: On busy multilane highways, staying belted inside with hazards flashing and calling nine one one beats standing near fast lanes.

sec16-card-r12.question_text: What is your first positioning goal during a breakdown on a lower-capacity road?
sec16-card-r12.teaching_text: Getting completely off narrow travel lanes onto the right shoulder prevents blind-curve rear-end collisions.

sec16-card-r13.question_text: If you must exit a disabled car on a lower-capacity road and it is safe, which door side and waiting spot belong?
sec16-card-r13.teaching_text: Stepping out away from live lanes and waiting behind a guardrail or on a sidewalk shields you from drifters.

sec16-card-r14.question_text: What three actions apply if you cannot safely exit a disabled vehicle?
sec16-card-r14.teaching_text: Whenever traffic, terrain, or weather blocks a safe exit, seat belts and steel doors offer your best shield.

sec16-card-r15.question_text: If you break down on an Illinois toll road, how should you position and secure yourself — and which two numbers summon help?
sec16-card-r15.teaching_text: Dialing Illinois's star-nine-nine-nine helpline or emergency dispatch sends tollway roadside patrol while you wait safely belted inside.

sec17-card-f01.question_text: What general equipment standard must every Illinois vehicle meet, and when is driving a vehicle illegal?
sec17-card-f01.teaching_text: Taking a mechanically unsafe car onto public streets endangers everyone around you and breaks Illinois equipment law.

sec17-card-f02.question_text: How many brake systems and wheel brakes must a passenger car have — and what exception applies to motor-driven cycles?
sec17-card-f02.teaching_text: Dual independent systems ensure you can still slow a passenger car if primary hydraulic pressure fails.

sec17-card-f03.question_text: From twenty miles per hour, within how many feet must your main foot brake stop the vehicle?
sec17-card-f03.teaching_text: Needing more than thirty feet from twenty miles per hour warns that worn pads or fluid need service.

sec17-card-f04.question_text: From twenty miles per hour, within what distance must the parking brake stop your car — and what hill test applies?
sec17-card-f04.teaching_text: Your backup brake must both halt a rolling car within fifty-five feet and anchor it parked on grades.

sec17-card-f05.question_text: How many headlamps does a car require, and which two lighting or weather conditions mandate turning them on?
sec17-card-f05.teaching_text: Both sunset-to-sunrise darkness and any rain or snow requiring wipers make running two working headlamps mandatory.

sec17-card-f06.question_text: At what forward visibility distance does the Illinois manual also recommend switching on your headlights?
sec17-card-f06.teaching_text: Heavy overcast, smoke, or mist hiding objects a thousand feet ahead calls for headlamps even without wipers.

sec17-card-f07.question_text: At how many feet must you dim high beams before meeting an oncoming vehicle or overtaking one ahead?
sec17-card-f07.teaching_text: Dropping to low beams at five hundred oncoming and three hundred behind keeps bright glare out of eyes.

sec17-card-f08.question_text: How far ahead must a motorcycle or moped headlamp reach, and when must it stay switched on?
sec17-card-f08.teaching_text: Keeping that five-hundred-foot single headlamp burning on every daytime and nighttime ride helps drivers spot narrow bikes.

sec17-card-f09.question_text: Does Illinois allow tinted or smoked covers over vehicle lamp lenses?
sec17-card-f09.teaching_text: Darkened lens covers cut critical brake-light and headlight visibility when rain or sun glare hits.

sec17-card-f10.question_text: How many red rear lamps must a car carry versus a motorcycle or moped, and how far back must they show?
sec17-card-f10.teaching_text: Visible red taillights five hundred feet back prevent fast nighttime closures on unlit rural roads.

sec17-card-f11.question_text: How far must standard front and rear turn signals be visible, and which three vehicle types are excluded from that entry?
sec17-card-f11.teaching_text: Standard vehicles need front and rear blinkers visible three hundred feet away, with separate rules covering bikes and trailers.

sec17-card-f12.question_text: What color lamp must illuminate your rear license plate, from what distance must it read, and when must it turn on?
sec17-card-f12.teaching_text: Wiring the white plate bulb to glow with your headlamps keeps plate characters readable fifty feet back.

sec17-card-f13.question_text: What lights are required on a vehicle stopped along a highway at night, and what local exception can apply?
sec17-card-f13.teaching_text: Unlit cars parked along dark highways invite high-speed strikes unless local town rules permit unlit curb parking.

sec17-card-f14.question_text: How many front seat-belt sets must a passenger car have, and which model-year cutoff bars beltless sale or operation?
sec17-card-f14.teaching_text: Any passenger vehicle built from nineteen sixty-five onward needs installed front belts to be sold or driven legally.

sec17-card-f15.question_text: How far behind your car must at least one rearview mirror give a clear view?
sec17-card-f15.teaching_text: Seeing at least two hundred feet straight back lets you spot fast-closing traffic before signaling or braking.

sec17-card-f16.question_text: What glass standard applies to vehicle windows, and which four hazards must stay off your windshield?
sec17-card-f16.teaching_text: Laminated safety glass resists shattering into shards, while frost, fog, or deep cracks distort hazard judgment.

sec17-card-f17.question_text: What obstruction rule applies to the space between the driver and the front or rear windows?
sec17-card-f17.teaching_text: Dangling charms, stacked cargo, or window decals create blind zones big enough to hide pedestrians and cyclists.

sec17-card-f18.question_text: What is Illinois's rule on windshield tinting, and how deep may the sole allowed top strip extend?
sec17-card-f18.teaching_text: Tinting lower windshield glass dims night vision, so Illinois restricts tint to a six-inch top sunband.

sec17-card-r01.question_text: Which three weather accumulations must working windshield wipers be able to clear?
sec17-card-r01.teaching_text: Split or brittle wiper blades smear winter slush right across your sightline when road spray peaks.

sec17-card-r02.question_text: From what distance must your horn be heard — and who alone may carry sirens, whistles, or bells?
sec17-card-r02.teaching_text: Everyday cars need a two-hundred-foot warning horn while reserving emergency sound gear strictly for authorized responders.

sec17-card-r03.question_text: What two outputs must a muffler control, and which exhaust alterations are illegal in Illinois?
sec17-card-r03.teaching_text: Installing loud exhaust cutouts, bypasses, or straight-pipe modifications violates state noise and equipment laws.

sec17-card-r04.question_text: Which weight class of vehicles — plus which recreational category — must carry both front and rear bumpers?
sec17-card-r04.teaching_text: Matching bumper heights on everyday vehicles under nine thousand pounds and RVs absorbs crash energy safely.

sec17-card-r05.question_text: When cargo sticks out four feet or more past your rear bumper, how must you mark it by day versus night?
sec17-card-r05.teaching_text: Unmarked lumber or pipes jutting four feet back look invisible until a trailing driver spears into them.

sec17-card-r06.question_text: Which two colors are legal for backup lamps, and when must those lamps stay switched off?
sec17-card-r06.teaching_text: Burning white or amber reverse lights while rolling forward confuses trailing drivers into thinking you are backing toward them.

sec17-card-r07.question_text: How many spotlights may a vehicle carry, and how must you aim one when approaching another vehicle?
sec17-card-r07.teaching_text: Keeping a single spotlight aimed away from the left and inside one hundred feet avoids blinding oncoming traffic.

sec17-card-r08.question_text: At most how many lamps rated at three hundred candlepower may a vehicle burn at once?
sec17-card-r08.teaching_text: Capping three-hundred-candlepower lamps at four prevents aftermarket light bars from overwhelming oncoming drivers at night.

sec17-card-r09.question_text: Aside from turn signals and hazard flashers, who may use flashing or moving lamps on Illinois roads?
sec17-card-r09.teaching_text: Banning novelty strobes on private cars ensures drivers immediately recognize genuine police and emergency beacons.

sec17-card-r10.question_text: Which vehicles are the only ones allowed to display red lights visible from the front?
sec17-card-r10.teaching_text: Forward-showing red lamps signal urgent emergency response, so private vehicles can never mount red grille lights.

sec17-card-r11.question_text: How many running-board lights are permitted per side, and what colors and glare standard apply?
sec17-card-r11.teaching_text: Limiting side step lamps to one soft white or amber bulb per side lights entry steps without distracting traffic.

sec17-card-r12.question_text: What count, glare rule, and color choices govern cowl or fender lights?
sec17-card-r12.teaching_text: Restricting fender accent lighting to two nonglaring white or amber bulbs prevents confusion with emergency colors.

sec17-card-r13.question_text: Are metal-studded tires generally legal in Illinois — and which vehicles qualify for the November fifteenth to April first exception?
sec17-card-r13.teaching_text: Metal studs chew up bare pavement, so Illinois limits winter exemptions strictly to rural mail carriers and eligible disability plates.

sec17-card-r14.question_text: Where must a disability-plate vehicle owner live to qualify for Illinois's seasonal studded-tire exception?
sec17-card-r14.teaching_text: Township and county roads outside city limits stay snow-packed longer than plowed municipal streets.

sec17-card-r15.question_text: Which slow work machines are also exempt from Illinois's studded-tire ban, and below what speed?
sec17-card-r15.teaching_text: Farm equipment and heavy graders creeping under ten miles per hour need extra bite without tearing up highway lanes.

sec17-card-r16.question_text: What does Illinois law say about a moving vehicle's TV/video screen in the driver's view or watching live phone video?
sec17-card-r16.teaching_text: Streaming shows on dash monitors or phones steals visual attention completely away from live lanes.

sec17-card-r17.question_text: How do equipment rules for lamps, brakes, and turn signals apply to vehicles more than twenty-five years old?
sec17-card-r17.teaching_text: Classic cars over twenty-five years old follow tailored historical rules for lights, brakes, and signals.

sec17-card-r18.question_text: Is possessing or operating a police radar jammer allowed inside any Illinois vehicle?
sec17-card-r18.teaching_text: Illinois bans even keeping a radar-jamming device inside a car or commercial rig, whether switched on or not.

sec18-card-f01.question_text: Within how many days after a dealer vehicle sale must paperwork go in, and what documents and separate payments belong?
sec18-card-f01.teaching_text: Licensed dealers handle your application, signed title or origin certificate, and split checks for fees versus sales tax within twenty days.

sec18-card-f02.question_text: What causes the sales-tax rate on a dealership vehicle purchase to vary in Illinois?
sec18-card-f02.teaching_text: Local municipal and county tax rates change the exact sales-tax bill depending on where the purchase takes place.

sec18-card-f03.question_text: When you buy a car from a private seller, what four items must reach the state agency within twenty days?
sec18-card-f03.teaching_text: Private buyers must submit the application, seller-signed title, title/plate fees, and vehicle-use tax within twenty days.

sec18-card-f04.question_text: How is private-party vehicle-use tax calculated below fifteen thousand dollars versus at or above fifteen thousand?
sec18-card-f04.teaching_text: Fifteen thousand dollars flips the private-sale tax table from vehicle model year over to actual purchase price.

sec18-card-f05.question_text: Which tax form and state department receive your private-party vehicle-use tax payment?
sec18-card-f05.teaching_text: Private vehicle-use tax goes on form R U T fifty directly to the Illinois Department of Revenue.

sec18-card-f06.question_text: Along with the application, fees, tax, and bill of sale, what ownership proof does an out-of-state new or used purchase need?
sec18-card-f06.teaching_text: New out-of-state cars require the dealer-signed certificate of origin, while used ones need the assigned title.

sec18-card-f07.question_text: What extra document must you include when transferring existing Illinois plates onto an out-of-state vehicle purchase?
sec18-card-f07.teaching_text: Attaching your current registration identification card links your existing Illinois plates cleanly to the newly acquired vehicle.

sec18-card-f08.question_text: How does vehicle registration differ in legal purpose from an Illinois certificate of title?
sec18-card-f08.teaching_text: Confusing the two is a classic exam trap — titles prove legal ownership while registration authorizes public-road travel.

sec18-card-f09.question_text: Do vehicles and mobile homes still require an Illinois title even when they are not registered for road use?
sec18-card-f09.teaching_text: Parked cars and stationary mobile homes still need an official title to establish legal ownership.

sec18-card-f10.question_text: How often do registration fees renew, and what late penalty triggers more than one month past expiration?
sec18-card-f10.teaching_text: Waiting past one full month after your plate sticker expires tacks twenty extra dollars onto renewal.

sec18-card-f11.question_text: What annual registration fee does the manual list for a passenger car or qualifying truck up to eight thousand pounds?
sec18-card-f11.teaching_text: Standard passenger cars and light B-truck plates up to eight thousand pounds share that one-hundred-fifty-one-dollar rate.

sec18-card-f12.question_text: How do the listed annual registration fees compare between a motorcycle and an autocycle?
sec18-card-f12.teaching_text: Three-wheeled enclosed autocycles carry a seventy-one-dollar registration fee compared with forty-one dollars for motorcycles.

sec18-card-f13.question_text: What replacement fees does the manual list for one lost plate, two plates, and a replacement registration sticker?
sec18-card-f13.teaching_text: Replacing a lost renewal sticker costs twenty dollars — more than twice the nine-dollar fee for two metal plates.

sec18-card-f14.question_text: Why can custom plate totals exceed standard rates, and what can change the handbook's published fee schedule?
sec18-card-f14.teaching_text: Personalized and vanity plates add extra charges, and new state laws can revise published registration numbers.

sec18-card-f15.question_text: Where must your vehicle-registration card be kept whenever you are driving?
sec18-card-f15.teaching_text: Police stops require immediate registration proof either stored inside the glovebox or carried in your wallet.

sec18-card-f16.question_text: Where must cars, trucks, and vans mount license plates — and what rules govern frames and covers?
sec18-card-f16.teaching_text: Clear or tinted plastic plate covers are illegal in Illinois, and frames can never hide state names or sticker dates.

sec18-card-f17.question_text: Which five vehicle categories display just one license plate mounted on the rear?
sec18-card-f17.teaching_text: Motorcycles, mopeds, trailers, semitrailers, and apportioned buses carry a single rear plate instead of two.

sec18-card-f18.question_text: Which two commercial truck categories mount their single license plate on the front bumper?
sec18-card-f18.teaching_text: Because truck tractors haul swapped semitrailers behind them, Illinois puts their lone plate up front.

sec18-card-f19.question_text: What must you do with the license plates when selling your vehicle in Illinois, and why?
sec18-card-f19.teaching_text: Leaving your Illinois plates bolted onto a sold car risks toll bills and tickets tied to your name.

sec18-card-f20.question_text: Where does an Illinois temporary registration permit mount, how long does it last, and what if metal plates arrive late?
sec18-card-f20.teaching_text: Mounting the ninety-day TRP in the rear plate bracket keeps your car legal, with reissuance possible if plates lag.

sec18-card-f21.question_text: What two steps must you take with your temporary permit once permanent metal plates arrive?
sec18-card-f21.teaching_text: Shredding and discarding the expired temporary tag prevents anyone from stealing and reusing your registration number.

sec18-card-f22.question_text: Which four authorized places issue Illinois temporary registration permits?
sec18-card-f22.teaching_text: Even private buyers can pick up a temporary tag through currency exchanges, remitters, or Secretary of State offices.

sec18-card-f23.question_text: Roughly how far ahead of expiration might a courtesy registration-renewal reminder arrive?
sec18-card-f23.teaching_text: Watch your plate's month sticker yourself too, since sixty-day reminders are a courtesy rather than an excuse.

sec18-card-f24.question_text: Through which five methods or locations can Illinois owners renew vehicle registration?
sec18-card-f24.teaching_text: Flexible online, phone, mail, agency, and participating bank or remitter options make beating late fees easy.

sec18-card-f25.question_text: Which exact corner of which plate holds your renewal sticker — and what happens if you leave an expired sticker showing?
sec18-card-f25.teaching_text: Leaving the new sticker sitting in your glovebox after expiration still invites a traffic stop and citation.

sec18-card-f26.question_text: How long can a printed online-renewal receipt carried in the car cover for a mailed sticker not yet received?
sec18-card-f26.teaching_text: Provided you renewed online before expiration, keeping that receipt inside your car grants a thirty-day mail buffer.

sec18-card-r01.question_text: Who qualifies to have the standard registration renewal fee waived right after returning to the United States?
sec18-card-r01.teaching_text: Active-duty members and reservists showing proof of combat service get their next immediate registration renewal fee-free.

sec18-card-r02.question_text: How many days after returning from abroad do qualifying noncombat military and Defense civilian personnel get to register or renew?
sec18-card-r02.teaching_text: Illinois residents returning from noncombat military or Defense overseas duty receive a forty-five-day registration grace window.

sec18-card-r03.question_text: At least how many days should you allow after ordering personalized or vanity Illinois plates?
sec18-card-r03.teaching_text: Custom-stamped vanity or personalized plates take at least forty-five days to manufacture and ship.

sec18-card-r04.question_text: Who can receive an annual Illinois plate-fee discount under the Benefit Access Program, and on how many vehicles?
sec18-card-r04.teaching_text: Qualifying seniors and residents with disabilities receive one discounted registration per year on an eligible car or RV.

sec18-card-r05.question_text: What does mandatory Illinois auto liability insurance pay for after a crash?
sec18-card-r05.teaching_text: Liability insurance protects other people you injure or property you damage rather than paying to fix your own bumper.

sec18-card-r06.question_text: What is Illinois's minimum liability coverage for injury or death of one person in a crash?
sec18-card-r06.teaching_text: Twenty-five thousand dollars forms the first number in Illinois's mandatory twenty-five, fifty, twenty insurance split.

sec18-card-r07.question_text: What is Illinois's minimum liability coverage when two or more people are injured or killed in one crash?
sec18-card-r07.teaching_text: Fifty thousand dollars sets the minimum per-crash bodily-injury cap across multiple victims.

sec18-card-r08.question_text: What is Illinois's minimum liability coverage for damaging someone else's vehicle or property?
sec18-card-r08.teaching_text: Twenty thousand dollars completes Illinois's mandatory twenty-five, fifty, twenty minimum coverage trio.

sec18-card-r09.question_text: Does the standard twenty-five, fifty, twenty minimum apply to every vehicle category in Illinois?
sec18-card-r09.teaching_text: Specialized commercial or passenger-carrying categories must carry liability limits above standard personal-car floors.

sec18-card-r10.question_text: When must you show proof of liability insurance, and what two formats are accepted?
sec18-card-r10.teaching_text: Illinois officers accept either a printed insurance card or an electronic policy display on your phone.

sec18-card-r11.question_text: While waiting on a replacement insurance card, which four backup documents prove active coverage?
sec18-card-r11.teaching_text: Keeping a current binder, declarations page, certificate, or payment receipt in your glovebox prevents an uninsured ticket.

sec18-card-r12.question_text: Which three enforcement checkpoints verify that Illinois vehicles carry active liability insurance?
sec18-card-r12.teaching_text: Automated state database checks catch lapsed policies even if you never get pulled over in traffic.

sec18-card-r13.question_text: What three financial, renewal, and suspension consequences hit drivers caught without required Illinois insurance?
sec18-card-r13.teaching_text: Driving uninsured can freeze plate renewal and suspend both your driver's license and vehicle registration until you prove coverage.

sec18-card-r14.question_text: What penalties apply if someone submits false insurance details to the state agency or a renewal remitter?
sec18-card-r14.teaching_text: Falsifying policy numbers during plate renewal escalates from a traffic issue into criminal prosecution and fines.

sec18-card-r15.question_text: How do Illinois emissions tests tie into registration renewal, and how do owners learn their test window?
sec18-card-r15.teaching_text: Covered owners get notified of their assigned month and year and cannot renew expired stickers until the car passes.

sec18-card-r16.question_text: Which three Illinois counties require emissions testing countywide, and which seven counties are partly covered?
sec18-card-r16.teaching_text: All of Cook, DuPage, and Lake plus parts of metro Chicago and Metro East counties fall inside testing zones.

sec18-card-r17.question_text: What must you do after relocating away from an Illinois emissions-testing area?
sec18-card-r17.teaching_text: Updating your address promptly clears testing holds from blocking your next registration renewal.

sec18-card-r18.question_text: Which two residency, disability, and title conditions let an individual obtain Illinois disability license plates?
sec18-card-r18.teaching_text: Standard individual disability plates require both a permanent qualifying disability and the vehicle titled in that resident's name.

sec18-card-r19.question_text: When may an immediate household family member obtain two sets of disability plates for someone else?
sec18-card-r19.teaching_text: When a permanently disabled resident owns no car and relies on household family for rides, up to two plate sets qualify.

sec18-card-r20.question_text: Which groups outside individual households can also obtain Illinois disability license plates?
sec18-card-r20.teaching_text: Qualifying agencies and nonprofits that transport passengers with disabilities can register fleet vehicles with disability plates.

sec18-card-r21.question_text: Do disability license plates automatically exempt a vehicle from parking-meter fees or meter time limits?
sec18-card-r21.teaching_text: Many drivers wrongly assume wheelchair-symbol metal plates mean free meters, resulting in avoidable parking tickets.

sec18-card-r22.question_text: Who must be present and using the vehicle whenever a disability parking placard is displayed in an accessible space?
sec18-card-r22.teaching_text: Borrowing a relative's placard while they stay home or wait outside the trip is illegal placard misuse.

sec18-card-r23.question_text: What disability standard earns a meter-exempt permanent placard, and which meters still charge even with one?
sec18-card-r23.teaching_text: Even a meter-exempt placard never waives fees or limits at short-term meters capped at thirty minutes or less.

sec18-card-r24.question_text: What parking access does an ordinary permanent placard grant — and what meter rules still apply?
sec18-card-r24.teaching_text: Standard permanent placards unlock marked accessible stalls while still requiring regular meter payment and time compliance.

sec18-card-r25.question_text: How long can a temporary disability placard last from the state versus a municipality, and does it waive meters?
sec18-card-r25.teaching_text: Temporary placards cap at six months from the state or ninety days locally, and never waive meter fees.

sec18-card-r26.question_text: When may an organization placard be used for accessible parking, and how do parking meters apply?
sec18-card-r26.teaching_text: Organization placards apply only while actively transporting qualifying passengers free of charge and never exempt meters.

sec08-card-f01.question_text: Who is included inside the Illinois handbook's pedestrian category?
sec08-card-f01.teaching_text: Inline skaters, skateboarders, and travelers with disabilities share pedestrian protections rather than counting as motor traffic.

sec08-card-f02.question_text: How should drivers behave whenever people on foot are near the roadway?
sec08-card-f02.teaching_text: Skimming past someone walking along the curb leaves zero room if they stumble or step around a puddle.

sec08-card-f03.question_text: What must a pedestrian do when crossing outside a marked or unmarked crosswalk?
sec08-card-f03.teaching_text: Mid-block crossers lack crosswalk priority and should use overhead bridges or tunnels whenever one is provided.

sec08-card-f04.question_text: Where should pedestrians walk first, and how must they walk if forced onto a two-way road?
sec08-card-f04.teaching_text: Walking on the left side facing headlights lets you spot a drifting car early instead of getting struck from behind.

sec08-card-f05.question_text: What rule applies to walking along a highway while impaired by alcohol or drugs?
sec08-card-f05.teaching_text: Slowed balance and poor night judgment make impaired roadside walking nearly as lethal as impaired driving.

sec08-card-f06.question_text: What rights apply to a pedestrian using a guide dog, white cane, wheelchair, or assistive device?
sec08-card-f06.teaching_text: Drivers must yield completely and patiently whenever a white cane, service dog, or mobility chair enters a crossing.

sec08-card-f07.question_text: Which four route and awareness habits should walkers and joggers follow?
sec08-card-f07.teaching_text: Headphones and narrow blind shoulders hide approaching engines until a fast vehicle is right beside you.

sec08-card-f08.question_text: What two precautions should walkers and joggers take at night or in poor visibility?
sec08-card-f08.teaching_text: Dark hoodies vanish outside low-beam range until reflective strips bounce headlight glare back to the driver.

sec08-card-f09.question_text: How do railway gates, bridge gates, and other safety barriers apply to pedestrians?
sec08-card-f09.teaching_text: Ducking under lowered rail or drawbridge arms puts people on foot directly in front of trains or opening spans.

sec08-card-f10.question_text: What Illinois rules govern hitchhiking in the roadway and soliciting along highways?
sec08-card-f10.teaching_text: Standing in live lanes for rides, cash, or sales invites high-speed strikes and sudden rear-end braking.

sec08-card-f11.question_text: Under what age, daylight, speed-limit, and traffic conditions may someone skate on a public road?
sec08-card-f11.teaching_text: Exam questions test all four limits together: age eighteen, sunrise to sunset, forty-five or lower, and zero obstruction.

sec08-card-f12.question_text: Where should drivers expect children near the road and prepare to slow down?
sec08-card-f12.teaching_text: Kids chasing balls or catching buses focus on play rather than scanning oncoming traffic lanes.

sec08-card-f13.question_text: What two driveway and play-area precautions help protect young children?
sec08-card-f13.teaching_text: Rear pillars and tall tailgates create huge blind zones right where small toddlers stand unseen in driveways.

sec08-card-f14.question_text: When should parents teach pedestrian rights and responsibilities to children?
sec08-card-f14.teaching_text: Building curb-check and crosswalk habits early protects kids before they start walking to school or parks solo.

sec08-card-f15.question_text: How do a motorcycle's legal status and narrow profile affect traffic safety?
sec08-card-f15.teaching_text: A slim single-headlight silhouette tricks the human eye into thinking an approaching bike is farther and slower than reality.

sec08-card-f16.question_text: How often should you expect motorcycles in traffic, and when must you check extra carefully?
sec08-card-f16.teaching_text: Warm winter afternoons still bring riders out, and left turns across bikes cause the deadliest intersection crashes.

sec08-card-f17.question_text: What must a left-turning driver do when an oncoming motorcycle approaches?
sec08-card-f17.teaching_text: Many motorcycle turn signals do not self-cancel, so wait until the rider actually slows and turns before crossing.

sec08-card-f18.question_text: When may a motorcyclist proceed through an unchanging red light, and what duty applies first?
sec08-card-f18.teaching_text: Lightweight bikes sometimes fail to trip buried pavement sensors, so Illinois allows proceeding carefully after two full minutes.

sec08-card-f19.question_text: How much of a traffic lane belongs to a motorcyclist, and may a car share beside it?
sec08-card-f19.teaching_text: Riders shift left and right inside their lane to dodge potholes, oil streaks, and wind blasts.

sec08-card-f20.question_text: How should you drive while a motorcyclist is overtaking your vehicle?
sec08-card-f20.teaching_text: Speeding up or drifting sideways leaves an exposed rider stranded in oncoming traffic or blown by mirror turbulence.

sec08-card-f21.question_text: What minimum time cushion and headlight rule apply when following a motorcycle?
sec08-card-f21.teaching_text: Extra following seconds prevent rear-ending quick two-wheel stops, while low beams avoid blinding compact bike mirrors.

sec08-card-f22.question_text: How does a motorcycle's dry-pavement stopping distance compare to a car's, and what influences it?
sec08-card-f22.teaching_text: Light weight lets experienced riders shed speed faster than sedans on dry asphalt, surprising tailgaters behind them.

sec08-card-f23.question_text: How do wet or icy pavement and strong crosswinds affect a motorcycle?
sec08-card-f23.teaching_text: Balancing on two narrow contact patches means rain cuts braking sharply while gusts push riders sideways across lanes.

sec08-card-f24.question_text: How can potholes, gravel, oil, debris, or rail tracks affect a motorcycle ahead of you?
sec08-card-f24.teaching_text: Minor gravel or angled steel rails that cars roll right over can dump a two-wheeled bike unless the rider adjusts.

sec08-card-f25.question_text: How should you respond upon encountering a crash involving a motorcycle?
sec08-card-f25.teaching_text: Without a steel cage or airbags, riders suffer hidden spinal or internal trauma requiring trained paramedics immediately.

sec08-card-f26.question_text: What defines an Illinois autocycle, and what paperwork and license does roadway operation require?
sec08-card-f26.teaching_text: Because you sit in a bucket seat behind a steering wheel rather than straddling, a regular Illinois license covers it.

sec08-card-f27.question_text: What roadway status do bicycles hold on most streets, and which assisted bikes are included?
sec08-card-f27.teaching_text: Pedal riders and qualifying electric or gas-assisted bikes hold the same intersection right-of-way rules as cars.

sec08-card-f28.question_text: May a driver travel, park, idle, or load passengers in an empty marked bicycle lane?
sec08-card-f28.teaching_text: Stopping for even thirty seconds of passenger pickup forces approaching cyclists to swerve out into fast motor traffic.

sec08-card-f29.question_text: Why should drivers stay alert beside a marked bicycle lane?
sec08-card-f29.teaching_text: Broken glass, double-parked vans, or upcoming left turns legally bring riders out of the painted bike strip.

sec08-card-f30.question_text: In which direction do bicycles ride, and when might a rider move toward the center of the lane?
sec08-card-f30.teaching_text: Narrow lanes and curb hazards make riding mid-lane safer so cars wait for a real passing gap.

sec08-card-f31.question_text: When may cyclists ride two abreast, and when is riding more than two abreast banned?
sec08-card-f31.teaching_text: Two riders side by side must not hold up normal traffic, and three across is restricted to bike-only paths.

sec08-card-f32.question_text: How should you treat a cyclist's right-of-way and personal space on the road?
sec08-card-f32.teaching_text: Honking closely or squeezing past an unprotected rider risks a fatal fall over a few seconds of impatience.

sec08-card-f33.question_text: How much passing clearance must Illinois drivers give a cyclist, how is it measured, and what if space is tight?
sec08-card-f33.teaching_text: Notice Illinois measures three feet from your sticking-out side mirror edge, not the fender panel.

sec08-card-f34.question_text: What legal jeopardy can follow passing too close to a cyclist and causing a crash?
sec08-card-f34.teaching_text: Clipping a rider during an impatient squeeze pass escalates well beyond a routine traffic fine.

sec08-card-f35.question_text: What three precautions apply when following behind a bicyclist?
sec08-card-f35.teaching_text: Wet rims, slick leaves, or potholes can drop a rider instantaneously right in front of a tailgating bumper.

sec08-card-f36.question_text: What headlight rule applies when meeting an oncoming bicyclist after dark?
sec08-card-f36.teaching_text: High-beam glare blinds an oncoming rider's view of potholes, gravel, and the pavement edge.

sec08-card-f37.question_text: How must you handle oncoming cyclists or a cyclist ahead of you in a shared left-turn lane?
sec08-card-f37.teaching_text: Never try to swing wide beside a turning bike inside the intersection; let the rider clear the turn first.

sec08-card-r01.question_text: What must you do before turning right when a cyclist approaches on your right?
sec08-card-r01.teaching_text: Signaling early and waiting prevents the classic right-hook collision across a straight-moving bike lane.

sec08-card-r02.question_text: What check and hand habit help avoid striking a cyclist with a parked car's door?
sec08-card-r02.teaching_text: Opening the driver door with your right hand turns your head naturally toward cyclists approaching from behind.

sec08-card-r03.question_text: What pedal requirement and motor wattage limit define a low-speed electric bicycle?
sec08-card-r03.teaching_text: Working pedals and a sub-seven-hundred-fifty-watt motor distinguish legal e-bikes from mopeds or motorcycles.

sec08-card-r04.question_text: Where may low-speed electric bicycles operate, where are they barred, and what can local towns restrict?
sec08-card-r04.teaching_text: Sidewalks belong strictly to slower foot traffic, and municipalities can also ban e-bikes on specific local trails.

sec08-card-r05.question_text: How does a Class One electric bicycle deliver motor help, and at what speed does it stop?
sec08-card-r05.teaching_text: Class One motors never push on a thumb throttle alone and cut out once speed hits twenty.

sec08-card-r06.question_text: How does a Class Two electric bicycle differ from Class One, and where does its motor cut off?
sec08-card-r06.teaching_text: Class Two adds motor-only propulsion without pedaling while keeping the same twenty-mile-per-hour assist ceiling.

sec08-card-r07.question_text: What pedaling rule, speed figure, and minimum rider age apply to a Class Three electric bicycle?
sec08-card-r07.teaching_text: Higher twenty-eight-mile-per-hour pedal speeds explain why Illinois sets a minimum rider age of sixteen for Class Three.

sec08-card-r08.question_text: What two markings must a scooter carry to be titled and registered in Illinois?
sec08-card-r08.teaching_text: Toy scooters without a federal safety label and vehicle identification number cannot get Illinois license plates.

sec08-card-r09.question_text: What traffic rules bind scooter and moped riders, and what equipment is required to carry a passenger?
sec08-card-r09.teaching_text: Doubling a friend on a single-rider scooter without dedicated passenger pegs and seating upsets balance dangerously.

sec08-card-r10.question_text: How does a scooter's engine size around one hundred fifty cubic centimeters determine license class?
sec08-card-r10.teaching_text: Illinois splits two-wheel endorsements right at one hundred fifty cubic centimeters between Class L and full Class M.
sec08-card-r10.must_match_memory_hook: Under one-fifty Class L, else M

sec08-card-r11.question_text: Which license covers a moped, and what engine-size and shifting limits apply to gas mopeds?
sec08-card-r11.teaching_text: If a gas bike exceeds fifty cubic centimeters or needs manual clutch shifting, a regular car license will not cover it.

sec08-card-r12.question_text: What weight, wheel, frame, and speed limits define a low-speed electric kick scooter?
sec08-card-r12.teaching_text: Lightweight stand-up floorboards capped at ten miles per hour separate kick scooters from plated road scooters.

sec08-card-r13.question_text: What age, license, and local-permission rules govern operating a low-speed electric scooter?
sec08-card-r13.teaching_text: Even without a license requirement, riders must be eighteen and check whether the city or park district allows scooters.

sec08-card-r14.question_text: How many people may ride a low-speed electric scooter, and what lights or reflectors must it carry?
sec08-card-r14.teaching_text: Tandem riding destabilizes tiny scooter wheels, and front-and-rear lighting keeps low decks visible at dusk.

sec08-card-r15.question_text: Where should you position your car around a large truck or bus?
sec08-card-r15.teaching_text: If you cannot see the trucker's face in the cab's side mirror, that driver cannot see your car at all.

sec08-card-r16.question_text: Why must you watch large-vehicle turn signals and leave open space on the right before a right turn?
sec08-card-r16.teaching_text: Long trailers swing left first before tracking tight across the right curb, crushing any car that sneaks beside them.

sec08-card-r17.question_text: Why do large trucks and buses need extra space from surrounding cars?
sec08-card-r17.teaching_text: Cutting closely in front of an eighty-thousand-pound semi steals the long braking cushion it needs to avoid rear-ending you.

sec08-card-r18.question_text: Why must you dim high beams when following behind a large truck at night?
sec08-card-r18.teaching_text: Oversized West Coast side mirrors catch rear high beams and shine blinding light straight into the trucker's eyes.

sec08-card-r19.question_text: How does the handbook suggest alerting a truck driver before passing, and how should you complete the pass?
sec08-card-r19.teaching_text: Lingering alongside trailer axles exposes your car to tire blowouts, wind buffeting, and unseen lane changes.

sec08-card-r20.question_text: What must you do on a four-lane highway when approaching a disabled vehicle flashing hazard lights?
sec08-card-r20.teaching_text: Illinois's Move Over protection covers stranded motorists with hazards flashing, not solely police and tow trucks.

sec08-card-r21.question_text: What rules govern pushing a disabled vehicle on a rural highway and clearing it?
sec08-card-r21.teaching_text: Bumper-pushing slow cars along fast rural two-lanes invites high-speed rear-end collisions over blind crests.

sec08-card-r22.question_text: What else must be cleared from the pavement when a damaged vehicle is removed?
sec08-card-r22.teaching_text: Shattered glass and bumper shards left behind puncture tires and throw motorcyclists off balance.

sec08-card-r23.question_text: What hitch hardware, spacing limit, and backup links are required when one vehicle tows another?
sec08-card-r23.teaching_text: Rigid drawbars within fifteen feet prevent rear-ending on stops, while dual chains catch the load if a hitch pin snaps.

sec08-card-r24.question_text: After how long on an interstate, expressway, or tollway may police tow an abandoned or disabled car at owner cost?
sec08-card-r24.teaching_text: Shoulder-parked cars on high-speed corridors draw deadly drift crashes, so police clear them after just two hours.

sec08-card-r25.question_text: What are the abandoned-vehicle towing time thresholds on non-expressway highways inside versus outside urban areas?
sec08-card-r25.teaching_text: Compare all three Illinois tow clocks carefully: two hours expressway, ten hours urban, and twenty-four hours rural.

sec08-card-r26.question_text: What top speed and paperwork requirements apply to a four-wheeled low-speed vehicle?
sec08-card-r26.teaching_text: Unlike golf carts kept on private paths, road-legal low-speed vehicles carry Illinois titles and plates.

sec08-card-r27.question_text: Which posted speed limits allow low-speed vehicles on public streets?
sec08-card-r27.teaching_text: Keeping twenty-five-mile-per-hour vehicles off faster arterials prevents dangerous speed differentials unless prohibited locally.

sec08-card-r28.question_text: Which seven control, glass, restraint, and mirror items must a low-speed vehicle carry?
sec08-card-r28.teaching_text: Proper automotive windshields, seat belts, parking brakes, and dual mirrors separate street-legal units from yard carts.

sec08-card-r29.question_text: What reflectors, lamp visibility distances, brake lights, and signals does a low-speed vehicle need?
sec08-card-r29.teaching_text: Know both numbers cold for the exam: headlamps visible five hundred feet ahead and red tail lamps one hundred feet back.

sec08-card-r30.question_text: Which vehicles creep slowly along rural roads, and what rear emblem marks them?
sec08-card-r30.teaching_text: Spotting the glowing orange triangle warns you to lift off the throttle immediately rather than assuming highway pace.

sec08-card-r31.question_text: What typical speed range do slow-moving vehicles travel, and what danger does that create?
sec08-card-r31.teaching_text: At fifty-five miles per hour you eat up a football field behind a fifteen-mile-per-hour tractor in seconds.

sec08-card-r32.question_text: What precautions must you take before overtaking slow-moving farm or construction equipment?
sec08-card-r32.teaching_text: Tractor operators often swing wide before turning left into unmarked dirt field entrances right as impatient cars pass.

sec08-card-r33.question_text: From how far away in daylight must a slow-moving vehicle's high-mounted rear flashing amber light be visible?
sec08-card-r33.teaching_text: High-mounted amber strobes crest hills ahead of low trailers to give five hundred feet of daytime warning.

sec08-card-r34.question_text: Which lane does slow traffic normally use, and why might wide equipment edge into the next lane?
sec08-card-r34.teaching_text: Combines and plows overhanging the shoulder must swing left briefly to clear mailboxes, signs, or bridge rails.

sec08-card-r35.question_text: Where must winter motorists watch for snowmobiles sharing or crossing the road?
sec08-card-r35.teaching_text: Snowbanks along rural ditches hide sleds emerging briskly onto plowed crossings in winter.

sec08-card-r36.question_text: Which public roads may horseback riders use, and how must they ride?
sec08-card-r36.teaching_text: Horses legally travel most public roads outside controlled-access freeways, staying far right with traffic flow.

sec08-card-r37.question_text: Why must you never honk near horses or livestock, and how should you pass riders?
sec08-card-r37.teaching_text: A sudden horn blast spooks a thousand-pound animal into bolting sideways into your windshield.
